News.title: Mum, 48, loses seven teeth after tripping over deep pothole in the dark as council refuses to pay compensation
News.content:
POTHOLE HORROR Mum, 48, loses seven teeth after tripping over deep pothole in the dark as council refuses to pay compensation

A MUM who lost seven teeth after tripping over a deep pothole has blasted the local council for not taking responsibility.

Business owner Alison Smith, 48, shattered nearly all of her front teeth after falling into the hole in a dark area in Ventnor, on the Isle of Wight.



Horrifying photographs show the extent of her devastating injuries, which left her face swollen and bruised.

The cafe owner had been on her way to meet her daughter when she fell at around 7.40pm in January 2025 on the dimly lit pavement.



Alison said that her daughter, who was 17, had been left “traumatised” after finding her mum covered in blood.

She added that she was not able to see her own mother, who’d recently had a brain tumour operation, as the sight of her injuries would be too distressing.





“I just tripped on the pothole, and my foot got caught in the pothole, in the lip on the edge, and I fell on my hand and knocked all my teeth out,” she said.

“My hand now isn’t fully recovered. I can’t lift myself up on it.

“I went to A&E because I thought I had smashed my cheekbone.

“I reported it and had a shameful response. They filled the pothole in within a few days, which says they are liable.”

She added that her daughter thought she had been stabbed or attacked given her horrific injuries.



Alison had extensive dental work done at her own expense, but could not afford implants because she’d received no compensation.

A plastic plate, inserted into the top and bottom of her mouth, makes it difficult for her to eat.

Serious hand injuries meant she had to close her beloved Gaslight Cafe in Sandown as she was unable to hold trays or lift heavy objects.

“I’m still so upset about it,” she said.

“Island Roads are saying they’ve done enough and have now filled the pothole in.



“But if it caused this much injury to me, old people could have died if they had gone flying like I did.”

She said she had considered the ‘no win no fee’ compensation claim but after recently losing both parents had decided to delay action.

“I just want someone to take responsibility for this,” she said.

“I’ve paid the price, and my daughter, who found me all bloodied after the fall, is still traumatised by it.

“It’s so unfair. Something that was not my fault has ruined my life, while Island Roads has just filled the holes and resurfaced the whole road and dismissed me.”



An Island Roads spokesperson said: “We have every sympathy for Ms Smith and for the injuries she has sustained as a result of this incident.

“The road was inspected in October 2024 as part of its routine six-monthly inspection and in line with accepted industry practice.

“No defects were identified that met the threshold for intervention either at that time or during our investigation following the incident.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They concluded that following an investigation, they were not able to accept liability in this case.

The pothole referred to in the claim – and another one nearby – were backfilled as part of the council’s “outgoing maintenance”.

News.title: Cops launch urgent manhunt for suspect, 22, who escaped a prison van moments after arriving outside court
News.content:
ON THE RUN Cops launch urgent manhunt for suspect, 22, who escaped a prison van moments after arriving outside court

COPS have launched a manhunt for a man who escaped from a prison van just moments after arriving outside court.

Stephen Grzyb, 22, from Liverpool, ran off from the Magistrates’ Court at around 10am having been transported from a police custody suite, Merseyside Police said.

Grzyb, who was charged with a domestic-related burglary, fled down Red Cross Street in the direction of The Strand, after being transported by prisoner transport contractor GEOAmey, the force added.



He is described as white, with short, dark hair and was last seen wearing a navy t-shirt and navy shorts.



Extensive inquiries are currently being taken by officers to locate him and patrols have also attended the home of the alleged victim in the case.

Inspector Bethan Hannon said: “We understand the concern this incident will cause, and it is vital the public can see Grzyb’s face so they can report any sightings and help us bring him back into custody as soon as possible.

“If you have heard from him or know where he is, please do the right thing and come forward.



“Assisting him in any way will bring police to your own door, so it is not an association worth keeping.

“If you see Grzyb, please call 999 immediately.

“We are carrying out extensive enquiries to find him with patrols on foot and CCTV enquiries being made right across the city centre so that we can return him to custody.”

Anyone with information is asked to get in touch with police quoting reference number 26000615520.

News.title: 109 toys you should NEVER buy your children – as fresh wave of squishy dumplings are seized in UK
News.content:
PARENTS should never buy these toys for their children as recalls continue to flag up dangerous substances and chemicals.

Last week, hundreds of squishy toys were seized after reports of strong chemical smells.

In the past seven months, 109 children’s toys have been urgently pulled from shelves over fears they pose a health risk to children.



Despite these toys having squishy, cuddly, and cute appearances, some have been found to contain dangerous substances, and should be avoided at all costs.



Squishy Dumpling (fakes)

Viral “Squishy Dumpling” toys have been gaining media attention, as children hunt down the glittery rare squishies hidden inside the basket-style boxes.

However, parents have been gradually noticing that a number of these dumpling toys have been omitting a distinct, and unnatural chemical smell.



In June, Cardiff-based wholesaler and website Samsons Cash and Carry Ltd saw its Squeezy Dumplings toy recalled over fear they pose a serious chemical risk.

Inside, the toy contained four times the legal quantity of the carcinogen benzene, which can irritate the eyes, nose, throat, skin, and digestive tract, and cause types of leukaemia after long-term, consistent exposure.

Experts have also urged parents to stop their children from microwaving squishy dumpling toys, after the trend caused a number of children to require skin grafts for life-changing burns.

To spot squishy dumpling fakes, it is important to look for clear safety instructions, a safety mark, and the name of a reputable importer or manufacturer on packaging.



Four details that tell you if a 'Squishy Dumpling' toy is genuine or fake According to Which?, anyone buying a dumpling toy should look out for the following: Clear safety instructions explaining what to do if the product leaks or is punctured.

explaining what to do if the product leaks or is punctured. A CE or UKCA mark that shows the item has been safety assessed.

that shows the item has been safety assessed. The name and address of a UK-based responsible person , such as an importer or manufacturer.

, such as an importer or manufacturer. Be wary of products that give off a strong or unusual chemical smell. Swansea Trading Standards launched its investigation after concerns were raised about some dumpling toys emitting a noticeable odour.

Craft Kits (containing decorative sand)

Reputable names such as Crayola, Galt, and Hobbycraft, have all seen craft kits be pulled from shop shelves.

This comes as decorative sand contained inside the kits, whether it be inside small tubes or packets, were found to contain asbestos.

To safely store unused packets of decorative sand in these sets, place them in a heavy-duty plastic bag, double-tape it shut, and store it out of reach of children.



Sand-filled Stretchy Toys

74 sand-filled stretchy and squishy toys have been recalled this year due to asbestos contamination, including 40 from the HTI Stretcherz range.

Even though the sand is contained inside the product, repeated stretching increases the risk of it bursting.

The simplest solution is to follow the Office for Product Safety and Standards (OPSS) disposal guidance to get rid of these toys, and to stop buying them.

Safety watchdogs had found that the rock and mineral samples inside the kits posed a “serious risk” to children’s health.

Two science kits involving sand and slime were pulled by KTL Toys as well, with the educational kits also flagging asbestos contamination.

Like any toys including decorative sand, it is important to be wary of these excavation or archaeological dig sets, as a number have been flagged for contamination.

Sand art bottle craft sets and jars



A number of sand art bottles, as well as tubes of decorative sand, have also been recalled due to asbestos contamination.

The sets usually consist of a clear bottle or jar, with multiple bags of decorative sand to used to create layered rainbow patterns inside.

As expected, given decorative sand has provoked these recalls, avoiding large quantities, such as in these kits, should be avoided.

Wooden blocks containing sand

Wooden toys are often considered the safest for children, however, the sand contained inside these were contaminated with asbestos.

News.title: Was Epstein ‘pimp’ POISONED? Investigators demand murder probe into mystery death of model scout ‘who knew too much’
News.content:
HE was suspected of being Jeffrey Epstein’s Paris ‘pimp’ and mentioned more than 2,000 times in the infamous FBI files on the prolific paedophile.

Now the body of Daniel Said – who was found dead in his Paris home earlier this month – is to be tested for poison over suspicions he was murdered, The Sun can reveal.





French prosecutors believe the model scout, 69, could have been bumped off because he knew too much about the paedophile’s global sex trafficking ring.

Politicians, celebrities and even royals such as the disgraced Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor have been linked to the web, which included underage girls.

Epstein himself died in suspicious circumstances in a New York prison cell in 2019 at 66 while awaiting trial – and now Siad’s sudden death has come under intense scrutiny.

The lifeless body of the Swedish national – who is said to have “sourced” girls for the billionaire financier to abuse – was found at his home in the Parisian suburb of Colombes on July 20.

Siad was due to be questioned by authorities on his links to the shamed financier before his sudden death.

An autopsy was held last week, after being ordered by Nanterre prosecutors, and – following an examination of results – further expert analysis has now been demanded.

This is “because of suspicions that the deceased had been poisoned”, an investigating source told The Sun.

He added: “There was no sign of physical violence, but forensic examination revealed a compromised state of health, including signs of a past heart attack.





“Toxicology tests will now take place, with sample tissues analysed for poisonous substances.”

The tests are considered urgent because potent poisons in chemical compounds such as cyanide break down within days of death.

The Sun can also reveal that the investigation into the French side of the Epstein sex ring has not ended with Siad’s death.

Instead, the investigation opened in February by France’s Central Office for the Repression of Trafficking in Human Beings focusing on Siad will carry on.

Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau said it “will continue in order to identify all individuals who could potentially be implicated”.

Siad continually denied any wrongdoing, and claimed to be “looking forward” to clearing his name through interviews with prosecutors.

He was officially known as a modelling scout, but he is mentioned thousands of times in the US Department of Justice documents relating to Epstein.

In the files, Siad appeared to liken his job of recruiting women to fishing.



Siad wrote to Epstein in 2014: “In This busyness (sic) I feel like fisherman some time I cache quick, some time no fish.”

Born in Algeria, he allegedly acted as a recruiter in France for Epstein – working with him from the late 2000s up until 2017.

He carried out scouting jobs in countries such as Poland, the Czech Republic, South Africa, Morocco, Cuba, and also France.

Among his closest contacts was Jean-Luc Brunel, the fashion agent found dead in a Paris prison in 2022, at the age of 75.

Like Epstein, Brunel was found hanging in his cell in an alleged suicide that has always been viewed as suspicious.

Brunel was said to have killed himself after spending 14 months in custody awaiting trial on charges of rape of minors and sexual harassment, which he denied.

Before his death, Siad said he believed he had been providing would-be models to Epstein.

Siad wrote: “He had a big apartment where he used to organise all his meetings, including casting for models I recruited, for Victoria’s Secret and MC2.



“The casting time would not last more than 10 minutes. I always left the place with the models immediately.”

The property referred to was a £10million Paris flat next to the Arc de Triomphe – regularly visited by men including Andrew and ex-British politician and diplomat Peter Mandelson.

Both Mandleson and Mountbatten-Windsor have been arrested in Britain as part of an investigation into misconduct in public office.

They have both since been released without charge, and vehemently deny any wrongdoing.

This will not prevent them becoming involved in the ongoing Siad enquiry, however.

Abused children as young as 12 were said to have passed through the Epstein apartment in the French capital, which included a massage parlour.

Cotrin Valdson, the Paris flat’s former concierge, said the former Prince Andrew was often a guest – just as he was at Epstein’s properties in New York, Florida, and the Virgin Islands.

Mr Valdson said that he “regularly looked after Prince Andrew” during low-key visits to the French capital.

There is no suggestion that either Mountbatten-Windsor or Mandleson were aware of any criminality at the flat.

Earlier this year, the former Swedish model Ebba Karlsson accused Siad of rape.



She said he had “scouted” her in her home town of Stockholm, Sweden, in 1990, when she was a 20-year-old model, and later raped her in France.

Siad then went by a different name, she said, and she was only able to identify him after seeing images of him in the international reporting of the Epstein files.

Responding to the news of Siad’s death, Ms Karlsson said it was “very frustrating” that he had died before being fully investigated.

Enquiries about the activities of Epstein and his friends in France related to Siad were reinvigorated by new witness testimonies earlier this year.

A woman who cannot be named for legal reason said she worked as a “sex slave” at Epstein’s Paris apartment, leaked interview transcripts with Paris prosecutors reveal.

Asked if women were solely being procured for Epstein, a convicted paedophile, for sexual purposes, the woman replied: “Yes, and I don’t think it was just for Epstein, but for other important people as well.”

The Avenue Foch property was also visited by Virginia Giuffre Roberts – another former Epstein ‘sex slave’ who alleged Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor slept with her when she was a teenager.

Before her death by suicide in April last year, at the age of 41, she said Andrew was “an abuser, a participant” in Epstein’s worldwide sex trafficking ring.

Regular guests at the Epstein property also included his long-term British girlfriend Ghislaine Maxwell, now 64, who is serving 20 years in an American prison for child trafficking.

Mountbatten-Windsor and Maxwell, the daughter of the late tycoon Robert Maxwell, were close friends, and travelled extensively together.



In a further chilling twist to the case, Virginia said 12-year-old twin girls were “recruited” in Paris and sent to America for Epstein to have sex with.

French prosecutors issued a public appeal to try and find the pair, who were said to be Eastern Europeans living in Paris.

The investigation into Siad’s links with Epstein continues.

News.title: Harrowing twist in timeline of husband’s murderous rampage of wife and six kids in family home before setting it on fire
News.content:
HOME HORROR Harrowing twist in timeline of husband’s murderous rampage of wife and six kids in family home before setting it on fire

A HARROWING detail in the timeline of the deaths of a mom and her six children has been revealed by their autopsy results.

Kristopher Karolkiewicz, 47, launched into a murderous rampage on July 24, wiping out his family and setting fire to their $750,000 home in Grand Haven Township, Michigan, before taking his own life.



His wife, Amanda ‘Mandy’ Karolkiewicz, 39, was found next to Kristopher’s body in their bedroom.

The bodies of their six children – four boys aged five, 11, 12, and 15 and two 11-year-old girls were found in other bedrooms in the property.





Their four beloved pets, three dogs and a cat, also died in the torched home.

All eight family members suffered gunshot wounds to the head.

read more on news BLURRED LINES Hidden tactics as Lindsay Clancy's trial divides USA - murderer or victim?

Now, the autopsy results have revealed that Amanda was “likely” killed by her husband before the children – possibly hours before.

The death certificates obtained by WLNS revealed that Mandy’s date of death is listed as “on or after” July 23, though it also notes the date of injury as July 24.



Meanwhile, the certificates for Kristopher and the children note their date of deaths as July 24.

The exact times of death for all family members is “unknown” but Ottawa County Sheriff’s Office Captain Jacob Sparks told the news outlet that the results suggest Mandy “likely died earlier than the children.”

“We don’t have have an exact timeline yet and are still working to establish that.”

Police are now examining surveillance footage and interviewing neighbors, relatives and friends as they try to reconstruct the family’s final hours.

Authorities said there was no record of previous police calls or visits to the home and no evidence of a struggle inside.



A motive for the killings has not been established.

It has been revealed that Krisopher lost his job at the American Heart Association earlier this month where he worked as a national vice president of sales and marketing for three years.

“This is an unspeakable tragedy that we may never completely understand why it happened,” Sparks previously said.

“But we’ll do our best to find the answers and to honor the memory of those victims.”

Mandy, a substitute teacher and children’s author, has been remembered as a “kind and devoted soul who loved her family and her students,” her parents said in a statement.



“We treasured every moment we had with her and her six children, and words cannot adequately express our devastation.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We pray for God’s peace and comfort as we grieve their deaths and honor their lives.”

The investigation is ongoing.

News.title: Moment teenagers ‘attack shop staff in violent brawl after being caught stealing’ as workers barricade themselves inside
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a group of teenagers appear to attack shop staff in a violent brawl after allegedly being caught shoplifting.

The chaotic incident took place at a convenience store on Baldwin Street in Bristol yesterday evening.



According to police, the conflict began earlier in the evening when the group were reportedly caught stealing from the shop and acting aggressively towards the staff.

They fled the scene after police were called, but the gang returned at around 8pm, triggering a frantic second confrontation as staff tried to keep them from entering.



Video footage shows shop workers battling to keep the tracksuit-clad teens outside the shop.

The youths can be seen repeatedly punching the staff in the doorway of the shop with one boy appearing to spit at them.

Amid the chaos, a girl’s voice can be heard crying out “he kicked my tummy”.

Moments later, a staff member turns his back to shield the entrance, only for the teens to grab him from behind and yank on his clothes.



Another worker, dressed in a cream jumper, lunges towards a boy in a white t-shirt before a colleague grabs him to break up the violence.

One of the yobs shouts: “Why you punching little kids?”

Then a boy in a black tracksuit spits at the staff again as they start retreating inside.



The violence then flares up again when one of the youths hurls a bottle of a liquid at the shop sign above, spraying its contents over the rest of the gang and the staff.

One of the yobs then throws a bottle of liquid at the shop sign, spraying everyone with its contents, causing more violence to occur.

Four teens start swarming a worker, raining down punches and furiously kicking him in the legs.

The teen recording the violence starts laughing and repeatedly exclaims “What the f***?”

DUring the tussle, one teen accidently falls backwards onto the pavemetn, knocking down a lottery sign.



Another gang member grabs the sign and begins using it to ram into the shop’s glass door while the other kid kicks it.

They shout “Are you f***ing mad? Open the door or I’ll smash it in.”

The shop keeper quickly steps out, spooking the kid with the sign who drops it and runs away.

The other teen stays standing in the door way, and is heard saying “I’m just standing here” before being kicked by a shop worker.

Eventually, one of the shop staff appears to reason with the boys and persuading them to clear off.



In a statement about the incident, Avon and Somerset Police said: “We are aware of social media videos that have been published relating to incidents at a convivence store in Bristol yesterday evening.

“Police were called to Baldwin Street about 6pm after reports of suspected shoplifting and a group of teenagers acting aggressively towards shop staff.

“Officers attended at about 6.10pm and the youths had left the scene.

“We were called to Baldwin Street shortly before 8pm with staff saying the group were trying to re-enter the store.

“The teenagers fled the area prior to officers arriving at about 8.10pm and they could not be located.



“An officer has since spoken to staff and provided reassurance that an investigation will be undertaken to try to identify those involved.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Enquiries, including reviewing footage of the incidents, are ongoing.

Anyone with information that could help the police’s enquiries have been asked to contact them either online or by calling 101, quoting reference number 5226215030.

News.title: ‘Murdered’ glam model, 28, seen smiling & holding hands with ‘killer’ 24hrs before suspect left flat and dumped suitcase
News.content:
SUITCASE HORROR ‘Murdered’ glam model, 28, seen smiling & holding hands with ‘killer’ 24hrs before suspect left flat and dumped suitcase

A GLAM model found stuffed in a suitcase was smiling and holding hands with her suspected killer just hours before her death, cops reveal.

Lyudmila Turkova, 28, had been missing for six days when her grisly remains were discovered floating in the Vizelj canal, northwest Serbia.



The model was reportedly last seen on CCTV walking towards a flat at 5:30am on July 25.

A law enforcement source says Turkova was smiling and the couple seemed “cheerful and happy” in the footage.



But just 24 hours later, the same man was seen hauling a heavy suitcase wrapped in fabric and containing her body at 6:56am, according to investigators.

Local residents then spotted a suspicious package floating in Vizelj canal on Thursday evening.

Police raced to the scene and deployed sniffer dogs to identify the remains.

The corpse was identified as that of the Russian body-art model but cops have not yet revealed how she died.



Investigators believe she was murdered in the early hours of 26 July in her rented apartment in Borca.

The body was then crammed into a suitcase, cops believe, and wheeled to a canal in a botched attempt to cover the suspected killer’s tracks.

Police have since identified a 25-year-old Turkish man as their prime suspect in the investigation.

He is the man pictured in a black t-shirt in the newly released CCTV.

The suspect – known only as K.E – was arrested at Belgrade’s Nikola Tesla Airport while allegedly attempting to flee the country.



The Serbian Interior Ministry said that a Turkish citizen born in 2001 was arrested on suspicion of the murder.

Turkova had been visiting Serbia on a two-week holiday when the tragedy unfolded.

Originally from St Petersburg, she had worked as a promoter, bartender and body-art model.



In her last message to her mother, the model said she was going out to “meet friends” at a nightclub in the Serbian capital.

A local report said: “The body has been sent to the Institute of Forensic Medicine, where… the cause of her death will be determined after an autopsy.”

News.title: Is Lindsay Clancy a murderer or a victim? Hidden trial tactics as case of devoted mom turned kid killer divides America
News.content:
THE trial of a young mom who killed her three children before attempting suicide has left the public divided over whether she is a calculated murderer or a victim of mismanaged mental health struggles.

Lindsay Clancy, 35, has pleaded not guilty to murder after her kids were found strangled with exercise bands three years ago, as her lawyer plans to argue she was suffering from undiagnosed postpartum psychosis.



On January 24, 2023, Lindsay sent her now ex-husband Patrick Clancy to pick up dinner and medicine from CVS.

While he was out, she strangled their three children — five-year-old daughter Cora, three-year-old son Dawson and eight-month-old son Callan — in the basement of their Duxbury home.





She then jumped from her second-story bedroom window after she crushed up pills and took a knife from the kitchen to slash her wrists and neck.

Patrick found Lindsay on the ground in their backyard when he returned home, and later discovered his three children in the basement, where he removed the exercise bands from their necks.

Lindsay has admitted to killing her children, but her attorney Kevin Reddington, plans to seek an insanity defense.

In the four months leading up to the Clancy children’s deaths, Lindsay was prescribed 13 medications by different healthcare providers and was hospitalized several times for suicidal ideation.



Opening statements began in the trial on Monday, where both the prosecution and Lindsay’s lawyer told jurors what to expect to see and hear in the case.

Reddington began talking about Patrick and Lindsay’s relationship and how they lived in a humble house after briefly warning the jury of the case’s contents.

Skye Lazaro, a Utah-based criminal defense lawyer told The U.S. Sun that Reddington’s remarks about the couple were a “brilliant” attempt to set the scene of Lindsay as a struggling mother and not a cold blooded killer to the 18 jurors.

“The reason is, is they’re sitting there looking at Lindsay in a wheelchair as a defendant in a criminal trial, accused of murdering her children. Him telling the story of this is who these people are.

“They’re the people next door. They’re the people who are in everybody’s neighborhood. They’re the people that your kids go to preschool with, or your kids go to school with, or your kids play soccer or baseball with.



“This was a normal, loving family. And, you know, they’re educated. They had good jobs. They had a great relationship. Everything was normal.

“Everything was okay until she began suffering from this course. Postpartum depression and psychosis. And what that does is it sort of lays the explanation.

“It lays the bedrock for where they’re going with this entire trial is this is not a woman who’s been crazy her whole life,” she said.



Lazaro explained that Reddington highlighting Lindsay’s life before her kids deaths could make the jury think: “Oh my gosh, this could be me. You know, this could be me sitting in that chair if things went bad or things got out of control.”

Prosecutor Shanan Buckingham began her opening statements by telling jurors about Cora’s love for princesses and how she tried to convince her Pre-K teacher that her name was Sofia, because she loved the Disney character from the show Sofia the First.

Buckingham then brought up Dawson’s love of trucks, how he was “full of energy,” and spoke with a raspy voice. Lastly was Callan, who was “always smiling with chunky cheeks.”



Lazaro further broke down the tactics used by the attorneys on Monday, saying the prosecution started off by describing the children to “really get the jury thinking.”

“They humanize them in a very, very effective way,” she explained, saying the descriptions helped the jury create a visual so when they listen to evidence, they’re thinking about how there are real people involved.

“They’re thinking about this kid who was boisterous, or this kid who played or smiled or loved a color. All of those types of things make it very real in a jury mind.

“So when they’re considering evidence and considering what the state is trying to prove and the arguments being made in the back of their mind, they’re thinking ‘these poor three little kids.'”

Lindsay became visibly upset in court, trembling and wiping away tears, as Buckingham talked about her kids in court.



“The jury is also judging everybody from the second they walk in, including the defendant. And so when she’s sitting there crying as they’re talking about their children, that probably helps her,” Lazaro said.



Lazaro said this case isn’t about whether Lindsay killed her three children, but instead whether or not she had “the legal mental intent” to do so.

The prosecution is trying to prove that Lindsay deliberately took her children’s lives, planning it out by sending Patrick out of the house, as Buckingham alleged, Lindsay “gave herself the time and privacy needed to commit the murders.”

“There’s multiple elements to every crime, but one of the ones that’s very, very important is this mental state element,” Lazaro explained. “But what the state has to prove here is that she intentionally and purposely murdered her children.”

Lazaro said the prosecution chose to use strong words in their opening statements to reach the jurors on an emotional level.

Buckingham said Lindsay “coldly and efficiently executed” the kids and “this was not a woman in the throes of psychosis.”



“They were strangled, deliberately and meticulously, killed by this defendant on January 24th of 2023,” the Plymouth County assistant district attorney said.

“One by one, she grabbed exercise bands around each one of the kid’s necks and pulled until their little bodies were limp and lifeless.”



“These other phrases about the execution, I think, really go more to trying to implore upon the jury just how depraved this act was, that this was not just she was out of her mind in a psychosis, that she purposely planned to execute her children or to murder her children,” Lazaro said of Buckingham’s statements.

When Reddington got up to give opening statements after Buckingham, he immediately addressed the jury, telling them that they were going to see and listen to “the most horrific things.”

“You people will never forget this case,” he told the jury of 12 women and six men.

“I think that immediately gets people on the edge of their seats,” Lazaro told The U.S. Sun.



“There’s a couple of things you want to do [as] an effective defense attorney in trial. You want to take the sting out of things that are not helpful to you, because if you say them first, you can kind of pass them off a little bit, like we’re aware of that.”

“Anytime you can invoke passion, which I think he did a very good job of doing, I think it’s far more effective,” she said.



Lindsay Clancy Murder Trial Lindsay Clancy is accused of strangling her three children, Cora, five, Dawson, three, and eight-month-old Callan, with exercise bands inside their Duxbury, Massachusetts, home on January 24, 2023. The former labor and delivery nurse does not deny killing them, but has pleaded not guilty and claims she was not criminally responsible because she was suffering from postpartum psychosis. Prosecutors argue Clancy deliberately sent her then-husband Patrick out to collect medicine and dinner so she could be left alone with the children. The trial began with Patrick on the witness stand, describing Clancy’s declining mental health before recounting how he returned home, found her injured outside and discovered the children in the basement. Jurors have since heard his harrowing 911 call, seen the bands that were removed from the children’s necks and viewed their pajamas and other evidence from the home. WHAT HAPPENS NEXT? Lindsay Clancy’s murder trial is expected to last between six and eight weeks, meaning testimony could continue well into September.

Proceedings are scheduled to begin at around 9am ET on sitting days and normally continue through the afternoon, with morning, lunch and afternoon breaks.

Prosecutors will present their case first, calling first responders, police officers, investigators, medical professionals and other witnesses connected to the killings.

The state listed more than 180 potential witnesses, although prosecutors are not expected to call everyone named.

Jurors are also expected to visit the Clancy family’s former Duxbury home with the judge and lawyers to see the scene for themselves.

Once prosecutors rest, Clancy’s defense will begin calling its own witnesses, including people who knew her and experts expected to testify about her medication, mental health and alleged postpartum psychosis.

The defense listed more than 60 possible witnesses, but some overlap with the prosecution’s list and may not be called twice.

After both sides finish presenting evidence, lawyers will deliver closing arguments before the judge instructs jurors on the law.

The jury will then decide whether Clancy is guilty of murder or was not criminally responsible because of her mental state when she killed her children.

In his remarks, Reddington also shared graphic images from the case, including closeups of Lindsay’s injuries and the bloody knife she used left on a table.

Lazaro said the defense can “acknowledge all the bad facts before the prosecution,” and by him showing the photos early on, it again takes “the sting out of it.”

“It really diminishes their impact for the prosecution because they’re still going to be thinking, yeah, we already know this. He already told us this.”

Patrick, Lindsay’s now-ex-husband, was the first witness to testify in the trial, which Lazaro explained the first witness is “always a strategic decision.”



She believes Patrick was called first to help lay out the trial by having him recall what he observed that fateful day and all of the events that unfolded.

Lazaro said as the trial goes forward, the prosecution will “hone in on to show that this this was not a psychotic break. This was not a product of postpartum depression,” as they argue their case.

On the flipside, the defense will set up how “the system failed” the Clancy family.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

If you missed day one of the trial or day two, you can catch up with a recap on our YouTube Channel. Catch up on day three of the trial from our live blog.

If you or someone you know needs help or support for their mental health, text “STRENGTH” to the Crisis Text Line at 741-741 to be connected with a certified crisis counselor.

News.title: Mum and daughter, 10, killed in horror crash are buried together in same wicker coffin
News.content:
Mum and daughter, 10, killed in horror crash are buried together in same wicker coffin

Heartbroken loved ones have gathered to say goodbye to author Nell Raven and her daughter, Ira, both born in the UK

View 4 Images Former journalist and writer Nell (53) and Ira (10), lost their lives following the two-car collision on Friday, July 24. (Image: Anglo Celt)

A mum and daughter who were born in the UK before moving to start a new life in Ireland have been buried together in the same coffin after a tragic crash cut their lives short.

‌



Acclaimed author Nell Saffron Raven and her young daughter Irena, known as Ira, were killed in a two-car collision on Friday, July 24. Nell, 53, was a former journalist, and lived with her family. including 10-year-old Ira, in Gortnacleigh, Milltown in Belturbet, Co Cavan.

‌



Originally from the UK, Ms Raven had recently become an Irish citizen. An emotional funeral brought together the loved ones to celebrate the lives of the pair, including Nell's talents as a writer, her dedication as a mother, and her triumph over cancer. Ira was remembered as a "kind, creative and joyful little girl" who loved music, Irish dancing and life in Co Cavan.

‌



The fatal incident occurred on the R162 at Corclare, Sherlock. Ms Raven passed away shortly after the crash, while Ira succumbed to her injuries on Tuesday afternoon, July 28, at Children's Health Ireland at Temple Street Hospital.

A single wicker coffin carrying Nell and Ira was brought into St Patrick's Church, Milltown on Saturday morning to the strains of 'Hallelujah' by Leonard Cohen, a favourite song of Nell and her husband Alex. A framed photograph of the mother and daughter was placed atop their coffin, reports the Irish Mirror.

View 4 Images St Patrick's Church, Milltown in Co Cavan (Image: Google Maps )

‌



During the funeral Mass, mourners learned that Ira had posthumously given the gift of life to four children through organ donation. Among the chief mourners at the funeral Mass were Nell's devastated husband and Ira's father Alexandru, daughters and sisters Eveline Margalla Kemp and Violet Elizabeth Kemp, parents and grandparents Erik Raven and Christina Smith, and Nell's sisters Daisy Raven and Poppy Sharrock.

Struggling to contain his emotions, Alexandru addressed the mourners, admitting he was "not a storyteller", but his wife had always been one. He reminisced about meeting Nell in Oxford in 2013, witnessing their family expand, and ultimately settling down in rural Cavan, where they discovered friendship, community, and joy.

"When I met Nell, she already had two girls of her own, Eveline and Violet. They were very sweet kids, bright and gorgeous. It didn't take too long and soon after I became the fourth member of their family," Alexandru shared with those gathered.

‌



He revealed that in 2016, their daughter Ira was born at John Ratcliffe Hospital in Oxford, and spoke fondly of their blissful family life in Oxford and later near Southampton, until Nell expressed her desire to relocate to Ireland, believing it to be the ideal place for writers. Alexandru recounted how they all embarked on the ferry from the UK in 2019 and made the move to Ireland.

"It was very hard at the beginning but when the pandemic started in March 2020, we fell in love with a very old cottage in Cavan," he said.

"We didn't hesitate in buying it and we made it our new home and from there on, we had a very happy life together."

‌



View 4 Images Former journalist and writer Nell (Image: Anglo Celt)

Paying tribute to Nell as a talented writer, dedicated mother and cancer survivor, he portrayed Ira as a "kind, creative and joyful little girl who embraced music, Irish dancing and life" in Cavan.

Confronted with the incomprehensible loss, he confessed, "Is there any justice, or is there any meaning of what happened? I do not know.

‌



"But perhaps, like in all stories, not just the beginning, or the middle, or the end but the whole story is all that matters."

He concluded his tribute by reciting Dylan Thomas's Do Not Go Gentle into That Good Night, a poem his wife had treasured.

Meaningful symbols and cherished belongings of Nell and Ira were placed upon the altar, including a George Orwell book, who served as Nell's greatest literary inspiration; Ira's beloved teddy, 'Ratty', her treasured comfort companion; a vase containing dried flowers that Alex had presented to Nell on Valentine's Day; and Ira's dancing shoes that secured her a spot on iconic Irish TV programme The Late Late Toy Show.

‌



View 4 Images Ira, 10, has been buried in the coffin alongside her mother (Image: Anglo Celt)

Ira's closest friend and classmate, Liam Connolly, reminisced about their cherished moments together, recalling how they attempted to construct a fort only to hurl stones at it afterward, their water pistol battles, and during sleepovers when they would launch their teddies as high as possible.

Liam also remembered their chess matches and how Ira concealed the king piece outside "because she was fed up playing chess with me.

Article continues below

"Ira was one of my best friends and I will miss her a lot," Liam told mourners.

Their coffin was carried from the church as Ira's beloved song 'Hey Brother' by Avicii echoed throughout.

The interment followed at Drumlane cemetery.

News.title: Wildfire expert delivers sobering warning about impact of climate change
News.content:
Wildfire expert delivers sobering warning about impact of climate change

EXCLUSIVE: Andy Elliott spoke out after a spate of blazes in recent days, including in Suffolk, where firefighters tonight continue to tackle flames for a fourth successive day

View 4 Images Emergency services near the scene of the wildfire at Dunwich Heath, Suffolk (Image: Humphrey Nemar/PA Wire)

Devastating wildfires are set to become the new normal, a top consultant has warned today.

‌



Andy Elliott, who has 35 years experience as a firefighter and consultant, says conditions across the UK are becoming very challenging and the government can do more to help land managers and the fire service, including by providing better personal protective equipment.

‌



The alert comes after blazes ripped through Suffolk and other parts of the country in recent days. Mr Elliott told the Mirror: "Compared to 20 years ago, it will be much more frequent. It's likely to happen almost every year. This will be the new normal.

‌



"They are going to become much more frequent. There will be years when we get the odd wet summer, but we can expect to see more flooding in the winter and more frequent hot periods, resulting in drought conditions in the summer."

Met Office names 29 areas facing heavy rain on Monday – see full list READ MORE :

UK drought maps turn red but temperatures set to drop after record dry July READ MORE :

View 4 Images Two fire service workers being driven away from the site covered in soot (Image: Humphrey Nemar/ daily mirror)

Increasing threat to life

Speaking about the threat to human life, he added: "We should expect to see an increase in wildfires and we should expect to see loss of life. The risk to human life increases all the time.

‌



"We only need to look at France and Spain where people have lost their lives - they're fighting very similar wildfires. The British public need to be aware of that. It's very challenging."

Mr Elliott spoke out as firefighters today continue to tackle the Suffolk wildfire, on Dunwich Heath, close to Sizewell B nuclear power station, for a fourth successive day. At its height, it was estimated to span 370 acres – the size of about 220 football pitches.

View 4 Images Cottages were saved despite the landscape around them being burnt to the ground (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Suffolk wildfire continues

Around 200 families, including residents and holidaymakers staying in caravans and lodges near the heath, were evacuated around two miles to a pop-up rescue centre at Westleton Village Hall late on Wednesday night after police banged on their doors telling them they were in danger.

The National Trust, which have been caring for Dunwich Heath since 1968, have launched a public appeal for donations to help restore the site to its former glory. There were also other ongoing blazes yesterday, including across Europe.

Speaking about the Dunwich Heath fire, a Suffolk Fire and Rescue Service spokesperson said: "The situation remains stable, although firefighting operations continue and crews are responding to hotspots where they emerge.

‌



Suffolk Fire and Rescue Service and supporting agencies have the resources they need on scene and work continues to create a large firebreak around the perimeter of the site.

A Suffolk Lowland Search and Rescue spokesperson said their teams expect to carry on working alongside firefighters until Monday night at the earliest. They added: "The main tasking is focused around using drone technology to identify hot spots and areas of reignition.

"We are in awe of the efforts of the firefighters, who are working relentlessly around the clock, and we are grateful to have the drone capability to be able to assist their work."

‌



View 4 Images Greek firefighters try to extinguish a blaze in the area of Porto Germeno, some 70 kilometres (45 miles) northwest of Athens (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Western Europe ravaged by wildfires

There have also been wildfires across Europe in recent weeks, again following huge rises in temperatures. Firefighters held a vast wildfire inside its perimeter in southwestern France today, allowing about 198,000 people to return home after what may have been the country’s largest peacetime evacuation.

But other fires have forced thousands from their homes elsewhere in France and Greece. In the Mediterranean Var, a fire thought to have stopped advancing raced across 10 square kilometers (4 square miles) in six hours on Friday.

Article continues below

The opposing movements — mass returns in France's Gironde region, renewed displacement in the Var and boat evacuations from a Greek resort — underscored how quickly days of firefighting progress can be reversed. At their peak, fires in France and Spain alone drove a third of a million people from homes and vacation sites, stretching firefighters, aircraft and emergency services across simultaneous crises.

News.title: Donald Trump spirals furiously as reflecting pool saga ends in humiliating climbdown
News.content:
Donald Trump spirals furiously as reflecting pool saga ends in humiliating climbdown

Trump lashed out at his long-time ally after she admitted his hand-picked contractors botched the Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool refurb - and not, as he has repeatedly claimed, "vandals"

View 2 Images Trump has contradicted one of his own top lawyers (Image: AP Photo/Alex Brandon)

Donald Trump lashed out after his administration was forced to admit his hand-picked contractors botched the Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool refurbishment - and not "sick vandals" as he has falsely claimed.

‌



The Justice Department made a humiliating climbdown and dropped charges against a former Olympian the administration accused of deliberately damaging the pool.

‌



But Trump lashed out at the long-time ally prosecuting the case, posting on Truth Social: "I disagree 100% with Jeanine Pirro, the U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia, on the Reflecting Pool. I don't know what she was thinking? To me it was a pure case of VANDALISM."

‌



He added: "There may have been some contractor difficulty, but the major damage was caused by VANDALS!"

In April, Trump announced he had scrapped a multi-year, $3 billion plan to refurbish the iconic landmark, where Martin Luther King delivered his "I Have a Dream" speech.

Instead, he said he would arrange for his own hand-picked contractors to line it with industrial swimming pool sealant in "American Flag Blue".

‌



View 2 Images The lining of the pool began to peel off within days (Image: JIM LO SCALZO/EPA/Shutterstock)

The job was completed five weeks late, just days before the July 4th deadline, and at a cost of nearly $15 million - ten times the $1.5 million he promised it would cost.

And within days of it being refilled with water, algae turned it swamp green, and within a week the lining had begun to peel from the bottom of the pool.

‌



Trump blamed "sick, deranged vandals" for the damage, claiming a "300 foot long gash" was sliced into the sealant with a blade.

David Hearn, a champion canoeist, faced a 10-year prison sentence after being arrested on suspicion of vandalising the pool.

But in a court filing on Friday, the Trump administration said new information from the Department of the Interior (DOI) had indicated the damage "was the result of flawed installation by the contractor."

Article continues below

It also accepted it was down to "the rush to complete the project prior to events associated with the America 250 celebration in the weeks surrounding Independence Day 2026.

Trump's UFC Birthday Party event last month kicked off with an event next to the reflecting pool, a week after the work was completed.

The documents continue: "It was not until after these documents were produced that [prosecutors] first became aware of information showing that the damage was the result of a botched installation and not vandalism as initially represented by DOI."

News.title: Naples earthquake live: Italy struck by 4.7 magnitude quake as rocks crush cars
News.content:
Residents in Naples have been left terrified after a powerful earthquake caused damage to the Italian city - it registered at 4.7 magnitude

A powerful earthquake has struck southern Italy, causing damage in the city of Naples.

The 4.7 magnitude quake has left neighbourhoods without power, and residents are taking to the streets in fear. It occurred just before 8pm (local time).

According to data released by the INGV (National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology), the magnitude was 4.7. Power outages have been reported from Pizzofalcone to Fuorigrotta, and there has been a massive landslide in Pozzuoli.

Images show buildings have crumbled, with debris crushing cars.

News.title: Volodymyr Zelensky’s missile plea as fresh Russian blitz kills nine in Ukraine's Kyiv
News.content:
Volodymyr Zelensky’s missile plea as fresh Russian blitz kills nine in Ukraine's Kyiv

The Kremlin’s barrage overnight into Saturday is said to have wounded dozens of people, with Ukraine’s leader Volodymyr Zelensky calling for ballistic missile interceptors

View 4 Images Volodymyr Zelensky delivers a speech to the media (Image: Niall Carson)

Volodymyr Zelensky has made a plea for ballistic missile interceptors after a fresh Russian blitz on Ukraine’s capital Kyiv left at least nine dead.

‌



The Kremlin’s barrage of ballistic missiles and drones overnight into Saturday also wounded 33 people, authorities said. It follows Moscow’s attack two days earlier which killed at least 10 people and injured more than 50 others across Ukraine.

‌



The latest strikes prompted Ukraine’s president Zelensky to stress the need for ballistic missile interceptors – warning every night without them results in more casualties. Russia's defence ministry said on Saturday it had launched a massive strike against Ukrainian military-industrial complex facilities and logistics centers in Kyiv.

‌



View 4 Images A burned car after a Russian missile attack in Kyiv, Ukraine, in the early hours of this morning (Image: AP Photo/Dan Bashakov)

Ukraine batters Moscow hours before crucial Zelensky-Trump meeting READ MORE :

A five-storey residential building in the city's Solomianskyi District was damaged by falling debris and a fire broke out. Rescue workers evacuated 35 people from the upper floors of the building and two people died, with eight reported injured, including two kids, according to Ukraine's state emergency service.

In Kyiv’s Darnytskyi District, seven people were killed and another 14 injured after the attack caused fires and damage to houses, vehicles, an administrative and non-residential building, the emergency services said.

‌



Elsewhere, emergency workers extinguished a fire in a non-residential building in the capital's Shevchenkivskyi district. Damage to commercial and residential buildings was reported in two other city districts.

View 4 Images A firefighter works at the site of a Russian missile strike on August 1, 2026 in Kyiv, Ukraine (Image: Global Images Ukraine via Getty Images)

Zelensky has pressed the US and Western partners over Ukraine's need for more Patriot anti-ballistic missile defence systems to counter missile attacks from Russia. In a post on X, the leader on Saturday stressed the “shortage of ballistic missile interceptors… only encourages Russia to launch such attacks that take human lives”.

‌



He added: “It is critical that partners hear that these capabilities are needed not somewhere in stockpiles for hypothetical scenarios, but here and now, to contain and stop the Russian war in Ukraine. Every package of ballistic missile interceptors saves the lives of our people. And every night without them results in more casualties.”

At a NATO summit in Turkey’s capital, Ankara, last month, Donald Trump said the US would give Ukraine a licence to make Patriot systems. But he appeared to move away from the commitment on Friday during a Cabinet meeting at the presidential retreat in Camp David, Maryland, saying he had not yet made a final decision.

View 4 Images Local residents clear the aftermath of a Russian missile strike on August 1, 2026 in Kyiv, Ukraine (Image: Global Images Ukraine via Getty Images)

‌



From a basement shelter where she was taking cover as a second air alarm sounded for another wave, Liudmyla Nakonechna, 64, described how she was woken by loud explosions at 1.30am. Ms Nakonechna, whose health is poor after undergoing cancer treatment, said: "I ran into the corridor and was standing there when the bathroom door was blown off its hinges and struck me in the leg."

Ms Nakonechna, who had not taken cover in a shelter since Russia's full-scale invasion on February 24, 2022, but the stress became too much, added: "I heard the sound of shattering glass. My balcony was covered in glass and it was completely blown apart, while the windows in my bedroom were also blown out."

"It's getting worse by the day. Whereas before there was an attack once every two weeks, or maybe once a week, now it happens practically every day. It is incredibly hard to bear this psychologically."

Article continues below

In Russian-occupied Crimea, the Moscow-appointed head of the city of Sevastopol, Mikhail Razvozhayev, said on Saturday that a 60-year-old woman was killed and two other people wounded in a drone attack on the city.

Meanwhile, a sanctioned Russian container ship, the Yanina, sank in the Black Sea after being hit by Ukraine, Mr Zelensky said on Saturday, listing the ship as among facilities that sustain the war effort. A Russian airstrike killed one person and wounded five more in the city of Kherson in southern Ukraine, local officials said Saturday.

News.title: Police probe launched after man in his 40s found dead in hotel room in Liverpool
News.content:
Police probe launched after man in his 40s found dead in hotel room in Liverpool

Police said his death is being treated as 'unexpected'

View Image (Image: Google Maps )

Police are investigating after a man was found dead in a city centre hotel.

‌



Merseyside Police confirmed that a man's body was discovered this morning, Saturday, August 1, inside a hotel room in Liverpool. Officers have attended the Brownlows Inn on Mount Pleasant.

‌



Emergency services are currently at the scene in Liverpool city centre following the death, the force confirmed. They said that a report that the body of a man, in his 40s, had been found was received at around 11.15am, reports the Liverpool Echo.

‌



The man was found dead at the scene by paramedics. Merseyside Police said his death is being treated as unexpected.

The man's next of kin have been informed, and a postmortem investigation will be carried out to establish his cause of death.

Article continues below

Currently, enquiries at the scene remain ongoing, police have said.

News.title: 'Donald Trump's £40bn folly has drawn the west’s enemies ever closer'
News.content:
History will not view US President Donald Trump’s war on Iran kindly. This £40 billion folly has damaged World economies for years, made once delicately handled Middle Eastern fault lines increasingly unstable and drawn the west’s enemies ever closer.

Under his command the most powerful military the world has ever known has depleted its weapons stocks to dangerously low levels and these control the geopolitical balance of power. Beijing is watching carefully, licking its lips as increasingly the west’s ability to aid Taiwan if China makes its move reduces daily.

Terror groups such as Islamic State and al-Qaeda are burgeoning in the neglected ungoverned spaces of the Middle East, central and south Asia and Africa - and all have their eyes on Europe. Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps are unleashing proxy forces in Yemen to do deals with al-Qaeda groups in Somalia such as al-Shabab.

War in Iran has encouraged Tehran to let slip the Shia-Sunni Muslim schism for its Shia proxies to link up with Sunni groups. Previously its friendship of convenience with Sunni Hamas in Gaza was the most obvious Shia-Sunni link-up but now the dogs of terror are being let loose, forming ever-more dangerous alliances.

‌



View 6 Images US serviceman signals to fighter bomber crew (Image: CENTCOM)

Furious Donald Trump issues Iran a chilling threat with foul-mouthed outburst READ MORE :

Ukraine batters Moscow hours before crucial Zelensky-Trump meeting READ MORE :

One UK security source told the Mirror: “We are witnessing an escalation, a heightened risk of Islamic State on the rise and it is plotting against Europe. With so many resources going into the Iran crisis and the freezing of the Strait of Hormuz inevitably terror groups will take advantage in places such as Afghanistan, the Middle East and in Africa and the threat level is rising. And on Iran specifically we are seeing a large-scale increase in US munitions and fire-power arrive in the Middle East in preparation for a major increase in tempo. This war could go on well into the long-term and despite the talks that are apparently happening the prognosis for chance of peace any time soon is slim.”

It will take years for America to re-arm itself with missile stocks adequate enough to police global stability. Trump’s ill-thought-out war, a conflict with no strategy, is fuelling the conditions for conflict in Europe and the Middle East to converge dangerously as allies take up position alongside belligerents. And after years of defence spending negligence the whole of Europe is frantically arms racing to appease Trump’s demands for NATO members to do more to defend itself.

As Commander-in-Chief of the free world this ‘no war’ US President has probably done more to smash a wrecking ball into the delicate balance of global diplomacy than any other western leader since World War II.

‌



View 6 Images The US navy enforces the blockade on Iran (Image: US Central Command (CENTCOM)/AFP via Getty Images)

A snapshot of his misplaced trust in the world’s despots, whom he admires so much, happened when he was asked about China apparently smuggling 400 rocket launchers through Pakistan and into Iran to help its war effort. Trump replied that President Xi has “told me very strongly he wouldn’t partake. And he knows I would be quite disappointed.”

Add to that the near certainty that Russian intelligence is feeding the Iranian military with information on US bases in the Middle East and the drawing closer of the West’s enemies is even more chilling. It is entirely possible that at least some of the American military personnel who have died or been wounded were victims of Russian intelligence aid to Tehran - as it is they who have capability to pinpoint base locations, such as the one in Jordan.

To date, 18 American service members have been killed and more than 600 wounded in the conflict, according to the Pentagon. The Iranian Health Ministry said more than 3,500 people have been killed in the war.

‌



View 6 Images Donald Trump speaks during a Cabinet meeting on Friday (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

But the question of the US losing the war in Iran goes much deeper than Trump’s naivety as it affects every other conflict, Ukraine because it needs Patriot defence missiles desperately. Among the ground to air defence systems available to the US, the most heavily used was the Patriot, which used to target aircraft, as well as ballistic and cruise missiles. These are particularly valuable in Ukraine as Russian President Vladimir Putin has stepped up attacks on Kyiv with ballistic missiles.

Their near vertical trajectory and speed make ballistic weapons difficult to shoot down with anything other than Patriots or similar. Before the ceasefire was settled on April 8 US forces had struck over 13,000 targets across Iran, according to the White House. American air defences intercepted over 1,700 Iranian drones and ballistic missiles over the same period, at great cost to US defensive missile stocks.

View 6 Images Site of US Saudi strikes on Iraqi pro-Iranian forces (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



According to the Washington DC-based Centre for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) as many as 1,430 were used during the conflict from an estimated pre-war stockpile of about 2,330. Each Patriot interceptor costs approximately £3m. And some were used to shoot down £30,000 drones. Patriots are made at the rate of 650 a-year so it will take at least two years to get back to pre-war levels.

Also used was a newer, more sophisticated system known as Terminal High Altitude Area Defense, or THAAD, which has a longer range and higher intercept altitudes than the older Patriot. Supplies were already limited, with CSIS estimating that between 190 and 290 were fired out of an estimated pre-war stock of 360. America has just seven THAAD batteries so that the Iran war could leave the US without a system critical to defending ballistic missile threats from countries such as China or North Korea. Before the war the US had some 3,000 Tomahawk attack missiles but it has, according to sources, fired at least 1,000 so far and is running short. Getting these back to a normal stock level could take until 2031.

View 6 Images Mr Trump pictured with Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu (Image: GPO/AFP via Getty Images)

The Tomahawk Land Attack Missile - the TLAM - is usually fired from ships or submarines at targets well over 1,000 miles away, often hard shelters such as bunkers or fortress-like buildings. They allow attacks from a stand-off position, minimising the risk to troops. Even President Trump put aside his usual over -compensating confidence, letting it slip recently that production was slow for him. He said of missile stocks: "We have the best quality in the world. But we need a little more speed." And it was hardly surprising so-called Secretary of War Pete Hegseth recently told the Senate Appropriations Committee the Pentagon needs another £68bn for “critical shortfalls.”

‌



Beijing’s President Xi said some years ago that his Army had to be ready for a Taiwan invasion by 2027 and with the US entrenched in the Middle East with little sign of an exit strategy this is becoming a headache for the US.

It is possible China may feel the next couple of years would provide the optimum opportunity for success in taking Taiwan, with the US short of ammunition. Tel Aviv’s Institute for National Security Studies says it could be as soon as in 2027 and may include selective or extensive missile strikes; a civilian maritime quarantine or a military blockade; the seizure of one of the Kinmen Islands close to China; a special operation aimed at decapitating Taiwan’s leadership; and a full-scale amphibious invasion of Taiwan itself.

News.title: 'Nigel Farage has a problem with women and I won’t be afraid to call it out'
News.content:
'Nigel Farage has a problem with women and I won’t be afraid to call it out'

'Politicians like Nigel Farage want to scrap equality laws, doing away with protections for women, ethnic minorities, and disabled people', the Minister for Women and Equalities Bridget Phillipson writes

View 2 Images Bridget Phillipson tore into Nigel Farage's record (Image: Jordan Pettitt/PA Wire)

I’m delighted to be the new Minister for Women and Equalities in Andy Burnham’s government. It’s the first time this has been a standalone job and it speaks volumes about the importance of women’s rights and equalities to this Labour government.

‌



We’re at a perilous moment, with right-wing politicians wanting to roll back women’s hard-won rights, and an online discourse that’s increasingly down the gutter, pushing for a future that’s not what Britain is about.

‌



I don’t accept this and will do everything I can in my new job to take this country forwards not backwards. Whether it’s cutting child poverty, tackling violence against women and girls, or fighting for equal pay, I’ll give it my all.

‌



This week, I visited a rape crisis centre. The staff there do incredible work helping women to find safety, security, and space to heal from profound trauma.

Andy Burnham appoints Grammy-winning Clean Bandit star as top economic adviser READ MORE :

Bev Craig succeeds Andy Burnham as Greater Manchester Mayor in major Labour victory READ MORE :

View 2 Images Bridget Phillipson vowed to fight to strengthen rights (Image: Thomas Krych/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

Labour committed in our manifesto to halve violence against women and girls, and this is a pledge I’ll be putting at the heart of what I do.

‌



It’s deeply personal to me - before entering politics, I managed a refuge for women and children fleeing abuse.

I saw firsthand that ‘rights’ aren’t abstract. They’re a real and silent guardian in people’s day-to-day life. It’s the ability of a woman to walk home safely at night, of a disabled person to use public transport, or of workers to be paid equally for equal work, something our trade unions fought hard to secure.

As the parliamentary wing of the labour movement, it has been the duty of the Labour Party to secure these advances – and we have. The Equal Pay Act 1970, the Sex Discrimination Act 1970, the Equality Act 2010, the Employment Rights Act 2025.

‌



But not everyone thinks we should keep these laws. Politicians like Nigel Farage want to scrap equality laws, doing away with protections for women, ethnic minorities, and disabled people. Removing bars on discrimination on the grounds of religious belief or sexual orientation.

It’s unsurprising, given Farage’s form on this issue - he’s clearly got a problem with women, and I won’t be afraid to call it out. Whether he’s saying the awful Andrew Tate is an “important voice” for men, or that women shouldn’t get maternity leave.

So when right-wing politicians launch their diatribe against equality laws, remember what they really are – maternity rights, disability rights, the things working class people have fought for to drive progress in our society.

‌



As Minister for Women and Equalities, I won’t let Reform UK turn back the clock. I won’t just defend these rights, I will go further to strengthen them.

'I want to reinvigorate the party'

I’ve got myself a second job, but not the kind Nigel Farage loves. I’m now Chair of the Labour Party – and will be out speaking to people across the country, and of course Mirror readers, to hear about what you want to see from this government.

I joined Labour as a teenager, having watched the Conservatives wreck the North East. In time, I saw firsthand the difference Labour makes – stronger rights at work, a better NHS, more opportunities for children.

‌



I want to reinvigorate the party. That started with beating Reform and the Greens in Greater Manchester this week.

We face the fight of our lives, but I’ll work with members and unions to build the election-winning machine that sees off Reform’s divisive politics and secures a second Labour term.

'Andy Burnham can take on status quo'

Andy Burnham is off to a flyer as Prime Minister. He’s shown that he isn’t afraid to take on the status quo and has given us some hope.

‌



Too many people saw the decline of our country as inevitable. They said rough sleeping is a fact of life, public transport can’t be affordable, local pubs have to close, issues like social care are just too tricky.

Labour will show them.

'Cheaper summer for families'

Now school’s out, I hope everyone is enjoying their summer holidays.

Article continues below

Labour slashed VAT on children’s meals and attractions to give parents breathing space on days out.

When schools open again, uniform costs will be cheaper, more free breakfast clubs will open and half a million more children will have access to free school meals.

News.title: William and Kate bring children to Commonwealth Games
News.content:
The Prince and Princess of Wales have brought their three children to watch some of the final sporting events at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

Cheering crowds at the city's OVO Hydro were treated to exhilarating performances in the netball semi-finals where the family watched New Zealand's 61-54 win over England.

Known as the Duke and Duchess of Rothesay while in Scotland, the couple also spent time meeting athletes, staff and volunteers during a slightly blustery visit to the venue on the River Clyde.

They then made their way to the Sir Chris Hoy Velodrome - where they chatted to British cyclist Laura Kenny and sat one row behind Olympic cycling champion, Sir Chris.

News.title: Sir John Curtice: The 'Burnham bounce' is real but it's not massive
News.content:
But with still no more than a narrow lead over Reform, it is unsurprising Burnham has ruled out an early election. In any event, Reform's displacement from first place in the polls for the first time in over a year appears to owe more to its own difficulties than it does to Labour's new-found popularity.

Reform has been dogged in recent weeks by questions about the legality of the source of some of its funding and about whether Farage should have declared to the Commons authorities some of the funding he received before being elected an MP. Following these allegations, Farage announced on 7 July that he was standing down and putting himself again before the voters of his Clacton constituency in a by-election now scheduled for 13 August.

This move appears to have backfired. Immediately before Farage's announcement, Reform's average poll rating stood at 27%. In the polls conducted immediately after Farage's announcement, it fell by three points to 24%, the level at which it still stands now, and the lowest it has been for 15 months. At the same time, Farage's personal poll ratings are now the worst they have been since he returned as Reform's leader during the 2024 election campaign.

News.title: He thought a fitness supplement was safe, but it sent him into psychosis
News.content:
Daniel Murphy thought he was taking a safe and tested dietary supplement that would help him put on muscle in the gym.

But over the following two years, his mental health spiralled to such a degree he ended up in a state of psychosis in which he believed his wife was trying to steal his business and his mother-in-law was going to kill him.

Unknown to Daniel, the daily pills he had been taking had been mixed with testosterone.

The 32-year-old is one of 54,000 consumers listed in a case against a multimillion-pound peptide company based in the US, which sold its products around the world.

The owner of Paradigm Peptides, Matthew Kawa, was jailed for five years and 10 months on Thursday after he admitted deliberately selling unapproved medicines, trying to deceive people about what they were and illegally bringing the products into the country.

His sister, Jennifer Stechkober, who also pleaded guilty to selling unapproved medicines, was sent to prison for a year and four months.

Both admitted they had lied about where the pills were sourced, their purity and their company's testing procedures. Despite claiming the supplements were manufactured in the US, they were actually imported from China, India and several other countries. The pair also faked certificates of analysis, the documents that prove the safety and quality of a product.

Paradigm Peptides' website had stated it "stringently" tested all their products to ensure "efficacy, purity and potency", but the pair admitted not testing or analysing any of the products they sold, so they had not been aware they had been mixed with testosterone.

News.title: The five dramatic days that shook Infantino and world football
News.content:
The question many have asked around Infantino's plan is tied into a separate - but critical - aspect of the fundamental reasons behind this week unravelling.

Fifa is a not-for-profit organisation. It has huge financial reserves - over $2bn (Â£1.48bn) - and is expected to announce record revenues of about $15bn (Â£11.13bn) in relation to this summer's World Cup.

Given that backdrop - and the reality some countries simply did not need the extra $40m (Â£29.67m) being offered for football development initiatives if they signed up to Infantino's plan by 19 September - many wondered why private investment was needed in the first place.

It was a question that needed to be asked. But that did not happen in public - or, it has become apparent, privately in Fifa's corridors of power.

Many of Fifa's most senior people - from vice-presidents to special advisers and executives - did not have a chance to ask any questions, simply because they had no clue the plans were being drawn up.

Uefa had strongly opposed the plans from the moment they became public. When they were dropped, its response was damning.

"The current Fifa leadership has not only lost Uefa's confidence but also that of many other members of the football family," it said in a statement.

"When Gianni Infantino asked for the trust and the votes of Fifa's member associations to elect him as their president in 2016, he said: 'Of course we have to be transparent.'

"He told the assembled stakeholders: 'The money of Fifa is your money. It's not the money of the Fifa president. You are the national associations and the money of Fifa has to serve for the development of football and not for anything else.'

"On both these promises, he has failed to deliver."

It was not the first time a lack of transparency had been highlighted.

Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa - president of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), and one of eight Fifa vice-presidents - referred to it too.

He said any future plans that may impact global football should be presented to members "in a timely, transparent and meaningful manner".

"The future of global football must always be shaped through proper consultation, collective dialogue and respect for the established governance structures of our game," he added.

Football Australia chair Anter Isaac said trust was earned "not simply through good decisions, but through the integrity of the processes that lead to them".

"Football has never stood still, nor should it," he said.

"Some principles, however, should never change. Integrity. Independence. Good governance. Transparency. Meaningful consultation. Due process. These are not constraints on progress."

News.title: Faisal Islam: Four reasons why the World Cup plan never stacked up
News.content:
In the slides, Fifa's central argument was that football does not raise enough cash in relation to its fan base, that "Fifa has been under-monetised versus other leagues" and so "global football development gets squeezed".

It did this with reference to a comparative chart showing annual revenue as well as revenue per fan for Fifa, the Uefa Champions League, Premier League, US baseball and NFL American football.

On the face of it, Fifa is the poorer cousin at just $1 per global fan, compared to NFL's $52.80. But this measure is rather suspect.

The World Cup is not an annual competition - it happens once every four years. If instead this was done on revenue per World Cup 2026 match, Fifa makes multiples of the Premier League, perhaps more than three times as much.

As important, football is decentralised globally, so more of the revenues go to individual leagues, such as the Premier League or Champions League. Fifa was effectively arguing it wanted to keep more of that overall football pie.

Football's fans are also spread across the globe, in rich and poor countries alike. NFL has a much smaller base concentrated in the US and is pretty much the whole of American Football.

Finally, about half of NFL's revenues are paid out as wages. Fifa does not pay Erling Haaland or Lionel Messi or Vozinha. Profits would have yielded a rather different result than the chartâs focus on revenues.

News.title: Infantino on the brink? Who might replace him if he goes?
News.content:
Life moves fast for Fifa president Gianni Infantino.

It was doing so last month as he was zig-zagging across the United States in a private jet to make him virtually omnipresent as the World Cup reached its crescendo.

On 19 July he must have felt on top of the world as, together with US President Donald Trump, they handed the trophy over to Spain.

Less than two weeks later, Infantino is in a lonely place after scrapping controversial plans to sell off stakes in Fifa competitions to private investment.

Condemned by UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, castigated by fans of the game he professes to want to protect. These can easily be deflected as hazards of the job.

Less so the threatened boycott of Fifa competitions by European governing body Uefa, and its subsequent stunning statement in which it declared it had lost confidence in Infantino's leadership.

Concacaf (North and Central America and the Caribbean) and the AFC (Asia) also - in their own ways - have offered withering assessments of how Fifa is being run under Infantino.

"This issue extends far beyond a single proposal," said the AFC. "Rather, it has exposed fundamental weaknesses in Fifa's consultation and decision-making processes that must now be addressed."

Sources say, in addition to rejecting Infantino's plan, the vast majority of the Concacaf members are either losing faith in the Fifa president's ability to govern the game, or have lost it altogether.

On top of that, Carlos Cordeiro, special adviser to Infantino and appointed by Trump as senior adviser to the White House Task Force on the 2026 World Cup, has resigned.

Fifa's chief operating officer Kevin Lamour said in a statement to Associated Press that Fifa's own administration was "deceived" about the project.

BBC Sport has approached Fifa for comment.

It feels as though the walls are closing in on Infantino.

But if this is the beginning of the end of his tenure, who takes over?

News.title: What is Iran's Pickaxe Mountain and why does Trump say he wants to bomb it?
News.content:
US President Donald Trump has repeatedly threatened to bomb a suspected underground nuclear site in Iran known as Pickaxe Mountain, where recent satellite images appear to show construction work taking place.

Pickaxe Mountain is one of the few Iranian sites linked to the country's nuclear programme that has not been the target of US and Israeli strikes. There have been unproven claims that some of Iran's stock of highly enriched uranium may be kept there, which could be further enriched for use in nuclear weapons.
