"We'll be hitting that area pretty soon, and very heavily," Trump told reporters on 21 July. And on 28 July he said: "I know exactly what's going on at Pickaxe. It's not a big problem - we took out their nuclear sites, and we'll have to take out Pickaxe if we don't make a deal."

Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said on 22 July that "no nuclear activity is taking place" at Pickaxe Mountain, and described US threats as "a fabricated pretext for aggression, destruction, and sabotage".

BBC Verify and BBC Persian have spoken to experts and analysed satellite imagery to piece together what we know about the site, and the potential impact of any strike.

News.title: Decades-long search ends with discovery of new marine species
News.content:
The Great Barrier Reef might be the world's most famous underwater ecosystem, but hidden in UK waters lies an ancient marine world you may not have heard of.

Known as maerl beds, these carpets of coral-like seaweed create some of the richest habitats in the sea.

And 40 years ago, while studying one such bed for her PhD, Prof Christine Maggs found a fragment of pink-striped seaweed living on maerl she had never seen before.

The discovery would become a lifelong obsession and a decades-long scientific puzzle.

News.title: Greater Manchester mayor says Burnham's new powers will change lives
News.content:
Greater Manchester's new Mayor Bev Craig has said Prime Minister Andy Burnham's move to give the regions more power could "change our lives".

The Labour candidate claimed victory in Thursday's by-election after securing 309,525 votes over Reform's Sian Astley, who won 157,178.

The 41-year-old will succeed Burnham as mayor, after he stood down to run in the Makerfield by-election in June. The pair appeared together at a Labour rally in Manchester after Craig's election win.

Craig said: "For a prime minister two weeks in, to start giving powers out of Whitehall and putting it in the places that can make a difference - that can change our lives."

She added: "I will rise to his challenge about taking the power and control that he is offering mayors like me to make our regions better.

"Because that is what it is all about."

News.title: Soap star Shane Richie facing drink-drive charge
News.content:
EastEnders actor Shane Richie is to appear in court charged with drink-driving, police have said.

Essex Police confirmed it was called to reports of a suspected drink-driver in the Church Langley Way area of Harlow, shortly before 23:20 BST on Wednesday.

A force spokesman confirmed the 62-year-old, of Tadworth, Surrey, was arrested and a charge of drink-driving had been authorised against him.

It added Richie, real name Shane Roche, was due to appear at Colchester Magistrates' Court on 9 September.

Richie plays Alfie Moon in EastEnders, making his first appearance in the BBC soap in 2002.

The Sun reported he was arrested, external at a Tesco petrol station forecourt.

Essex Police said: "Officers were called to reports of a suspected drink-driver in the area of Church Langley Way, Harlow, shortly before 23:20 on Wednesday, 29 July.

"On arrival, officers arrested a man.

"A charge of drink-driving has subsequently been authorised against Shane Roche, 62, of Tadworth, Surrey."

Richie's representative has been contacted for comment.

Do you have a story suggestion for Essex? Contact us below.

News.title: Greek police fast-tracking tests to find out how British woman found in suitcase died
News.content:
Police investigating the death of a Scottish woman whose body was found in a suitcase in Greece say they could determine how she died "in the coming days" as they are fast-tracking toxicology tests.

Elisabeth-Jane Ross, 38, was found in an abandoned building in the Kypseli district of Athens on 18 July, reportedly by a homeless man.

The 38-year-old, known to her family as Lisa, is thought to have travelled to Greece from Edinburgh in late June, and went missing on 15 July.

Greek authorities are also looking to trace Lisa's American friends, who they said were also staying in Kypseli.

News.title: Suffolk fire 'stable' and fundraiser set up
News.content:
The blaze that has devastated heathland in Suffolk is now "stable" but crews have continued to tackle hotspots on what is the fourth day since the flames took hold.

The fire affecting RSPB Minsmere and Dunwich Heath started at about 17:00 BST on Wednesday and engulfed 371 acres (150 hectares) at its height - equivalent to the size of 210 football pitches.

Wildlife habitats of some of the UK's rarest species have been destroyed.

The National Trust has launched a fundraiser to help the habitats "recover and thrive in a changing climate".

Meanwhile, some local people have started returning to normal life.

A scheduled market went ahead at nearby Westleton earlier, which an organiser said was the chance for people to take their minds off recent events.

News.title: Manhunt after prisoner escapes from van outside court
News.content:
A manhunt is under way after a prisoner escaped from a van taking him to a court appearance.

Stephen Grzyb, 22, was being transported by contractor GEOAmey from Belle Vale custody suite to Liverpool Magistrates' Court to face burglary charges on Saturday.

As the van arrived outside the court building, at around 10:00 BST, Grzyb was able to flee and ran off down Red Cross Street towards the Strand.

Merseyside Police said: "Assisting him in any way will bring police to your own door, so it is not an association worth keeping."

News.title: Stick to spending limits, PM and chancellor tell ministers in joint memo
News.content:
Healey said the budget would "meet our fiscal rules" and "give businesses and families some of the stability they need to plan for the future".

A report in the Times says the joint letter told ministers they must work "within the budgets they have already got" even while "pay[ing] for new things they want to do this year and next".

While the ongoing war in Iran is pushing up inflation and borrowing costs, senior Treasury sources confirmed that the government was determined to stay "well within the fiscal rules" inherited from Sir Keir and Reeves.

But Burnham has said his government will stick to Labour's fiscal rules on spending and borrowing as well as the party's 2024 manifesto pledges not to increase income tax, VAT or National Insurance contributions.

He also said he will honour the fiscal rules imposed by Reeves, which include a pledge to balance day-to-day spending with tax revenues by the end of the decade.

An influential think tank said earlier this week that the prime minister only had a small margin of error to do this and that Healey may have to cut spending or raise taxes to meet Burnham's policy priorities, such as extra defence spending and better social care.

Healey was defence secretary under Sir Keir but resigned after a row over defence spending commitments, saying he was "certain" that Britain should lift its spending to 3% by 2030.

Questioned about funding on Thursday, Burnham's Defence Secretary Wes Streeting repeatedly refused to commit to that target.

"Before we set out specific spending commitments, we will also set out how we pay for them at the same time," he said.

Reeves left a Â£22bn buffer in her last Budget, but persistent inflation due to the Iran war could have eroded that.

On Friday, the PM said he would give all mayors of city regions in England a share of income tax revenue for the first time, as part of his efforts to move power away from Westminster.

Reeves had previously said that regional mayors could be given control of some tax revenue to spend on their local priorities.

Labour pledged to devolve more powers to local councils and mayors in areas such as housing and transport as part of its 2024 election manifesto.

More details of Burnham's plan are expected to be announced in the Budget, but the government said the rate of income tax will not change as a direct result of the reforms.

AJ Bell public policy director Tom Selby said Healey "doesn't have the luxury of pointing the finger of blame at the last administration".

"Healey will likely spend a chunk of his time leafing through the thesaurus looking for new ways to rephrase the 'tough choices' message of his predecessor," he said.

Shadow chancellor Sir Mel Stride said the announcement of the budget date meant "89 more days of unfunded spending commitments and damaging tax speculation until we get some details".

"Eighty-nine more days for Brits to wait before they know how much their taxes are going to go up to fund Burnham's spending addiction," he said.

News.title: Police arrest men over alleged modern day slavery
News.content:
Two men have been arrested on suspicion of modern day slavery and money laundering offences.

Dorset Police said the 20-year-old from Sussex and a 22-year-old from Buckinghamshire were arrested during an investigation into suspected exploitation, immigration and financial offences.

Officers made the arrests after raiding a business premises in Gillingham, Dorset, it added.

Three further men were also arrested for immigration offences, the force continued.

Dorset Police said the raid followed intelligence from the community and detailed enquiries.

The force added that the "day of action" had led to a number of individuals being safeguarded.

News.title: King's Theatre in Edinburgh re-opens after £41m refurbishment
News.content:
Edinburgh's historic King's Theatre has re-opened following a Â£41m refurbishment.

The 120-year-old venue has been closed for almost four years while the work was carried out.

The project has seen extensive modernisation work aimed at making the building more accessible.

First Minister John Swinney described the building as "an iconic landmark" and a "prized part of Edinburgh's identity and heritage".

"Its reopening will strengthen the city's vibrant cultural sector, draw in tens of thousands of visitors and support jobs and businesses across Edinburgh and beyond," he said.

Members of the public will be able to tour the theatre on Saturday and Sunday before performances begin on Friday.

News.content:

Michigan on Saturday joined Minnesota in reporting cyberattacks on nine of the state's water systems but an official said all systems were operating “safely.”

Earlier this week, authorities said cyberattacks targeted over 30 water systems in Minnesota. The source of the attacks is being investigated, but they came amid warnings that Iranian hackers have been focused on such systems.

The reports in Michigan surfaced after the state received a federal cyber alert Tuesday about attempts to tamper with operational technology at water systems.

Soon after, the state received “a small number of reports from Michigan communities indicating activity consistent with what federal agencies described,” said Dale George, the director of communications at the state's Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy. He later said nine systems were impacted.

“All systems continued to operate safely, issues were addressed by local operators, and there are no known impacts that posed a public health concern,” George said in an statement.

The FBI, which is investigating, has not publicly identified a culprit and a spokesperson declined to say Thursday who the bureau thought might be responsible. The FBI, Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency and other agencies warned in an advisory last week that Iranian hackers have been targeting water and wastewater systems and the operational controls of other critical infrastructure sectors.

“The FBI is aware of recent public reporting around Water and Wastewater (WWS) sectors," the agency said in a statement Saturday. "The FBI and our interagency partners are fully engaged to protect critical infrastructure and we remain well-equipped to protect against cyber threats of all varieties.”

Digital warfare has become ingrained in military conflict, and local water plants or healthcare facilities often lack the funds and know-how to install the latest software patches or take other security steps. That has made them a favorite target, both because of the relative ease of penetrating them and because of the panic such disruptions can cause.

Iran’s interest in the operations of water systems inside the U.S. dates back years. In 2016, the Justice Department charged a group of Iranian hackers in connection with a cyberattack targeting a small dam near New York City.

Minnesota IT Services said that as of Thursday, there were no active requests from Minnesota communities for residents to modify usage of their drinking water. The state agency said most of the confirmed attacks involved technology that water systems use to remotely monitor and control equipment. It said that being impacted meant investigators confirmed there was malicious activity involving the system’s technology and didn’t mean every impacted community had their water service disrupted.

For a few hours on Monday, the city of Braham asked residents to minimize water use as they tried to determine why the water plant was offline. The city of about 1,700 people, located about 70 miles (113 kilometers) north of Minneapolis, said in a news release that the water plant outage was due to a cyberattack, but it didn’t cause any issue with water quality.

The city said the attackers shut down the operating controls that shut down the well and water treatment plant. That left the city for a time only able to provide residents with the water held in the water tower.

In Plymouth, a city of about 80,000 located outside of Minneapolis, officials said on social media that their water infrastructure communications had been restored by Tuesday afternoon following a cyberattack.

During a Cabinet meeting on Friday at the Camp David presidential retreat in Maryland, President Donald Trump claimed without evidence that recent cyberattacks in Minnesota were the fault of the state, including Democratic Gov. Tim Walz.

Waltz responded on social media, saying Trump "knows exactly who is responsible for this attack, and knows that other states were hit too."

Huge crowds turned out for Brighton Pride, with around 300,000 expected to participate in the celebration over the weekend.

Marking its 35th anniversary, it drew headline act Raye on Saturday and it set to welcome Diana Ross on Sunday at its mainstage event Pride in the Park.

Performances from Five, Jessie J, Self Esteem, Leigh-Anne and a DJ set from RuPaul, will be taking place over the two-day music festival.

open image in gallery People taking part in Brighton Pride 2026 ( Getty )

The first Brighton Pride march took place in July 1973, organised by the Sussex Gay Liberation Front.

But only a small part of the community felt safe enough to take part, organisers have said, and Pride did not return to the seaside city again until 1991.

open image in gallery A huge Pride flag was strewn over the parade by marchers ( Getty )

For this milestone year, Brighton and Hove Pride sought to honour early activists and “remember the courage it took to be visible” as a member of the LGBT+ community.

Some 300,000 people are expected to take part or watch the parade, while up to 450,000 people are estimated to turn out city-wide for Pride, making it the biggest in the UK.

open image in gallery Raye performing at Brighton Pride ( Getty Images )

The event brings a big boost to the local economy, and organisers say it has raised more than £1.4m for LGBTQ+ causes.

The Pride parade set off from Hove Lawns at 11am on Saturday, going along King's Road, West Street, North Street and London Road.

open image in gallery It is the 35th Anniversary of Brighton Pride which held its first march in 1973 ( PA )

It ended near Preston Park where there is the two-day Pride on the Park festival.

Organisers say roads will be closed around Preston Circus to allow for the parade to disperse, as with previous years. They are set to reopen at around 4.30pm.

open image in gallery Around 450,000 people are expected to descend on the city for the celebrations ( Reuters )

Brighton and Hove Pride comes just a week after a van and stabbing attack Berlin left one person dead and injured at least 29 others.

People could be seen carrying placards in support of the German city, saying “we stand with Berlin.”

Following the fatal attack at the Berlin event, which defence secretary Wes Streeting condemned as “absolutely horrific”, police confirmed that armed police would be at the event.

open image in gallery A two-day music festival called Pride in the Park will be held over the weekend ( Getty )

open image in gallery The Brighton Pride parade came a week after the Berlin pride attack ( Reuters )

Speaking ahead of the events, managing director Paul Kemp said he knows the community is thinking of the people affected, and “we are coming out, and we are not going away”.

He has been managing director of the city’s Pride since 2013 but first became involved with it as a club promoter for the first dance tent on The Level in the mid 1990s.

Mr Kemp said: “I think it’s kind of poignant because this year our parade is the 35th anniversary, it’s the power of love and I think it’s really focused minds from a community perspective and the general climate of the feeling that LGBT rights are being rolled back.”

Republican Senator Thom Tillis threatened to withhold his vote for President Donald Trump’s attorney general nominee after the president indicated he would seek to fulfill his nearly $1.8 billion “Anti-Weaponization Fund.”

In the latest escalation between Senate Republicans and the president, Tillis and Trump exchanged demands across social media Saturday morning, with the president threatening to revive his unpopular “slush fund” if Tillis refused to confirm Todd Blanche.

In response, Tillis wrote on X: “It’s unfortunate that Todd Blanche, who I consider qualified for the job, will not be confirmed because of this reversal.”

“Despite comments as late as yesterday that the fund is dead, President Trump clearly intends to resurrect the payout pot for punks either by inappropriately establishing another bogus fund or pushing Congress to vote for a bill that the majority of Republicans in the Senate would be against,” Tillis wrote.

Tillis, a moderate Republican who has repeatedly pushed back on Trump’s use of power, has been locked in a battle with Trump over the $1.776 billion fund that the Justice Department created to pay those that Trump believes were unfairly prosecuted by the government – including January 6 rioters.

open image in gallery Republican Senator Thom Tillis said he will not advance President Donald Trump’s attorney general nominee unless the Justice Department permanently ends the $1.776 billion fund ( AFP/Getty )

The fund, announced in May, had been poorly received by the public as well as Democratic and Republican members of Congress.

Senate Republicans were so angry about the taxpayer-funded money pot that they refused to vote on a $72 billion immigration bill, which funded Trump’s signature anti-immigration agenda. Multiple lawmakers became outraged during a closed-door meeting with Blanche about the fund.

In June, the Justice Department moved to dissolve it, though some, such as Tillis and Republican Senator John Cornyn, are concerned it may not be permanent.

Tillis and Cornyn are holding out on confirming Blanche until the White House commits, in writing, to permanently axing the multi-billion-dollar fund.

Tensions bubbled over Friday after Trump said he wanted his “Anti-Weaponization Fund” to move forward. Later, the Justice Department lawyers filed an intent to appeal a recent ruling that cast doubt over the legitimacy of the fund.

open image in gallery John Cornyn, whom the president refused to endorse in a close Republican primary, is holding out on advancing Trump’s nominee until the administration confirms it will end the ‘Anti-Weaponization Fund’ ( Reuters )

On social media, Tillis cemented his position that he would only confirm Blanche as attorney general if they ended the fund.

In response, the president accused Tillis and Cornyn of revolting because he wouldn’t endorse the lawmakers in their respective races.

“If Senators Cornyn and Tillis, both upset because I wouldn’t Endorse them (they lost, and quit, respectively!), aren’t going to approve Todd Blanche, one of the most respected professionals, according to everybody, in the Country, to be the United States Attorney General, then I will keep Todd as Acting A.G., and push hard to get the Anti-Weaponization Bill, which takes care of those who have been so badly treated by the Crooked Joe Biden (and Obuma!) Administration (I get nothing, although I was treated horribly!), PASSED.” Trump wrote on Truth Social Saturday morning.

Cornyn told reporters Friday that his personal feelings toward Trump “had nothing to do” with his desire to axe the “Anti-Weaponization Fund.”

A dangerous heat wave will bring record-breaking temperatures to parts of the Western U.S. this weekend, prompting warnings for people to stay inside and heightening wildfire risks in areas that already are dry or burning.

A ridge of high pressure is holding heat close to the ground — what’s known as a heat dome — from Arizona to Montana, though the good news is that it will be relatively short-lived, National Weather Service meteorologists said.

The National Weather Service on Saturday forecast a high of 115 degrees Fahrenheit (46 degrees Celsius) in Las Vegas, the hottest temperature of the year. Phoenix is expected to reach 116F (47C), while El Centro, California, was expected to hit a record 118F (48C). Even parts of Montana were expected to broil, with a record 104F (40C) forecast for Great Falls.

In Las Vegas, Saturday's forecast high was 10 degrees above normal, with meteorologists warning of dangerous heat through Sunday, when the high is expected to be 114, said weather service meteorologist Morgan Stessman.

Overnight lows in the upper 80s to low 90s will make the situation especially dangerous because it doesn't allow people’s bodies to recover. “There's just no relief overnight,” Stessman said.

People are urged to stay indoors and hydrated.

The August record for Las Vegas is 116F (47C), while the hottest on record was 120F (49C) in July 2024, which also was the hottest summer on record, Stessman said.

In Montana, the entire east side of the state was under an extreme heat warning Saturday, said weather service meteorologist Jeff Kitsmiller.

Great Falls was expected to reach 104F (40C), topping its previous record of 101F (38C), while Helena was expected to match or surpass its record of 102F (39C), he said.

Still, it’s not as bad as the heat wave in mid-July, when some areas broke all-time records, including Billings, which reached 111F (44C) on July 12, Kitsmiller said.

“That was a rare heat wave,” he said. “This one fits for this time of year.”

By Sunday, much of the state will have highs in the 70s, he said.

Heat is exacerbating wildfire risks

Forecasters are warning that this heat wave, combined with drying from past heat, will add to wildfire risks across the West.

“We’re definitely worried about that” in Montana, where fires already are burning and high winds are forecast for the weekend, said Kitsmiller, adding that most of the state was under a red flag warning.

In Nevada, “with this heat dome setting up, we’ve lost some of the moisture that we did have — like relative humidity in the afternoon bottoming out in the single digits in quite a few places,” Stessman said.

The U.S. Forest Service has said there is an enhanced wildfire risk through Sunday in most of Southern California except for the coastline.

Climate change is making heat waves, wildfires more frequent

Climate change from the burning of coal, oil and natural gas is causing larger, more intense and longer-lasting heat waves — which lead to more intense droughts and contribute to larger, more destructive wildfires.

This year’s weather is also expected to be affected by El Nino, a natural warming of the equatorial Pacific that alters weather patterns and spikes temperatures across the globe.

The current El Nino is expected to rank as among the most intense since the weather service began tracking the phenomenon in 1950, experts said. It's already broken records for intensity at its early stages, United Nations officials warned Friday.

Iraq and Turkey signed a deal Saturday to increase oil exports through a pipeline to the Turkish Mediterranean port of Ceyhan, as Baghdad seeks to diversify its oil export routes and reduce reliance on Gulf shipping lanes.

Iraqi Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair al-Abadi said in a statement that the agreement will remain in effect for one year while the two countries finalize a broader framework agreement covering cooperation in the oil, electricity and water resources sectors.

The agreement comes as Iraq moves to strengthen the resilience of its oil export infrastructure following disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz since the U.S.-Iran war began in February.

Al-Abadi said the deal provides for a minimum export volume of 750,000 barrels of Iraqi crude per day through the pipeline, which runs from Kirkuk in northern Iraq to Ceyhan.

The Iraq-Turkey pipeline has been largely idle since 2023 after exports from Iraq’s semiautonomous Kurdish region were halted following legal and commercial disputes, although exports through it resumed in a limited capacity last year.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi called the agreement “an important strategic milestone to ensure the uninterrupted flow of our oil exports and strengthen economic cooperation.”

Before the conflict, Iraq was exporting around 3.5 million barrels of crude oil per day in total, with most of those exports shipped through its southern terminals via the Strait of Hormuz.

The planned exports through the Turkey pipeline would represent part of that total export capacity. It would not reach prewar levels but would represent an increase from the current exports of around 200,000 barrels per day.

Iraq relies heavily on oil revenues, which account for the vast majority of government income.

The signing of the deal comes days after al-Zaidi visited Ankara for talks on security, trade, energy, transportation and water management, as well as joint infrastructure projects between the two neighbors.

One project under consideration is a pipeline that would connect southern Iraq’s Basra to western Iraq’s Haditha and from there to the Ceyhan port in Turkey and the port of Baniyas on Syria’s coast.

News.content:

A North Carolina woman who investigators believe was abducted from her home was found dead, and a registered sex offender has been charged with her kidnapping and murder.

Robin M. Doyle, 58, of Hickory, was reported missing after a family member last saw her on Monday. Authorities believe she was taken from her home the next day after her father, with whom she lived, woke up to find her missing, her car still in the driveway and the back door left open, according to WSOC.

Doyle’s body was found on Friday afternoon in a wooded area in northwestern Catawba County, the Catawba County Sheriff’s Office said. The agency said it was not releasing Doyle’s cause of death as of Friday afternoon, while the manner of death is suspected to be homicide.

Investigators identified Leroy Allen Loper, 54, a registered sex offender, as a person of interest in Doyle’s disappearance. Loper was arrested Wednesday in Surry County, about 60 miles from Doyle’s home, on unrelated sex offender registry violations. Doyle was not found at the location where Loper was taken into custody, officials said.

Following the discovery of Doyle’s body, Loper was charged with felony murder, first-degree kidnapping and concealment of death in connection with her abduction and death, the sheriff’s office announced on Friday night.

open image in gallery Robin M. Doyle (left) of Hickory, North Carolina, was found dead Friday, and Leroy Allen Loper (right), a registered sex offender, has been charged with kidnapping and murder in connection with her death ( Catawba County Sheriff's Office )

Evidence collected during the investigation, including a bra found near her home and zip ties in her yard, suggests Doyle was taken against her will. Surveillance footage and witness reports also showed a red vehicle speeding away from Doyle’s neighborhood, leading authorities to Loper’s 2015 red Kia Optima. Similar zip ties were later found inside the vehicle, investigators said.

Loper has previous felony convictions for first-degree kidnapping and second-degree forcible sexual offense, according to the sheriff’s office. He remains in custody at the Catawba County Detention Facility without bond and is scheduled to appear in Catawba County District Court on Monday.

Catawba County Sheriff Don Brown expressed the agency’s condolences to Doyle’s family following the charges.

"We are deeply saddened for Robin Doyle's family as they continue to endure an unimaginable loss,” Brown said in a statement Friday night. “While today's charges mark a significant step in this investigation, they cannot undo the pain this family has suffered. The acts in this case represent pure evil, and those responsible will be held fully accountable under the law. This investigation remains active, and we will continue pursuing every fact until justice is fully served."

Investigators are continuing to look into Loper’s movements around the time of Doyle’s disappearance. Anyone who saw him or his car between July 27 and July 29 is asked to contact the sheriff's office. Loper may have traveled through both Catawba and Surry counties during that time, officials said.

President Donald Trump forcefully disputed U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro’s decision to drop charges against a former Olympian accused of vandalizing the newly renovated Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.

“I disagree 100% with Jeanine Pirro,” Trump wrote on Truth Social Saturday afternoon, less than a day after Pirro admitted in a court filing that damage to a recently installed pool liner was “the result of flawed installation by the contractor.”

“I don’t know what she was thinking?” Trump added. “To me, it was a pure case of VANDALISM, that included the grass, which had a big 86 47 emblazoned in giant letters on it, and other elements of the surrounding area.”

Friday, Pirro moved to dismiss the felony destruction of property charge against David Hearn and indicated the Interior Department misled her office into accusing Hearn of damaging the pool liner.

Instead, she said, the company contracted to do the refurbishment quickly had poorly installed the new liner, which started peeling after installation.

open image in gallery On social media, people accused US Attorney Jeanine Pirro of recklessly bringing a criminal indictment against a man who did not damage the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool ( AFP/Getty )

Pirro’s admission was not only a complete contradiction of her and President Donald Trump’s previous assertions, but it’s just the latest in a string of high-profile losses – leading to scrutiny online.

Mark Zaid, an attorney who focuses on national security cases, called the situation “absolutely embarrassing” for Pirro, adding: “I trust at least a public apology is forthcoming to all of those adversely affected by these frivolous prosecutions.”

Norman Ornstein, a political scientist at a conservative think tank, wrote on X: “She is utterly culpable and should be removed and disbarred.”

Ron Filipkowski, an attorney and editor of MediasTouch, also called for Pirro to be disbarred, saying, “It is absolutely indefensible and gross misconduct to rush through a criminal indictment for political reasons before an investigation has been completed, which resulted in false evidence being presented to a grand jury.”

Conservative political commentator Scott Jennings criticized the administration’s faulty evidence in the case, agreeing that Hearn is “owed an apology.”

“The administration looks like a monkey having intimate relations with a football,” Jennings told CNN’s “The Source” Friday evening.

Jennings added: “[Hearn] ought to sue anybody that he thinks he can to get his name back.”

open image in gallery Trump ordered his administration to fix the Reflecting Pool, which has been plagued by problems for years ( Reuters )

When asked for comment on criticism, a spokesperson for Pirro's office said: “The filing speaks for itself.”

Earlier this month, Pirro brought a one-count felony indictment against Hearn for deliberately destroying property after the administration accused him of “violently” pulling up on the newly installed Reflecting Pool liner.

While announcing the indictment, Pirro had fervently pushed back on skepticism that Hearn destroyed the pool liner. Hearn had denied the government’s accusations and insisted the pool was damaged when he visited it.

But Pirro’s assertion aligned with Trump’s claim that multiple people vandalized the Reflecting Pool – which the president had ordered his administration to quickly refurbish to try and get rid of the blooming algae on the surface.

However, algae returned shortly after the pool was re-sealed and a liner was installed. The new sealant also started to peel off in chunks that bubbled to the surface.

In Friday’s court filing, Pirro said her team was misled by the Interior Department, which allegedly misrepresented that “nearly all of the damage” to the pool was due to vandals when it was the result of faulty installation.

open image in gallery David Hearn, the former Olympian briefly indicted by the Trump administration, had denied Pirro’s accusations and pleaded not guilty to charges before Pirro moved to dismiss the case Friday ( Reuters )

Pirro blamed the peeling of the pool’s lining on rushed repairs completed by a first-time government contractor that received a no-bid contract.

Though Pirro has seemingly blamed the Interior Department for not providing all the information, people online still held her accountable.

Gretchen Carlson, a former Fox News host, called Pirro’s reversal “unbelievable” and “disgraceful.”

Marc Scaringi, an attorney who represented Trump’s campaign in 2020, said it was “stunning how easily and brazenly Jeanine Pirro, President Trump, and other Trump Administration officials lie…”

“The blatant lies, political prosecutions, and lawfare coming from the Trump DOJ must stop,” Scaringi wrote on X.

Pirro’s office has previously failed to secure prosecutions against individuals that the Trump administration had targeted.

Last year, Pirro failed to persuade three separate grand juries to indict a woman on felony charges for assaulting an FBI agent during an anti-ICE protest. Once Pirro reduced the charges to a misdemeanor, a jury still refused to find the woman guilty.

The U.S. Attorney for D.C. also failed to secure grand jury indictments for a person accused of making threats against an official as well as a man accused of physically resisting arrest.

Notably, a jury declined to charge a man who flung a sub-style sandwich at a Customs and Border Protection agent.

News.title: Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid
News.content:
Manchester United 2 Atletico Madrid 1

JJ Gabriel gave glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

News.title: City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter
News.content:
Manchester City 1 Inter Milan 1; Inter win 3-1 on pens

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

News.title: Richarlison grabs last-gasp winner for 10-man Spurs in fiery Chelsea friendly
News.content:
Tottenham Hotspur 2 Chelsea 1

Tottenham concluded their tour Down Under with a 2-1 victory over London rivals Chelsea at Accor Stadium in Sydney.

Sandro Tonali put Tottenham in front with a deflected effort before Estêvão equalised for Chelsea minutes later. Tottenham’s cause was not helped by a red card for Austrian defender Kevin Danso, who lasted just three minutes after coming on at half-time.

After making a mistake, Danso brought João Pedro down and was given his marching orders for denying a clear goal-scoring opportunity. Chelsea came close to taking the lead with their one-man advantage only for Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky to make some crucial saves.



Just as the game appeared to be heading to penalties, Richarlison scored on the follow-up after Jamie Donley hit the post in the final few seconds of added time.

News.title: Massage guns vs compression boots: Which is better for muscle recovery?
News.content:
Looking after your body is no longer just about getting a good workout in; it’s ensuring that you’re properly recuperating afterwards, too. Luckily, in 2026, there is a huge range of products designed to aid recovery.

In fact, the recovery tech boom is playing a big role in the growth of the sports technology market overall. Estimates show it’s projected to grow from $39.6 billion in 2026 to $192.3 billion by 2034.

Two of the most popular products in this category are massage guns and compression boots. Both claim to ease muscle soreness and help you bounce back to training sooner, but they sit at very different price points. You can pick up a basic gun from around £40, whereas the cheapest boots we tested were £300. But which method is actually better for improving workout recovery?

Massage guns can help to improve flexibility in older muscles

Massage guns work by delivering repeated percussion and vibration to one specific area, which helps improve the mobility and flexibility of a specific muscle. In turn, this can make your muscles feel less tense and stiff. These gadgets can be used before and after workout sessions.

While useful for all ages, massage guns can be helpful for anyone looking to improve range of movement, ease muscle stiffness and boost blood flow – whether exercising or not.

“It will help temporarily improve your mobility so that you feel like you’ve got a bit more flexibility in that muscle,” explains Jonathan Wreaves, clinical physiologist at preventative health clinic Viavi.

But how do they actually work?

Most massage guns offer a revolutions per minute (RPM) range, which refers to how many times the massage head moves back and forth every minute. This tends to be somewhere between 1200 and 3500. The lower range is ideal for gentle massage and warming up, while a higher RPM is better for targeting bigger muscle groups and more intense tightness.

News.title: Battle rages over access to new ‘miracle’ HIV drug
News.content:
For the first time in the four-decade fight against HIV there is a “miracle” drug that can all but eliminate the risk of infection, but in the Latin American countries where it was tested almost no one can get it.

Trials show that Lenacapavir, made by Gilead Sciences, is almost 100 per cent effective in preventing HIV infection. With just two shots a year, those taking it will avoid contracting the virus even when frequently exposed.

The drug, which many believe could bring an end to the global HIV pandemic, costs $14,000 a dose in the United States. Gilead has agreed to licence generic versions of the pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) medication at around $40 a dose in 120 low-and middle-income countries, but almost all of Latin America is excluded.

Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Peru are among those with serious HIV epidemics that are shut out, despite having run some of the clinical trials that proved the drug works.

Their status as “upper-middle income countries” means they are too rich to qualify for the cut price generic version and yet they remain too poor to pay the US price.

News.title: Senior dating: a guide to finding love later in life
News.content:
Whether you’re a widow, widower or divorcee, the thought of online dating in later life can feel daunting. However, more and more people are turning to the internet to find romance. Roughly 16 per cent of UK adults are using online dating services to meet a partner, according to Statista. Among them, there are lots of singles over 50 using dating sites.

So here’s how to navigate your senior dating online, with expert advice from psychologist and dating coach Dr Pam Spurr, and sex and relationship coach Angela Vossen.

How do I know if I'm ready to date again as a senior?

Coming out of any relationship is hard. If you’re hoping to date after a divorce, bereavement or break up, it can take a long time to feel ready to date again. Dr Spurr advises taking your time.

“Many people feel bruised, even traumatised, after coming out of a long-term relationship or having been bereaved,” she explains. “Your feelings naturally vary from day to day about whether you're ready to get back out to look for love – or even for fun. A crucial factor is if you've come to the point where you have more good days compared to bad days”.

Dr Spurr explains that good days are the days on which you feel more optimistic about life generally, and you find your thoughts turning to meeting someone new. “That's an important sign that you are healing,” she says. “However, if you're still feeling deeply insecure or are riddled with self-doubt about your worthiness, take your time. When you feel worthy, you will find someone worthy of you”.

Feeling heartbroken? Learn how to get over a break up

How to start senior dating online

If you’re new to online dating, it can feel intimidating at first. The secret is taking things step by step so that you do things at your own pace. The first step, however, should be choosing a senior dating site that will help match you with like-minded people. This will narrow your search and ensure your dating experience is more successful.

Step 1: Create an online profile

Once you’ve decided on a dating site or app and signed up, you’ll be asked to write a dating profile. This should reflect who you are along with your passions, values and what you seek in a partner.

Try to be authentic rather than creating a fantasy version of yourself. If you exaggerate your accomplishments, your date will only feel deceived once they get to know you. Likewise, don’t be tempted to use a photo of yourself from 10 years ago.

Step 2: Spark meaningful chats with potential dates

Once you have signed up to a senior dating site and created a profile, you will be free to start looking at other people’s profiles and sending messages to anyone that catches your attention. But how can you initiate a conversation after an introduction?

“When messaging people on dating sites, ask open-ended questions to spark meaningful chats,” says Angela. A good example would be, ‘I can see you enjoy travel. What place have you always wanted to visit but haven’t yet?’ or “tell me more about your love of tennis? Did you watch the US Open?” If things go really well and the chat seems to flow naturally, you may decide to organise a phone chat or ask them out on a date. An initial chat over the phone can help gauge how well you get on and how easily the conversation flows. If this goes well, meeting in person may feel less nerve wracking and a little less ‘blind’.

Step 3: Prioritise your safety

“While most people are well intentioned online, it’s important to protect your safety,” advises Ms Vossen. “Keep personal details private (like where you live or your social media profiles) until you’ve met in person and built trust”. You should also arrange first dates in public places, share your plans with a friend, and trust your instincts if something feels off.

If the first date or two doesn’t quite hit the mark, try not to be too disappointed and remember that you can say no to another date. Ms Vossen says: “Be patient – online dating takes time, but with practice, you’ll gain confidence and enjoy the journey”.

Traditional ways to meet senior singles

Of course, couples continue to meet in a manner that predates online dating sites. If you’re keen to join the older dating scene but find the online world overwhelming, there are plenty of ways to meet people in real life.

1. Holidays and group trips

We are often our best selves on holiday, so it’s the ideal place to find a single senior woman or to meet men if the opportunity presents itself. Why not organise a trip on which you meet new people while doing what you love, whether that’s cycling, walking, sightseeing or just travelling around a new part of the world. There are many escorted tours that cater to specific age groups and interests. They also take away the stress of organising a trip yourself.

“An organised holiday or trip can be a great place to meet someone new and there are many organisations offering these for the over 50s,” says Dr Spur. “A word of caution though, you can spend a lot of money and there's no guarantee that you will meet that special person. However, if it's a place you've wanted to travel to then go with the mindset that you're going to have a great trip. If you meet someone, that's an added bonus”.

2. Activities and social groups

Whether you enjoy walking, reading or volunteering, taking up a new hobby or joining a social group is a great way to enhance your social life and increase your chances of meeting a new romantic interest.

“Joining a club or taking up a hobby can be a fantastic way of meeting singles who enjoy the same pastimes,” says Dr Spur. “You're doing an activity you enjoy knowing that there might also be someone there that will catch your eye”.

If you do meet someone that you’re interested in at a social event, Dr Spur advises starting with a simple ‘hello’ and an easy question such as how long they've been doing that particular activity or hobby. “This can open-up a friendly conversation that might lead to flirting down the line,” she says.

Start online dating for seniors today

Whichever way you decide to start looking for love, approach it in a way that you feel comfortable with. Signing up to an online dating service is a great way to meet other seniors. Remember, it’s never too late to begin a new chapter.

News.title: UK economy to flatline, warns Bank of England
News.content:
Britain’s economy is set to almost grind to a halt for the rest of the year, the Bank of England has warned.

Growth will drop to just 0.1pc per quarter, the Bank predicted, slowing sharply after a strong start to 2026.

Higher petrol prices and energy bills, a weak jobs market and rising mortgage costs are all draining confidence and spending power from the economy.

Inflation, which slowed to a 15-month low of 2.6pc in June, is also expected to rise again to 3.2pc later this year, the Bank warned.

Andrew Bailey, the Bank’s Governor, said inflation had “fallen faster than we’d expected” but warned that war in the Middle East would lead to a fresh spike.

He added that growth would “weaken slightly further in the near term as the effects of the conflict weigh further on demand”.

The Bank also predicted that unemployment will rise back above 5pc in the coming months, limiting workers’ ability to ask for higher wages to cope with rising living costs.

It presents a challenging backdrop for Andy Burnham and his Chancellor, John Healey, who have pledged to help voters struggling with the cost of living.

The forecasts came as policymakers led by Mr Bailey held interest rates at 3.75pc.

Although three members of the nine-strong Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) voted for higher rates, up from two at the previous meeting, the Governor dismissed suggestions the Bank is moving towards higher interest rates.

The public should “not… [think] the Bank of England is edging towards a hike,” Mr Bailey said.

“Frankly there is nothing I have said, or any of us have said, along those lines. We took a decision today to leave the Bank Rate unchanged and that is the relevant conclusion.”

Clare Lombardelli, a Deputy Governor, said voting to keep rates at 3.75pc “was not a close judgement”, calling the decision “pretty clear” given slowing inflation in the domestic economy.

Officials are monitoring the economy for any signs that increases in oil, gas and petrol prices caused by the war in Iran are creeping into higher costs and wages in the wider economy.

Mr Bailey said: “The possibility of repeated resumptions of conflict, combined with lower than usual European gas stock levels and a fall in global refining output, mean that risks to energy prices lie to the upside.”

He added: “Reassuringly, there are few signs so far that second-round effects are generating more broad-based inflationary pressures.”

Companies are struggling to pass higher costs on to their customers because of the economy’s weakness, he added.

Workers are typically securing only modest pay rises as the weak jobs market leaves them in a poor position to push for bigger salaries.

Mr Bailey stressed there are still major risks to the outlook given the war and promised to “monitor the situation carefully” and was “ready to adjust our stance”.

“It is our job to ensure that inflation gets back to the 2pc target and stays there, and that is what we will do,” he said.

Borrowing costs dropped in financial markets after the decision.

The Government’s two-year borrowing cost fell from 4.44pc to 4.34pc, the sharpest fall in a month.

The FTSE 250 index of mid-sized UK companies rose 0.8pc to a record high of 24,184.10.

Traders still believe the Bank will raise interest rates twice within a year.

However, Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said rate rises “remain more a threat than a reality”.

He said there was evidence of disinflation in the economy and interest rates could be “cut to 3pc in 2027”, adding: “That’s very different to market pricing for rates to be close to 4.5pc in 2027.”

News.title: Arsonists torch more Ebola clinics as misinformation spirals in DRC
News.content:
Two more Ebola treatment facilities have reportedly been burned down in recent days as health officials struggle to overcome violent public mistrust of medical teams.

At least a dozen facilities have now been attacked since Congo declared its Ebola outbreak amid fear, misinformation and suspicion of outside authorities.

The outbreak is the fastest growing on record and officials said the virus had now killed more than 1,500 people.

The official death toll from the outbreak centred on the north eastern Ituri province of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has risen by 500 in only a week.

Sources told the Telegraph the large jump in deaths was largely caused by a “data harmonisation exercise” between different regions, and the new deaths may not have all happened in the past week.

However, the daily confirmed toll has also continued to climb sharply with the latest government update reporting 50 people dying in the previous 24 hours.

Airfinity, a health analytics firm, said the outbreak “continues to outpace detection and the response” and there is a high chance of it spreading further inside DRC.

Sports.title: Uefa president calls on every European nation to revoke support for Gianni Infantino with Fifa chief’s future in doubt
Sports.content:
UEFA president Alexander Ceferin has urged European nations to revoke their support for Gianni Infantino amid rising pressure on his position.

Fifa president Infantino is facing calls to resign after his controversial plot to sell off the World Cup.



The 56-year-old devised a plot to create a subsidiary called Fifa Forward Enterprise, which would have presided over money-making assets at the World Cup.

Fifa’s proposal enraged the world of football, with Uefa leading the opposition and threatening to stage a boycott of the World Cup.



They were joined by the Concacaf and AFC federations, which effectively killed off the idea.

Infantino has since pulled the plug on the plans after admitting the project had “created divisions” that mean it could no longer move forwards.

But Uefa have now lost confidence in Infantino’s leadership after insisting he has “failed” on his promise to bring transparency to the role.

And according to Ben Jacobs, Uefa chief Ceferin want their member associations to withdraw their letters of support for Infantino that were drawn up before the World Cup final.

It’s understood that more than 200 Fifa members endorsed Infantino for a fourth term at the helm, including over 40 Uefa federations.

One of those includes the English FA, but Uefa want their members to turn their back on Infatino, the report says.



It goes on to say that Infantino’s future “is in serious doubt” after a contentious few months that has seen fans rage at Fifa over their bizarre decision to suspend Folarin Balogun’s red card at the World Cup.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

There has also been opposition to hydration breaks at the tournament, as well as a 30-minute half time show during the final amid fears football is becoming too commercialised.

With Infantino seemingly on the brink, Concacaf president Victor Montagliani is believed to be one of the favourites to replace him.

That comes despite being a long-time ally of Infantino’s.



PSG chief Nasser Al-Khelaifi has also been tipped for the gig, but the Qatar FA have thrown their support around Infantino – which may scupper any hopes.

Uefa’s damning statement strongly suggested they wanted to see a major change at the top of Fifa.

Their statement read: “UEFA welcomes FIFA’s decision to withdraw its plan to sell a stake in its competitions – including the World Cup – into private hands.

“We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game. We must identify those responsible and hold them to account.



“It is right that, in the coming days and weeks, UEFA will work with its associations and in close cooperation with other confederations to reflect on how this happened and devise a plan to make sure that it cannot occur again.

“The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA’s confidence but also that of many other members of the football family.

“The shabby, back room, opaque deal [Infantino] hatched and tried to force through were anything but transparent.

“This is a victory for the whole game. But it must not be the end of the story. The proposal has gone. The task of rebuilding trust in FIFA has only just begun.”

Concacaf also put out a strong statement which piled more pressure on Infantino this week.



They said: “When people entrusted with protecting the game conclude they can no longer do so from within, the football family is entitled to ask how such a proposal was allowed to proceed, and who bears responsibility for it.

“FIFA is not a private enterprise. It is a body held in trust for the game and its members.

“Those appointed to serve it carry a fiduciary duty, a duty of service over power. Where that duty is not upheld, accountability cannot be optional.

“We are all simple custodians, serving a game that belongs to us all.”

Sports.title: West Ham break silence on ownership after Amanda Staveley’s consortium 'agrees 25% stake'
Sports.content:
West Ham break silence on ownership after Amanda Staveley’s consortium 'agrees 25% stake'

West Ham United have released a statement which throws the future of the club ownership into doubt.

View 2 Images Amanda Staveley is reported to have purchased a 25 per cent stake in West Ham. (Image: Anthony Devlin/Getty Images for IWG)

A consortium led by Amanda Staveley has reportedly brought a 25.1 per cent stake in West Ham United. The Championship club have given an update an official statement.

‌



The move comes after the family of the late David Gold agreed to sell 16 per cent of their stake to Royal Mail owner Daniel Kretinsky. It, however, seems that Staveley offered a higher price to buy the full stake.

‌



In a club statement, released on Saturday, the Hammers said: "West Ham United can confirm it is aware of the announcement from Joint-Chair Vanessa Gold that she has reached a provisional agreement to sell her shares to a consortium of PCP Capital Partners, led by Amanda Staveley and Mehrdad Ghodoussi, in partnership with Ashland Forest Capital Partners.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"The proposed transaction will now be subject to a pre-emption rights process. This provides all existing shareholders with the opportunity to acquire their proportional percentage of shares in round one, and any remaining shares in round two. This process will take approximately two months and, until it is completed, nothing will change regarding the ownership structure of the Club.

"West Ham United would like to assure supporters that the day-to-day running of the football club is in no way affected by this situation.

‌



"Preparations for the new season continue to take shape with diligence and focus, and we thank all fans for their continued loyal backing at this time.

"The Club will be making no further comment while the pre-emption process runs its course."

Staveley is known in English football for leading the Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund's takeover of Newcastle United. She left her role as a director at the club in 2024.

‌



The consortium who have brought the stake in West Ham is reported by the Times to be led by Staveley, alongside her husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi and their firm PCP Capital Partners. They are said to be in partnership with the American private investment firm Ashland Forest Capital Partners.

View 2 Images Amanda Staveley is the former co-owner of Newcastle United. (Image: Lucy North/PA Wire)

Following the twist, a spokesperson for Krentinsky, who still owns 27 per cent of the club, told the Times: “The agreement we had reached with the Gold family in June provided stability for the club at a crucial time.

‌



“This does the opposite. We will always act in the best interests of West Ham United and are reviewing all of our options, including exercising our pre-emption rights in full.”

Representative of the Gold family, Vanessa Gold, said: “On the 12th of June Daniel Kretinsky and I agreed a sale that would have made EP Group the single largest shareholder in West Ham. Unfortunately, since that time the original deal and other alternatives that we have discussed could not be brought to fruition.

"In light of this, I have now reached an agreement to sell my family's shareholding to a consortium of PCP Capital Partners, led my Amanda Staeley and Mehrdad Ghodoussi, in partnership with Ashland Forest Capital Partners. While the process has not yet concluded, I wanted to be open with our fans about where things stand and my intentions.

Article continues below

"My ambition throughout this process has been to ensure the club has the right leadership and ownership to enable West Ham to achieve its potential and return to its rightful place in the Premier League."

West Ham suffered relegation to the Championship at the end of last season. They start their bid for an immediate return on Sunday, August 15, when they travel to take on Burnley at Turf Moor.

The summer transfer window is now in full swing with several Premier League clubs continuing to do business. The likes of Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea have been particularly busy and spent big money with Liverpool, Arsenal and Manchester United likely to follow.

Sales have been the priority for the latter in recent weeks but it looks as though Marcus Rashford will be staying at United after he said a formal goodbye to Barcelona.

Arsenal have been loosely linked to the United star but are firmly focused on deals for Vinicius Jr and Bruno Guimaraes. The Newcastle United captain has been the lesser priority in recent days but that has seemingly changed with an offer north of £75million reportedly enough for the deal to go through.

Elsewhere, Liverpool will likely need to pay well in excess of that fee to sign Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain. The French champions may ease their stance, however, as they edge closer to signing Maghnes Akliouche.

Sports.title: Kevin Keegan's plea boosts brain disease campaign led by England legend Nobby Stiles' son
Sports.content:
Kevin Keegan's plea boosts brain disease campaign led by England legend Nobby Stiles' son

EXCLUSIVE: Just before he died, Kevin Keegan spoke to Nobby Stiles' son, John, and encouraged him to push on with a campaign for a fund to be established to help with the cost of Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy

View 4 Images Kevin Keegan, who played 63 times for England, sent John Stiles a message of support

Retired footballers face being struck down with a brain disease at epidemic levels, campaigners warn.

‌



John Stiles, 62, son of 1966 World Cup legend Nobby Stiles, is calling for a fund to help with the cost of Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy (CTE) due to heading the ball.

‌



Kevin Keegan sent him a message just before the Newcastle legend’s tragic death from cancer, telling him: “Keep fighting, John." Former Leeds man Stiles said ex-England boss Keegan was one of the key voices highlighting CTE.

‌



The brain disease has claimed the lives not only of John’s dad but also other players, including Scotland legend Gordon McQueen, former England and West Brom striker Jeff Astle and Chris Nicholl, the ex-Aston Villa and Northern Ireland player.

Funeral director Robert Bush who hoarded bodies and gave wrong ashes jailed READ MORE :

Chelsea hit with £10m fine and suspended transfer ban after Roman Abramovich breaches READ MORE :

View 4 Images John Stiles with a photo of his late dad, the Man Utd and England great Nobby Stiles (Image: Mirrorpix)

A coroner ruled Nobby died as a result of repeatedly heading the ball, which he did around 136,000 times in his career.

‌



Even John’s grandson George, 12, is aware of CTE and apologised for heading the ball to stop a goal in a recent junior game. John, from Doncaster, South Yorkshire, warned the future impact on players could be unprecedented.

He said: "We need a proper fund like the one in America, which had $1.5billion; the £1million fund set up by the FA and PL (Premier League) is just a stunt. It’s an insult. At the moment, the families are funding the treatment of ex-pros, and the taxpayer is covering costs through the benefits system, which is wrong.

“There are at least 55,000 ex-footballers in England. Research suggests there could be 16,500 to 27,500 footballers withdementia. That is as scandal. The boom in the women’s game is a real concern for me."

‌



View 4 Images John Stiles with a photo of his late dad, the Man Utd and England great Nobby Stiles

Norbert “Nobby” Stiles died in 2020, aged 78. His family had to sell his medals to help pay for his care.

Born in Collyhurst, Manchester, in 1942, he made 395 appearances for United between 1960 and 1971 and earned 28 England caps.

‌



He played every minute during the legendary 1966 World Cup campaign, despite his own concerns that he was going to be dropped after the Argentina game.

View 4 Images John Stiles with his dad Nobby at a dinner alongside 1966 England star Martin Peters

An FA Spokesperson said: "While the link between heading in football and long-term brain health remains the subject of ongoing scientific and medical research, we have consistently been at the forefront of efforts to help improve the safety of our game.

Article continues below

"We have led the way in this area to proactively review and strengthen player welfare across every level of English football, working closely with our domestic and international stakeholders.

"We were the first governing body to introduce comprehensive heading guidelines across both professional and grassroots football, and we continue to review and enhance our game-wide concussion protocols in line with worldwide best practice.

"We have also invested in and actively supported multiple independent research projects, often resulting in groundbreaking and valuable insight, in order to gain a greater understanding of this complex area through objective, robust and thorough analysis."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick drops clear hint over three Man Utd transfers after Atletico Madrid win
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick drops clear hint over three Man Utd transfers after Atletico Madrid win

Manchester United beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 in a pre-season friendly in Sweden on Saturday in a match which offered plenty of clues to the club's transfer plans

View 2 Images Michael Carrick's squad for the 2026/27 season isn't settled yet (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United manager Michael Carrick offered a telling hint towards his plans for the summer transfer window through his starting line-up against Atletico Madrid on Saturday.

‌



United came from behind to beat the Spanish side 2-1 in Sweden thanks to two goals from Bryan Mbeumo. The Cameroon international scored from the penalty spot to make it 1-1 after Shea Lacey was fouled before bundling in a second from Jack Fletcher's low cross.

‌



There were plenty of encouraging signs for Carrick, who has also overseen a 5-0 win over Rosenborg and a 1-0 defeat by Wrexham so far in pre-season. Further friendlies are scheduled against Paris Saint-Germain, Leeds and AC Milan before United begin their 2026/27 campaign against newly-promoted Hull City on August 22.

‌



United have used the summer transfer window to recruit Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, while a handful of players have left already. But it's clear that there is still more work to do, and that the current squad on pre-season tour isn't the one Carrick wants to start the campaign with.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Bryan Mbeumo inspires Man Utd win vs Atletico Madrid as transfer hint drops - 6 talking points READ MORE :

Man Utd forward set for shock Premier League transfer 'approach' with stance clear READ MORE :

There were two changes to the starting XI from the United boss, with Radek Vitek and Joshua Zirkzee dropping out for Tom Heaton and Amad. Zirkzee scored and assisted in the thrashing of Rosenborg, yet only got 17 minutes as a substitute against Atletico Madrid, with Carrick prioritising playing time for others.

‌



The Dutch striker is on the transfer list and United hope to find a buyer for a player who has managed just nine goals in 75 appearances since making a £36.5million move to Old Trafford two years ago. Juventus are reportedly interested in Zirkzee, whose future is currently up in the air.

Vitek's status in the squad is clear, with United signing Darlow on a free transfer to become Senne Lammens' back-up. The 22-year-old impressed on loan with Bristol City last season and has no shortage of suitors, although his £10m valuation is yet to be reached. United are keen to cash in and reinvest the cash elsewhere.

View 2 Images Altay Bayindir was not involved against Atletico Madrid (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



Meanwhile, Altay Bayindir was not involved at all against Atleti, with Heaton, Vitek and youngster Dermot Mee the three goalkeepers chosen by Carrick. Bayindir conducted a training session prior the game in Stockholm before taking a seat behind the dugout to watch proceedings.

Manchester Evening News reports that Bayindir is keen to leave United this summer to find regular minutes and that Celta Vigo are keen to sign the Turkey international on a season-long loan deal, while a Turkish side could sign him permanently.

Bayindir has made just 17 appearances for United since joining for £4.3m in 2023. He played second fiddle to Andre Onana initially before Lammens' arrival last season made it clear he wouldn't get a chance as No.1.

Sports.title: Man Utd forward set for shock Premier League transfer 'approach' with stance clear
Sports.content:
Man Utd forward set for shock Premier League transfer 'approach' with stance clear

Manchester United striker Ethan Wheatley had two loan spells in League One last season and now the young star is reportedly attracting Premier League interest

View 2 Images Man Utd striker Ethan Wheatley is being linked with Everton (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Everton are reportedly preparing a transfer approach for Manchester United striker Ethan Wheatley. However, it is understood that nothing is advanced at this stage.

‌



The 20-year-old ended last season on loan at League One side Bradford City after spending the first half of the campaign with Northampton Town. The Red Devils youngster made 12 appearances for the Bantams in 2025/26 as he sought more senior first-team football.

‌



However, he failed to score for the West Yorkshire club and did not feature in either of their League One play-off semi-final fixtures with Bolton Wanderers. It came after Wheatley became United's 250th academy graduate to feature for the first team, making his debut in a 4-2 win over Sheffield United in April 2024.

‌



Bryan Mbeumo inspires Man Utd win vs Atletico Madrid as transfer hint drops - 6 talking points READ MORE :

After impressing in the academy, he was one of several young stars who joined first-team training back in October 2024 as Erik ten Hag prepared his side for their upcoming Europa League clash against Fenerbahce.

And Premier League side Everton are now reportedly interested in a deal. Journalist Fabrizio Romano has claimed that the Toffees are preparing a formal proposal and are expected to make an official approach to United shortly.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Our sister paper, the Liverpool Echo, understands that Everton are interested in Wheatley, but a potential deal is still some way off. It is also understood that the move is initially directed towards the club's academy.

The young star has also been linked with German Bundesliga side Schalke 04 and Dutch club SC Cambuur, but is still on United's books as it stands.

View 2 Images Ethan Wheatley had two different loan spells last season (Image: Cat Goryn/Shutterstock)

‌



Wheatley is under contract at Old Trafford until 2028, therefore interested parties would have to fork out a fee to land him on a permanent basis.

Following his recall from Northampton in January last season, manager Kevin Nolan said Wheatley had made lots of progress during his spell at the club and shared his disappointment at the forward's departure.

"I know he enjoyed himself here, I know his family were appreciative of how we looked after him, and I know Manchester United were pleased with how the loan went."

Sports.title: Arsenal reach transfer agreement with medical to come next in major Bruno Guimaraes boost
Sports.content:
Arsenal reach transfer agreement with medical to come next in major Bruno Guimaraes boost

Arsenal are hoping to sign Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimaraes this summer, with a possible hint at their confidence in a deal

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta is looking to stregthen his Arsenal squad ahead of the new season. (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Arsenal have reached an agreement to sell midfielder Christian Norgaard to Everton, in a hint over their confidence in completing a deal for Bruno Guimaraes. The Brazilian is a key transfer target for Arsenal this summer.

‌



As reported by the Liverpool ECHO, Arsenal have agreed a fee in the region of £7million with Everton over the sale of Norgaard. A medical is due to take place next week, ahead of the move being finalised.

‌



Norgaard only joined Arsenal last summer, but found game time hard to come by at the Emirates Stadium. Last season saw him make just seven appearances in the Premier League, with a further 18 coming in all other competitions.

‌



New Newcastle boss makes Bruno Guimaraes stance clear amid Arsenal offer READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Despite the lack of game time, selling the midfielder indicates that Arsenal expect more additions in the position, with Guimaraes emerging as a priority addition. Arsenal's interest in the Newcastle midfielder comes at a time of chaos at St James' Park.

It was confirmed this week that Eddie Howe has left his position as Newcastle boss. It was reported that his decision to leave the club was partly due to the possibility of Guimaraes being sold this summer, following the sales of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali.

‌



Incoming boss Matthias Jaissle is expected to hold face-to-face talks with Guimaraes. The chat will see him try to sell his vision and philosophy.

View 3 Images Arsenal are closing in on a transfer for Newcastle midfielder Bruno Guimaraes (Image: Jordan Pettitt/PA Wire.)

However, it is expected that the two clubs will reach an agreement over a fee in the coming days. The transfer fee is expected to be at least £80million, possibly up to £85million with add-ons.

‌



If an exit for Norgaard, and a transfer for Guimaraes is sealed, then the Brazilian will add to Mikel Arteta's midfield options. Martin Odegaard is club captain and is joined by Martin Zubimendi, Declan Rice and Mikel Merino, with three of the four players still on their extended break following their success in the World Cup.

The talk over Norgaard's future comes after he made a promise last October. Speaking to Danish outlet Bold, he said: "I can guarantee that Arsenal will be my last club abroad.

View 3 Images Christian Norgaard is leaving Arsenal for Everton

‌



“I still want to return to Brondby when my contract at Arsenal expires. My contract is two years with an option for a further year.

“I would be happy to stay at Arsenal for the extra year if things develop in that direction. If it turns out that it wasn’t the right match, we’ll go home to Denmark after two years.”
