The move will come as a huge blow to Newcastle, who have already lost Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali.

2 Guimaraes is on his way to Arsenal this summer Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Eddie Howe, who led the club to their first trophy in 56 years, has also left the club.



Arsenal will be welcoming a signing who has made 153 appearances in the Premier League, scoring 30 goals and assisting 26.

Guimaraes will likely be their fourth signing of the summer after deals for Piero Hincapie, Illan Meslier and Christos Tzolis.

The Premier League champions could also be set to sign Vinicius Jr from Real Madrid.

Arsenal have been weighing up a move for the Brazilian, who has one year left on his deal at the Bernabeu.



However, they have not yet submitted a bid to Madrid.

Sports.title: Lucas Herrington in line to become most expensive Australian ever in Premier League move
Sports.content:
Lucas Herrington in line to become most expensive Australian ever in Premier League move

Premier League newcomers Hull are poised to sign Australia World Cup star Lucas Herrington.

The 18-year-old centre-back, currently playing his club football for MLS side Colorado Rapids, was one of the breakout stars of this summer's World Cup.

2 Herrington featured in the 2026 MLS All-Star Game as one of the league's standout players Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands Hull are in advanced talks about a deal to bring Herrington to the Premier League.

The Tigers are ready to pay more than £20million, which would be a record for an Australian player, and Herrington is keen to join.

Harry Souttar previously held the record from his £14.5m move from Stoke to Leicester.

Herrington's Socceroos defensive teammate Harry Souttar currently holds that record after joining Leicester from Stoke for a reported 26m Australian dollars (£15m) in 2023.

Born in Brisbane, Herrington came through the ranks at local A-League club Brisbane Roar.

Last summer, he agreed a deal to join Colorado Rapids ahead of the 2026 MLS season, making his MLS debut in February.

But, helped by his impressive showings in Australia's run to the World Cup last 32, he appears set to make the biggest move of his career yet.

Herrington has earned six caps for his country since making his senior debut in March.

He previously starred in Australia's 2025 AFC U-20 Asian Cup triumph.

Herrington became the Socceroos' youngest-ever World Cup starter in their final group game against Paraguay.

2 Herrington achieved his ambition of representing Australia at the World Cup Credit: Getty

"I can't really describe it," he said after that game. It means everything to me to represent the Socceroos at a World Cup.

"I've been dreaming of it since I was a kid, and to be able to do that today, it's so, so special."

Herrington also featured in the last-32 defeat to Egypt, agonisingly missing a penalty in the shootout, drawing praise from Zlatan Ibrahimovic for 'showing a lot of courage' to step up to the spot.

Tigers continue to gear up for Premier League return

Hull are preparing for their first Premier League campaign in almost a decade after returning to the top flight as last season's Championship play-off winners.

Sergej Jakirovic's men have made four signings so far this summer as they aim to secure survival.

Former England goalkeeper Jack Butland and Ecuadorian midfielder Oscar Zambrano have arrived from Rangers and Maribor respectively, with left-back Matt Targett and Japan midfielder Hidemasa Morita heading to the MKM Stadium on free transfers.

Hull kick off the 2026/27 campaign at home to Manchester United on August 22.

Sports.title: UEFA president calls for blanket withdrawal of Gianni Infantino support with FA in talks to join mass protest
Sports.content:
UEFA president calls for blanket withdrawal of Gianni Infantino support with FA in talks to join mass protest

Gianni Infantino's future as FIFA President remains in serious doubt, talkSPORT understands.

It follows the shelving of plans to form a subsidiary body called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) that would have been part-funded by private equity and promised federations $40m each to join.



4 Infantino's time as FIFA president may be nearing its end Credit: AFP

Infantino sensationally backed down from the contentious project admitting it had 'created divisions', and off the back of UEFA threatening to boycott FIFA competitions if FFE got off the ground.

Infantino also lost the support of lead financier Joshua Kushner and JP Morgan in an embarrassing 48 hours where his grip of FIFA weakened.

Senior FIFA advisor Carlos Cordeiro also stood down, while FIFA COO Kevin Lamour issued a statement saying Infantino had 'deceived staff'. And British Prime Minister Andy Burnham called Infantino the 'wrong man' for the job.



Gianni, you've got mail

talkSPORT can reveal that UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin is discussing whether to ask all UEFA members that have backed Infantino in writing, a number believed to be above 40, to revoke their support.

UEFA declined to comment when approached.

Some senior figures in the English FA, speaking on condition of anonymity, have already discussed whether to remove their formal endorsement given to Infantino ahead of the World Cup.



The FA also issued a formal statement on Saturday calling for urgent change.

"It is time for a full and robust review of FIFA’s leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long term stewardship of football at its heart," the statement read.



talkSPORT understands the German FA remain opposed to Infantino standing, while the Norwegian, Polish, French, Swedish, Belgium, Canadian, Mexican and Jordanian federations will all hold meetings to discuss their stance.

How do FIFA presidential elections work?

There is a strong preference from several UEFA federations for Infantino not to stand again in 2027 and a willingness to block a vote against him if he does. UEFA carries 55 votes with 106 needed to win.

4 UEFA president Ceferin has lead the charge against Infantino's latest idwa Credit: AFP

Concacaf issue statement as FFE proposal withdrawn Concacaf and its 41 Member Associations welcome the withdrawal of the proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE). The Confederation also commends its 41 Member Associations and the wider football family for the courage and unity they have shown this week. At a moment that demanded principled leadership, our members stood together in defence of football’s long-term interests and the principles of good governance. That unity has prevailed. Concacaf would also like to acknowledge and commend the role of the media in bringing this issue out of the shadows and into the light. The events of recent days have exposed something that cannot now be set aside: the future of the FIFA World Cup, the greatest asset in world football, was advanced outside every established governance framework, without transparency, consultation or due process. A proposal of this magnitude does not reach that stage by accident. It is a symptom of leadership that has stopped putting football first. This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour. A full review of this leadership must now take place. This concern is not Concacaf’s alone. It is shared across many confederations, Member Associations and those who serve and love the game. When people entrusted with protecting the game conclude they can no longer do so from within, the football family is entitled to ask how such a proposal was allowed to proceed, and who bears responsibility for it. FIFA is not a private enterprise. It is a body held in trust for the game and its members. Those appointed to serve it carry a fiduciary duty, a duty of service over power. Where that duty is not upheld, accountability cannot be optional. As mandated by our Member Associations, Concacaf’s FIFA Council members will engage directly, and through the FIFA Council, to ensure that questions of governance, accountability and leadership are addressed properly through the institutions and procedures established under the FIFA Statutes. They will also work within that same framework to determine how existing vast reserves can be dispersed to our membership via the FIFA Forward funding for football development across our region, without compromising our shared future. We are all simple custodians, serving a game that belongs to us all. The unity demonstrated by our Member Associations this week has reaffirmed that when guided by courage, integrity, and sound governance the game will remain where it belongs: in the hands of football - not a single individual.

Concacaf also rejected Infantino's FFE plan and their president Victor Montagliani has aspirations to be FIFA President.



"He has always been focused on Concacaf re-election next year," said a senior source familiar with Montagliani's thinking.

"It is quite interesting that Concacaf and UEFA voting together only take a candidate 10 short of a winning a FIFA presidential election."

The election actually works with a candidate needing a two-thirds majority in the first round - 141 votes - but if a second round is needed then a simple majority is enough for victory.

Who are the candidates that could replace Infantino?

Plenty of UEFA federations would also back Nasser Al-Khelaifi to stand, even though a source close to the PSG president has insisted 'he has zero ambition to do so'.



Highly-regarded FIFA General Secretary Mattias Granström would prove another popular option.

4 Despite the likelihood of being a popular candidate, Al-Khelaifi is not gunning for Infantino's role Credit: Getty

Gianni Infantino's timeline of controversies 30 April, 2026: Gianni Infantino confirms at the FIFA Congress in Vancouver he'll stand for re-election in March 2027 30 April: Infantino tries and fails to orchestrate a handshake between the Palestinian Football Association’s President Jibril Rajoub and Israel FA’s VP Basim Sheikh Suliman 5 December: Infantino awards Trump the inaugural FIFA Peace Prize at the World Cup draw, an award seemingly created for the US President in light of his Nobel Peace Prize snub 7 June: Iran land in Mexico after moving their training base from America following rising tensions 8 June: Former UEFA president Michel Platini files a criminal complaint in France against both Infantino and FIFA alleging a smear campaign preventing him from succeeding Sepp Blatter as FIFA President 8 June: Somali ref Omar Artan is barred from entering the US with FIFA insisting they couldn't intervene, while Andrew Giuliani repeatedly accuses Artan of "talking to bad people" without elaboration 8 December: FairSquare make a complaint to FIFA’s Ethics Committee that Infantino has breached political neutrality 10 June: Infantino tells his critics to "chill, relax" 13 June: Trump doesn’t attend the USMNT's World Cup opener against Paraguay or any other game until the World Cup Final 2 July: Trump calls Infantino and asks him to review Flo Balogun's red card sustained against Bosnia 5 July: Balogun's red card is suspended by FIFA's disciplinary committee despite FIFA insiders originally claiming there were no grounds for appeal 19 July: A 27 minute and 22 second World Cup Final half-time show that Wayne Rooney called "crap" 19 July: Infantino and Trump present Spain with the World Cup trophy with the US President remaining on the podium for the lift 27 July: Infantino tells his critics to "pray, meditate or watch football" in a 15-slide Instagram statement 28 July: Infantino pitches FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) blindsiding confederations in the process 28 July: Sepp Blatter calls the relationship between Infantino and Trump "deeply damaging" 29 July: Infantino tells FIFA's 211 members they have 53 days to vote on FFE and offers each $40m if they join 30 July: UEFA reject FFE plans and threaten a boycott of all FIFA tournaments if they pass 30 July: Concerns over the project are raised by JP Morgan and private investor Joshua Kushner 31 July: Concacaf and the AFC reject FFE, senior FIFA advisor Carlos Cordeiro quits, FIFA COO Kevin Lamour says Infantino "deceived" staff and British PM Andy Burnham calls on the FIFA President the "wrong person for the job" 1 August: Infantino scraps FFE plans at 00:30 due to "divisions" but falls short of re-sign

The Swedish executive is not viewed as tarnished by Infantino's failed project and is believed to have been totally blindsided by it.

Within FIFA's currently divided leadership, there are prominent voices who want Infantino to quit now and Granström to take interim charge, potentially positioning him to stand next March.



Legia owner Dariusz Mioduski is another favoured name within UEFA, as talkSPORT revealed last month.

Those close to AFC President Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa insist he does not want to go head-to-head against Infantino, despite a strong AFC statement also rejecting FFE.

Multiple AFC and FIFA sources have told talkSPORT that privately there isn't the same unanimous position among all Asian federations as other confederations. Sheikh Salman would likely only consider whether to run if Infantino removes himself from the ballot.

talkSPORT has learned CAF President Patrice Motsepe also wants to be FIFA President one day, but as a close ally of Infantino sources believe he is currently more inclined to throw his support behind the current FIFA President doing one final term.



4 The AFC President would only seek to take Infantino's role so long as he doesn't run for re-election Credit: Getty

What is Infantino's current stance on re-election?

Those familiar with Infantino's thinking insist he has no plans to resign and is hoping plans to expand the World Cup to 64 teams, potentially as early as 2030, prove to be a vote winner.

Yet Infantino is in danger of a mutiny from some of his closest allies. As with FFE, if it becomes apparent another candidate has enough votes to defeat him, the FIFA President could yet walk.

Further emergency meetings are set to take place between Infantino and his inner circle to determine a path forward. His intent is to battle on, but a unified way forward under his leadership is not guaranteed if confederations and federations continue to vocally call for change.



Infantino is reliant on the fact that, as of now, he has 200-plus votes in writing, but there is nothing to stop federations transferring their support. The deadline for another candidate to come forward is November 18.

Montagliani appears to be the most viable candidate between now and then especially if he garners UEFA backing.

Sports.title: Ashley Williams reveals Robin van Persie refused apology over incident which ‘could have killed him’
Sports.content:
Ashley Williams has revealed Robin van Persie blanked his apology after he infamously kicked the ball at the Manchester United hero's head.

Back in 2012, Williams found himself the major talking point after a clash between Swansea and the Red Devils, when he launched his clearance into the back of Van Persie's head.

6 William's 2012 incident involving Robin van Persie was one of the most high-profile moments of his eight-year Swansea career Credit: Getty

The Dutchman was lying on the ground after being tripped outside the box, before Swans captain Williams blasted the ball at him from just yards away as referee Michael Oliver blew the whistle for a foul.

A furious row broke out with both players being booked, but that wasn't the end of the matter.

Fergie's fury

While the match ended 1-1, all the talk afterwards revolved around Williams, not least after a fiery post-match interview from Sri Alex Ferguson.

The legendary United boss famously said that the Welsh defender 'could have killed' Van Persie with his actions.

Ferguson fumed: “He could have been killed [Van Persie], I think the FA has got to look into it.

"I think irrespective of him having a yellow card, he should be banned for a long time because that was the most dangerous thing I've seen in a football field for many, many years."

The Scot insisted Williams had acted deliberately, and continued to call on the FA to ban him retrospectively.

He added: “Absolutely deliberate. Absolutely no question. The whistle's gone, the game has stopped, and he's done that right in front of the referee. Two feet from the player.

"He could have really killed the lad. It was a disgraceful act by the player. He should be banned for a long, long time.”

Ultimately, Williams received no further punishment for the incident, while Ferguson's comments have lived long in the memory of fans.

6 After Williams booted the ball at his head, Van Persie immediately jumped to his feet to confront the Swansea man Credit: Getty

6 Sir Alex Ferguson pulled no punches as he slammed Williams in his post-match interview Credit: YouTube/Sky Sports Retro

'I did try and hit him'

14 years on from the infamous incident, Williams was given a chance to share his side of the story on Friday's talkSPORT Drive.

And while the former Wales international revealed he had intentionally kicked the ball at Van Persie's head, he insisted there had been a huge overreaction to this, especially from Ferugson.

On the incident, he told co-host Ade Oladipo: “[Ferguson] He said that's the most dangerous thing he's seen on a football pitch.

"Did he see the Eric Cantona thing [kung-fu kick]? He didn't see that?”

Explaining his thought process at the time, Williams admitted he instantly regretted his split-second decision.

Asked if he felt bad at the time, he replied: “Yeah, I've spoken about this before. What happened was the ball came, and it was a little bit like when you're a kid and you go, ‘Oh, should I?'

6 Neither Williams nor Van Persie backed down in the aftermath of the Swansea captain's actions Credit: AFP

6 Van Persie had to be held back as he was left furious Credit: AFP

“And then I just hit it. And then once it hit him, instantly I was like, ‘hmm [that was a mistake]’.”

The 41-year-old added: “It wasn't a full punt. And I did try and hit him - there's no way around it.

“But I instantly regretted it and did apologise to him after that as well, so it was wrong.

"But I think it was just completely blown out of proportion. There were people on the news like the Monday, like neurologists and doctors saying how dangerous it was.

“I was like: ‘Hang on a second. I get paid to put my head in front of shots every single day, so it can't be that bad’.

“But it was one time, it was out of order. It was wrong. And it was one of the things that I definitely did [wrong]."

6 Williams revealed his attempts to make up with Van Persie were rebuffed Credit: Getty

Unforgivable?

Despite confessing to meaning to kick the ball at Van Persie, Williams then revealed he tried to make amends during their next encounter.

He shared that he had apologised to the 144-goal Premier League icon, but revealed that the Dutchman was having none of it.

Williams explained: "The next time I played against him, I apologised and he shrugged it off. He didn't really accept it.”

It's fair to say no lasting damage was done to Van Persie though, who went on to fire Man United to Premier League glory that year with 26 league goals, which also clinched him the Golden Boot that year.

Sports.title: Four new Premier League managers tipped to be sacked this season
Sports.content:
Four new Premier League managers tipped to be sacked this season

Half of the Premier League's eight new managers could lose their jobs before the end of the season.

That's the view of talkSPORT's Tony Cascarino, discussing the record number of changes in the dugout.

3 Chelsea's Xabi Alonso is among the eight new Premier League bosses already appointed Credit: Getty

Nine of the 20 top-flight teams will begin the 2026/27 campaign with a different manager from the one who ended last term in charge.

Eight clubs have already moved to appoint new bosses, with Newcastle searching for Eddie Howe's successor after he stepped down on Friday.

Premier League clubs with new managers for 2026/27

Bournemouth Marco Rose Chelsea Xabi Alonso Crystal Palace Pierre Sage Fulham Alvaro Arbeloa Ipswich Gary O'Neil Liverpool Andoni Iraola Man City Enzo Maresca Newcastle Matthias Jaissle (unconfirmed) Nottingham Forest Oliver Glasner

The previous record for coaching changes between the end of one Premier League season and the start of the next campaign was seven in 2016/17.

And Cascarino feels that with the managerial merry-go-round turning at full speed, chances are not all eight new starters will still be in charge come next summer.

"Now, out of that eight, you probably could say it’s very likely that half of them will be gone by the end of the season," the former Chelsea and Republic of Ireland striker told Shebahn Aherne on the talkSPORT Weekend Sports Breakfast.

Asked if he really thought that, Cascarino continued: "Well, if you just look at the numbers game… yeah, it’s very likely that out of them eight managers, four of them could be gone."

As such, he expects there to be opportunities for Howe to return to Premier League management sooner rather than later.

"Yeah, he’ll get offered jobs without a doubt," Cascarino said.

"How long he takes off, we don’t know that…I’m sure he’ll want to get back into football.

"He’s still, like you said, what, 48 he is – so he’s still a very young man in many ways as a manager.

3 Howe left Newcastle after the best part of five years in charge, during which he ended the Magpies' 70-year trophy drought by winning the 2024/25 Carabao Cup Credit: Getty

"And Eddie did a great job [at Newcastle], and I think if opportunities – like they always do – come up, Eddie…I guarantee he’ll be the bookmakers’ favourite about five times if he doesn’t take a job by Christmas, because there’ll be four or five managers that probably go by then."

However, talkSPORT understands Howe is in no rush to get back into management.

Newcastle, meanwhile, are expected to name Matthias Jaissle as Howe's successor.

The German is currently head coach of Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli, having previously led Red Bull Salzburg to two Austrian Bundesliga titles.

The managerial merry-go-round never stops turning

There were a whopping 11 managerial changes in the Premier League during the 2025/26 season, with Nottingham Forest sacking both Ange Postecoglou and Sean Dyche.

Arsenal's Mikel Arteta is still the league's longest-serving boss and one of only three who have been in post longer than three years, along with Aston Villa's Unai Emery and Leeds' Daniel Farke.

3 Arteta has been in charge of Arsenal since December 2019 Credit: Getty

The new Premier League campaign gets underway with Arteta's title-winning Gunners hosting newly promoted Coventry on Friday August 21.

There are five rounds of fixtures between then and the first international break at the end of September.

Sports.title: Bryan Mbeumo proves his credentials as a centre forward, Mason Mount makes his case for midfield spot and rising academy stars get their chance: THINGS WE LEARNED as Man United beat Atletico Madrid
Sports.content:
Bryan Mbeumo scored twice as Manchester United beat Atletico Madrid in the Strawberry Arena in Stockholm to win the Snapdragon Cup.

Michael Carrick’s side fell behind in the fifth minute when a cross from Arnau Ortiz crept inside Tom Heaton’s left-hand post, and United were unlucky to still be a goal down at half-time after Jan Oblak saved from Luke Shaw and Amad Diallo, who was making his first appearance since playing for Ivory Coast at the World Cup.

But Mbeumo scored a deserved equaliser from the penalty spot shortly after the restart when the impressive Shea Lacey was fouled, and another of United’s brightest academy players, Jack Fletcher, set up the Cameroonian for the winner in the 74th minute to send the majority of the 21,000 fans home happy after a game that also saw JJ Gabriel and Jim Thwaites make their senior debuts.

Daily Mail Sport looks at what we learned from United’s third game in pre-season after they followed up the 5-0 win over Rosenborg with victory over Diego Simeone’s side.

Mbeumo at the double

United could be in the market for another striker to support Benjamin Sesko this summer, particularly if Joshua Zirkzee leaves the club, but Mbeumo showed once again that he can be a threat through the middle as he scored both goals against Atletico.

The former Brentford player, who scored 12 times in his debut season for United – including in Carrick’s opening two games against Manchester City and Arsenal – converted from the penalty spot and then got on the end of Jack Fletcher’s cross to score the decisive goal.

Bryan Mbeumo scored twice for Manchester United as they beat Atletico Madrid in pre-season

Harry Maguire lifted the trophy as United claimed the Snapdragon Cup in Sweden

With Sesko yet to feature in pre-season as he recovers from a shin injury, and Zirkzee’s future up in the air, Mbeumo showed once again that he can switch from the right flank to give United another option at centre-forward.

‘I think obviously I have the luck to be able to play both positions, but I can't really choose,’ he said. ‘Obviously I've done great things on the right wing, but some good things as a striker as well. So I think I'm more experienced on the wing, but I enjoy playing as striker. It's always really good to score for the fans and for the team, but really good to give an assist as well.’

Shea goes from strength to strength

Shea Lacey was rewarded for his excellent performance – and opening goal – in the 5-0 win over Rosenborg last week with another start in Stockholm, and he seized the opportunity with another standout display.

Deployed again in the No10 role before moving onto the right flank when Jack Fletcher replaced Diallo in United’s only change at half-time, the 19-year-old’s movement and energy were a real problem for Atletico.

Lacey’s ability to go left or right and deliver with either foot is a huge asset. Having picked out Mbeumo with an inviting cross which he glanced narrowly wide in the first half, it was no surprise to see his trickery earn the penalty that enabled the Cameroon international to put United level.

Lacey’s flick bamboozled Jorge Castillo into tripping him up, and Mbeumo sent replacement goalkeeper Salvi Esquivel the wrong way from the spot.

A keen boxer before pursuing a career in football, Lacey showed his combative side with a meaty challenge on Ortiz before half-time which left the Atletico scorer in a heap asking why he hadn’t been given a free-kick.

We’ll see less of United’s academy players as the World Cup stars continue returning for pre-season, but Lacey and the Fletcher twins are expected to remain an integral part of the first-team squad in the remaining games against Paris Saint-Germain, Leeds and AC Milan.

Jack Fletcher also made a big impression against Atletico as he set up the second goal, seizing on a loose pass to intercept and go past his man before crossing for Mbeumo who beat Esquivel to the ball to score his second.

Teenage midfielder Shea Lacey continues to impress for the Red Devils in a midfield role

Bye-bye Bayindir

Altay Bayindir’s career at Old Trafford appears to be drawing to an end after United’s No2 goalkeeper was left on the bench in Stockholm and sources confirmed the club are in talks over a loan move to Celta Vigo.

It was the first time he had been named in Carrick’s squad in pre-season after going to the World Cup with Turkey, but third-choice Heaton played the entire game with Bayindir sat on the bench.

Senne Lammens returned to Carrington this week after helping Belgium reach the quarter-finals, and new signing Karl Darlow will be Lammens’ deputy when he is fully recovered from a minor procedure at the end of last season, so Bayindir is surplus to requirements after three years at United.

Heaton was caught out by Ortiz’s inswinging cross from the left when Atletico played a corner short in the fifth minute, and it appeared as though he was expecting one of the attackers or even Harry Maguire to get a touch as it bounced inside his left-hand post.

The 40-year-old recovered to make good saves from Ortiz, Sola and Iker Luque, but had a double let-off towards the end when Rodrigo Mendoza and Morten Hjulmand hit the woodwork in quick succession.

Altay Bayindir's United career appears to be coming to an end after he was left on the bench

Gabriel gets his chance

It may only have been a pre-season friendly, but the United fans among a 21,000 crowd in Stockholm will be able to say that they saw JJ Gabriel make his United debut alongside another rising star from the academy, Jim Thwaites.

Both teenagers came on in the 82nd minute, replacing Mbeumo and Andrey Santos, to play the final 11 minutes against Atletico.

There is huge excitement around Gabriel in particular, who doesn’t even turn 16 until October. The youngster dubbed Kid Messi looked eager to get on the ball and finally got his chance in the 90th minute. Faced with three defenders, Gabriel twisted and turned in the Atletico penalty box and saw his shot blocked. Moments later, he tried again but was forced to the ground.

United fans will be hoping to see plenty more of Gabriel and Thwaites, a gifted 18-year-old midfielder, in future and this was just the start.

Carrick said afterwards: ‘The senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players are doing really well. Jimmy and JJ coming on at the end are two younger players again. They had a first taste for it for us, so it's great for me to be in a position to give opportunities to the boys.’

Mount peaks early

One of the most pleasing things for Carrick in pre-season has been the midfield partnership between Mason Mount and new £50million signing Santos.

While the Brazilian has been playing a predominantly defensive role in front of the back-four, Mount has been given more licence to get forward and has embraced the opportunity.

The 27-year-old has had a frustrating time with injury at United since arriving from Chelsea in 2023, and he is looking to prove that he can be a key part of the club’s midfield rebuild this summer.

With Kobbie Mainoo and United’s other summer signing Youri Tielemans still to return to action after the World Cup, competition for places will be fierce – even more so if the club sign another midfielder. But Mount has looked sharp in pre-season, getting forward well and helping Santos out in defence when needed as well.

It’s a sign of his standing at United under Carrick, and how he has been mentoring some of the younger players, that he wore the captain’s armband in the second-half against Rosenborg.

Mason Mount has looked sharp during pre-season with competition in midfield fierce

Yoro’s a stand-in star

Another player who has impressed so far is Lenny Yoro, who has had to play at right-back with both Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui resting after the World Cup.

Yoro gave another strong performance in the win over Atletico, particularly in the first half when he was up against Ademola Lookman. He showed a little naivety towards the end when Thomas Lemar’s pass inside him almost set up an equaliser for Arnau Sola, but overall he will be pleased with this display.

‘Firstly, I’m a centre-back, I’m just playing there because Diogo and Mazraoui aren’t coming back yet,’ said Yoro afterwards. ‘I prefer centre-back, but if you can play two or three positions I’ll take it. The coach tried me at right-back and I’m doing well so it’s good for me and the team.

‘Atletico are a really good team. They were pressing at the beginning and we had to adapt a bit, but we did really well.’

Reds roll on

As United reached the halfway point of pre-season ahead of their Premier League opener at Hull City in three weeks’ time, Carrick stepped up the workload by making just one change at half-time – taking off Diallo on his return to action – and not making any more substitutions until the 73rd minute when Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire, Lacey and Patrick Dorgu were replaced by Harry Amass, Dan Armer, Ethan Williams and Zirkzee. Gabriel and Thwaites replaced Mbeumo and Santos towards the end.

Carrick revealed before the game that he will have ‘five or six’ of his World Cup stars back next week as they begin their fitness work at Carrington, and it’s possible that some of them could feature in the friendly against Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg next weekend.

The United boss was delighted with the character his players showed in coming from behind to beat Atletico, saying: ‘It's a long season and we're going to have to overcome some challenges and adapt at certain times, so we're trying to put things in place that will take us to the full distance.

'It's great to see the boys getting on so well; the spirit, the camaraderie. And naturally. It's not forced, it's not fake, it's just natural. And then, they enjoy each other's company, and they look after each other, and they did it again today.'

Sports.title: Chelsea confirm signing of Danny Welbeck as 35-year-old former England striker joins on two-year deal
Sports.content:
Chelsea have confirmed the signing of Brighton striker Danny Welbeck, 35, on a two-year deal.





Confirming Welbeck's exit, Brighton posted on X: 'Thank you for everything, Danny. The striker has joined Chelsea for undisclosed terms, bringing an end to a successful and memorable six-year spell with the club.'

Welbeck, who scored a career-high 13 Premier League goals last season, is now set to link up with his new team-mates on their pre-season tour of Hong Kong, before travelling on to Malaysia and Indonesia. The striker had 12 months remaining on his Brighton contract.

'I’m really honoured to come to a club of this stature at what feels like a really exciting time,' Welbeck said.

'I’ve had fantastic conversations with the manager and already feel that connection. I’ve got that fire in my belly.'

Chelsea have confirmed the signing of Brighton striker Danny Welbeck on 'undisclosed' terms

'I’m really honoured to come to a club of this stature at what feels like a really exciting time. I’ve had fantastic conversations with the manager and already feel that connection,' he said

Alonso and his squad are currently in Sydney, Australia for their pre-season tour but they will be moving on to Hong Kong this weekend after their 2-1 friendly defeat to Tottenham earlier today.

Alonso originally targeted the signing of Granit Xhaka, 33, but Sunderland refused to sell their captain. They also looked at bringing in John Stones as a 32-year-old free agent.

Maxence Lacroix, 26 and from Crystal Palace, has recently been confirmed for £52million. Morgan Rogers, the 24-year-old from Aston Villa, has also signed for £117m.

The arrival of Welbeck should lead to other movements in the striker department at Chelsea. Alonso already has Liam Delap, Emmanuel Emegha, Nicolas Jackson, Marc Guiu and Joao Pedro on the books. At least two of those five should be sold or loaned, and possibly three.

Joao Pedro is considered untouchable and not for sale, with Fabrizio Romano reporting on Saturday that he is set to sign a new long-term contract in the upcoming days. The Brazilian scored a nine-minute hat-trick in their 6-4 friendly victory over Western Sydney Wanderers. Delap struggled in that win, though he was surrounded mainly by academy products while on the pitch, whereas Joao Pedro was substituted on along with the A team.

Welbeck graduated through the youth system at Manchester United, for whom he scored 29 first-team goals across 142 appearances and later spent five years at Arsenal, where he scored 32 times.

The England international spent the 2019-20 campaign at Watford before joining Brighton, where he scored 51 goals across six seasons.

Sports.title: Man United star becomes target for Spanish club and Jordan Henderson inches closer to Chelsea move: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Everton discuss £7m Norgaard move

Everton are in talks with Arsenal over a £7million deal for midfielder Christian Norgaard.

The 32-year-old has been on Everton’s radar for some time as agreement over a new contract for veteran Idrissa Gana Gueye looked increasingly unlikely. They also have James Garner sidelined for the start of the season after groin surgery.

Norgaard would become Everton's fourth summer recruit after the £24m arrival of Hayden Hackney, while Tyrique George and Merlin Rohl joined permanently.

Norgaard made seven league appearances for Arsenal last season and 20 overall.

He joined last summer from Brentford in a £15m deal but wanted more game time. He also had offers from Turkey and Saudi Arabia but was keen to stay in the Premier League.

Norgaard, 32, has been on Everton’s radar for some time as agreement over a new contract for veteran Idrissa Gana Gueye looked increasingly unlikely

Arsenal want to upgrade their midfield with Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United.

The Toffees are also in talks over a move for Manchester United striker Ethan Wheatley.

The deal is viewed as one for the club’s academy. Everton technical director Nick Coc worked with Wheatley while with United’s academy.

The 20-year-old Wheatley was on loan at Bradford City last season and has been considering offers from abroad.

Dutch side Cambuur were keen to take him on loan.

Altay BYE-indir?

Manchester United goalkeeper Altay Bayindir is a target for Spanish side Celta Vigo.

The Turkey international was on the bench on Saturday for United's friendly against Atletico Madrid.

Bayindir had interest from Besiktas early in the window but they have since signed Alexander Nubel from Bayern Munich.

The 28-year-old Bayindir has other offers but Vigo are hopeful of reaching an agreement.

Manchester United goalkeeper Altay Bayindir is a target for Spanish club Celta Vigo

Cherries land Benfica defender

Bournemouth have completed the signing of Portugal international defender Antonio Silva from Benfica.

The transfer is worth £21.4m plus a potential £4.3m in add-ons.

'The mentality is always to win. I will try my best, and I will play for the fans,' said Silva.

'It's a pleasure to play for Bournemouth and in the Premier League. I can't wait to start the season with my team-mates and I'm excited to be here.'

Hammers youngster heading to Belgium

West Ham midfielder Freddie Potts is poised to join Club Brugge in a £10.5million deal.

The 22-year-old is due to travel to undergo a medical.

The Hammers have been trying to find agreement with Celtic for midfielder Arne Engels but had their latest offer rejected.

West Ham midfielder Freddie Potts is poised to join Club Brugge in a £10.5million deal

England U21 star swapping French clubs

England U21 defender Charlie Cresswell is joining Rennes on an initial loan from Toulouse.

The 23-year-old centre-back has had tentative interest from West Ham, Fulham and Crystal Palace but will undergo a medical tomorrow before joining the French side.

Rennes have an obligation to buy for £19m and a 10percent sell-on had been included.

Tigers target Nice winger

Hull City are in talks over a £17million deal for Nice winger Mohamed Ali-Cho.

The 22-year-old who can play across the frontline has also attracted interest from Monaco.

The France U21 international had spells with Paris St Germain and Everton as a teenager before signing for Angers.

Born in France, raised in England, and of Ivorian and Moroccan descent, Cho is eligible for all four national teams. He was a youth international for England U16s.

Tottenham academy graduate courts interest

Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott is attracting interest from Como, Ajax, PSV Eindhoven and Real Betis.

The former Tottenham academy graduate is in demand after scoring 31 goals last season.

Alkmaar are reluctant to sell the 24-year-old Republic of Ireland international to a rival Dutch club.

Chelsea inch closer to Henderson move

Chelsea have agreed terms with England midfielder Jordan Henderson.

The 36-year-old will be confirmed as a Chelsea player after putting pen to paper this weekend.

Henderson was a free agent after mutually agreeing cancel his contract with Brentford last week.

Jordan Henderson's path to Chelsea is clear with the two parties agreeing terms after his Brentford exit last month

Bees secure Sangare

Brentford have moved to sign Lens midfielder Mamadou Sangare for £39m.

The 24-year-old completed a medical on Friday and is set to sign a five-year contract with an extra year's option.

Tractor Boys revisit Enciso signing

Ipswich Town are in talks with Strasbourg over the permanent signing of forward Julio Enciso.

The 22-year-old Paraguay international had an impressive spell on loan at Ipswich in their last Premier League season in 2024/25. He also worked with Ipswich boss Gary O'Neil at Strasbourg last season.

Meanwhile, Strasbourg may yet take 19-year-old Chelsea right-back Godwin Antwi on loan.

West London calling for Real Madrid talent?

Fulham remain in discussions with Real Madrid over the signing of Thiago Pitarch.

As Daily Mail Sport reported last month, the teenager is wanted by Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa as well as £43million duo Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios, who are due in London today.

At 18 years and 226 days, Pitarch became Madrid's youngest player to start twice in the Champions League knockout stages, surpassing Brazil forward Vinicius Jr's record by 10 days.

Thiago Pitarch is one of a number of Real Madrid stars eyed by Fulham's new manager Alvaro Arbeloa, who was interim manager at the Bernabeu last term

He impressed in Madrid's 3-0 win over Manchester City in March and had arrived back in training determined to impress Jose Mourinho and fight for a first team place. But Fulham are hopeful of persuading him to join Palacios and Garcia.
