Sports.title: UEFA declares loss of confidence in Gianni Infantino's FIFA presidency: Pressure mounts on under-fire boss after disastrous World Cup plot as football chiefs look to overthrow him
Sports.content:
The FA, UEFA and CONCACAF are leading the charge to depose Gianni Infantino as FIFA president after he scrapped the 'shabby, back-room deal' to sell stakes in the World Cup.

Pressure is mounting on the under-fire boss after his controversial plan to sell a £3.1billion stake in football's most coveted tournament to a group of private investors led by Josh Kushner - an extended relation of US President Donald Trump - collapsed on Friday night.

The scheme, which received wholesale opposition from football nations around the world, has seen scrutiny on Infantino's presidency intensify.

UEFA, European football's governing body, spearheaded calls condemning Infantino's plot and, in a lengthy statement released on Saturday morning, declared they had lost trust in his leadership.

UEFA said: 'UEFA welcomes FIFA's decision to withdraw its plan to sell a stake in its competitions – including the World Cup – into private hands.

'The proposal was unanimously rejected by UEFA's national associations and by many other federations and confederations of all sizes around the world, whose job it is to protect football.

'UEFA thanks all the fans, leagues, clubs, players, individuals, associations and confederations that opposed the scheme, alongside the many Prime Ministers, Heads of State and commentators who have demonstrated to the FIFA President that football is not for sale.

UEFA have lost confidence in shamed FIFA president Gianni Infantino after 'shabby, back-room deal' to sell stakes in the World Cup.

Gianni Infantino waves goodbye to his unilateral plans for private investment in FIFA with his presidency in jeopardy

Carlos Cordeiro (left) quit as an advisor to Gianni Infantino (centre) on Friday

'We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast-track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game. We must identify those responsible and hold them to account,' the UEFA statement continued.

'It is right that, in the coming days and weeks, UEFA will work with its associations and in close cooperation with other confederations to reflect on how this happened and devise a plan to make sure that it cannot occur again. That review should be thorough and fundamental. No option should be off the table. The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA's confidence but also that of many other members of the football family.

'When Gianni Infantino asked for the trust and the votes of FIFA's Member Associations to elect him as their President in 2016, he said, 'Of course we have to be transparent. I have been this in the last 15 years of my life in UEFA. You will have to play a part every day in the life of FIFA', before telling the assembled stakeholders, 'The money of FIFA is your money. It's not the money of the FIFA President. It's your money. You are the national associations and the money of FIFA has to serve for the development of football and not for anything else'.

'On both these promises, he has failed to deliver. The shabby, back-room, opaque deal he hatched and tried to force through was anything but transparent.

'And with reserves standing at over $5bn, he has also failed to use associations' money for the benefit of the game.

'UEFA will begin work immediately with partners and stakeholders all over the world and right across the game to propose a new way of distributing resources through the existing FIFA Forward programme.

'We must start to use some of that money that is sat idle in FIFA's bank account to deliver the kick-start that the grassroots and the wider game need in each of the 211 countries of FIFA. But we don't need to sell off the family silver to pay for it.

'This is a victory for the whole game. But it must not be the end of the story. The proposal has gone. The task of rebuilding trust in FIFA has only just begun.'

FIFA member nations could trigger a vote of no confidence to oust Infantino, who is seeking a fourth term in next year's elections. The threshold to initiate the process is 46 FIFA member associations; UEFA have 55 members.

A spokeswoman for the English FA backed UEFA's statement despite the association having initially supported Infantino's re-election bid.

'We fully support UEFA's position,' an FA spokeswoman said. 'It is time for a full and robust review of FIFA's leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart.'

CONCACAF added: 'Concacaf and its 41 Member Associations welcome the withdrawal of the proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE).

'The Confederation also commends its 41 Member Associations and the wider football family for the courage and unity they have shown this week. At a moment that demanded principled leadership, our members stood together in defence of football’s long-term interests and the principles of good governance. That unity has prevailed.

'Concacaf would also like to acknowledge and commend the role of the media in bringing this issue out of the shadows and into the light. The events of recent days have exposed something that cannot now be set aside: the future of the FIFA World Cup, the greatest asset in world football, was advanced outside every established governance framework, without transparency, consultation or due process.

'A proposal of this magnitude does not reach that stage by accident. It is a symptom of leadership that has stopped putting football first. This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour. A full review of this leadership must now take place.

'This concern is not Concacaf’s alone. It is shared across many confederations, Member Associations and those who serve and love the game. When people entrusted with protecting the game conclude they can no longer do so from within, the football family is entitled to ask how such a proposal was allowed to proceed, and who bears responsibility for it.

'FIFA is not a private enterprise. It is a body held in trust for the game and its members. Those appointed to serve it carry a fiduciary duty, a duty of service over power.

'Where that duty is not upheld, accountability cannot be optional. As mandated by our Member Associations, Concacaf’s FIFA Council members will engage directly, and through the FIFA Council, to ensure that questions of governance, accountability and leadership are addressed properly through the institutions and procedures established under the FIFA Statutes.

'They will also work within that same framework to determine how existing vast reserves can be dispersed to our membership via the FIFA Forward funding for football development across our region, without compromising our shared future. We are all simple custodians, serving a game that belongs to us all.

'The unity demonstrated by our Member Associations this week has reaffirmed that when guided by courage, integrity, and sound governance, the game will remain where it belongs: in the hands of football - not a single individual.'

In the early hours of Saturday morning, Infantino abandoned his proposals to inject private equity into the operational and commercial aspects of FIFA tournaments.

His humiliating backtrack came thanks to the heroics of UEFA, CONCACAF, the AFC and two members of the FIFA hierarchy, who all took a stand against his divisive plans

The AFC, Asia's governing body, were the third and final confederation to reject Gianni Infantino's proposal. Their resistance made it clear he did not have the support to proceed, as opposing nations rose to a staggering 135 - 64 per cent of the FIFA membership.

With the controversy surrounding Infantino, member nations could trigger a vote of no confidence. The threshold to initiate the process is 46 FIFA member associations

The commendation followed CONCACAF's rejection on Thursday and came after UEFA announced a boycott of FIFA competitions. New Zealand Football also objected to the plans, despite the OFC delaying a continent-wide response.

Infantino said: 'The FIFA Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed.

'And more so, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the FIFA Member Associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the FIFA Council, the Confederations and wider stakeholders.

'Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place.

'Our purpose has always been - and will always be - to unite and improve. As a result, this proposal will not proceed.

'Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, and particularly in those countries that mostly need our support.'

The statement marked an embarrassing U-turn, less than 24 hours after he attempted to clarify his plans - blaming the media for misconstruing them.

One international football insider told Daily Mail Sport: 'UEFA's response is at the nuclear button end of the spectrum, which is impressive. We thought Infantino would survive the Trump refereeing intervention - but he has overreached this time.'

The proposal reached a terminal stage when Carlos Cordeiro, senior advisor to Gianni Infantino, announced his resignation from FIFA - becoming the first internal dissident.

Six hours later, FIFA's chief operating officer Kevin Lamour turned against the president - risking his job by criticising the plans and calling on nations to dethrone Infantino. Lamour admitted FIFA Forward Enterprise was the brainchild of 'one person' as he landed a critical blow to the FIFA president.

Infantino had hoped to create a new enterprise with significant investment from Joshua Kushner - brother of Jared, Donald Trump's son-in-law. Meanwhile, investment bank J.P. Morgan were advising on potential investors.

Democratic senator Ron Wyden, who leads an investigation into Jared Kushner, said on Friday: 'Soccer fans around the world are rightfully outraged by this scheme from Infantino and Joshua Kushner to turn the World Cup into just another commodity for private equity to buy up.

'It seems clear from the global backlash that this corrupt plan is unlikely to succeed, but it is just one of dozens of shady deals by Trump's family and close associates to get rich from the presidency.'

A significant number of FIFA members raised concerns from the initial leak of the plan, questioning how such thorough ideas could be developed unilaterally without prior consultation.

Despite FIFA maintaining throughout that there would be a proper consultation period, there were major questions about how that could be achieved when potential investors were already lined up.

UEFA accused FIFA of trying to bribe members with a £30million ($40million) incentive to approve Infantino's plan, with a September 19 deadline to respond to the offer.

Alongside UEFA's protest, sources told the Daily Mail Sport that CONCACAF nations believe he is losing or has already lost their confidence.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham believes Infantino's position is untenable and he is not alone.

Speaking to reporters in Sheffield on Friday, Burnham said: 'This was an outrageous suggestion. The idea that it could even be brought forward shows that, in my view, [he] is the wrong man to lead the organisation.'

President of the Norwegian FA, Lise Klaveness, has consistently taken a principled stand against Infantino and added her name to those supporting UEFA's call for him to quit.

'It was absolutely necessary for Gianni Infantino and FIFA to withdraw this proposal,' said Klaveness.

'That has now happened, and we are of course pleased with the outcome. It has been reassuring to be part of a strong and united UEFA throughout this process, and I would like to thank the UEFA President for his clear and decisive leadership.

'At the same time, we must acknowledge that the entire framework of international football cooperation was unnecessarily put at risk in pursuit of individual interests rather than the best interests of the game.

'This has been visible to many for a long time, including those of us elected to positions intended to safeguard checks and balances and provide ongoing oversight.

'We have to recognise that these mechanisms have not worked well enough. The situation ultimately reached a point where the threat of withdrawing teams from FIFA competitions became necessary. We cannot allow ourselves to reach that point again.

'Going forward, all our efforts must be directed towards improving governance. This cannot end as merely another power struggle conducted behind closed doors or through bilateral discussions.

'We must also use this moment to truly live by our own governance principles and to shift the internal culture away from fear and political positioning towards greater openness, where concerns and disagreements can be voiced and addressed, not only during election periods but throughout the years between presidential mandates.

'We will continue to be a clear and constructive voice on the international stage, in line with the strategy adopted by the Norwegian Football Congress.'

Sepp Blatter, Infantino's predecessor, took to social media to renew his attacks on his successor by writing on Friday evening: 'FIFA is not a private equity fund. It is an association with statutes, regulations, and a fiduciary responsibility to protect the global game.

'If you sell football's crown jewels to private investors, you also sell part of the game – especially its soul. Money matters, but it must never become everything.'

The president of Jordan's Football Association - who ran against Infantino for president in 2016 - Ali Al Hussein argued that one of the issues facing FIFA's hierarchy was its secret ballot.

'With all the controversy surrounding FIFA, world football is facing a clear cut crisis in leadership just before an upcoming election,' Al Hussein wrote on social media.

'As someone who has been through this process before, I believe one thing needs to be done immediately: remove a secret ballot for Presidential elections!

'Every other decision including hosting the World Cup is now done openly, except - of course - for presidential elections. With a President who we elect every four years and a council that makes all the decisions, a transparent ballot is the only way to hold us as MA (member association) Presidents accountable in front of our own football fans, officials and players who elected us.

'At the same time it is protection for each and every MA who might be pressured to make a decision based on coercion behind closed doors as has happened in the past. But most importantly it will empower each and every MA on the most critical vote we have, the leadership of the biggest and most popular sport in the world and the direction it takes in the future.'

Al-Hussein was the runner-up in the contest to replace Blatter, receiving 88 votes (43 per cent of the votes), to Infantino's 115 (56 per cent).

Sports.title: Arsene Wenger has ruined his own legacy. We once thought he was The Professor, now we see the truth - a silent stooge following his master Gianni Infantino... and is ex-Arsenal boss the real brains behind FIFA's hated schemes?
Sports.content:
Arsene Wenger has ruined his own legacy. We once thought he was The Professor, now we see the truth - a silent stooge following his master Gianni Infantino... and is ex-Arsenal boss the real brains behind FIFA's hated schemes?

Unlock more of the best of our journalism with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

Speaking in February on the tenth anniversary of Gianni Infantino’s accession as FIFA president, Arsene Wenger paid tribute to his friend for overseeing a ‘huge improvement’ in world football.

‘Gianni is always ready to move forward and to create new ideas. He’s open to new ideas,’ said Wenger.

Say what you want about Infantino, he’s most definitely open to ideas.

The idea to have a World Cup in Qatar at Christmas time, and increase the number of teams at the tournament this summer to 48. If he gets his way, it will be 64 in four years’ time, when the tournament is already being played across six countries.

The idea to introduce mandatory hydration breaks at the World Cup this summer, thinking we wouldn’t see them for the commercial grab they really were, and to have the finalists from Spain and Argentina kicking their heels in the dressing room at half-time for the best part of half an hour waiting for Madonna and Co to get off the pitch at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

It was Infantino’s idea to award President Donald Trump the ridiculous FIFA Peace Prize, and then say nothing when the Iran team were banished to train in Mexico while Trump's war against them raged in the Middle East, or when the Somalian referee Omar Artan was denied entry to the US.

‘Gianni Infantino is always ready to move forward and to create new ideas. He’s open to new ideas,’ said Arsene Wenger

Say what you want about Infantino, he’s most definitely open to ideas

And it’s his preposterous idea to carve up the World Cup and sell it to private investors for £3.1billion by strong-arming FIFA’s 211 member associations into accepting his proposals, thus plunging world football into crisis.

All the while, Wenger has hovered at Infantino’s right hand like a silent stooge, a sight we witnessed so often in North America this summer.

As FIFA’s chief of global football development, the 76-year-old Frenchman is part of Infantino’s inner circle. One of the people, it’s fair to assume, who would have been aware of the great World Cup sell-off when so many other executives weren’t. For all we know, Wenger may have played an active role in hatching the plot given that he has Infantino’s ear.

Either way, it’s not a good look for the man English football first came to know 30 years ago when he arrived from Japan to take over as Arsenal manager.

The Professor, they called him. The forward-thinking coach whose ideas had a profound effect on the Arsenal culture and beyond the marbled halls of Highbury.

Wenger has continued to influence football’s development since he was appointed by Infantino in November 2019, 18 months after he had left Arsenal after 22 years in charge.

Among other things, he heads up the £160million FIFA Talent Coach Programme which develops young players in poorer countries where the path to professional football is lacking, and for that he deserves credit. He also leads a FIFA taskforce on player welfare which aims to address concerns over the increasing demands of the football calendar, although how Wenger’s proposal to stage the World Cup every two years would help in that regard is anyone’s guess.

It would be refreshing to think that a man of his influence and intelligence would be able to stand up to Infantino’s rampant egotism, but sadly that doesn’t seem to be the case.

It’s not a good look for the man English football first came to know 30 years ago when he arrived from Japan to take over as Arsenal manager and turned them into champions

Wenger will do what he always does these days. He will follow his master and nod along to whatever hare-brained idea Infantino comes up with next

Before the World Cup final, he claimed the new 48-team format had been a success – though at least had the decency to admit that not everyone was a fan of the hydration breaks.

It would be fascinating to hear what Wenger really thinks of the plan to sell off the World Cup and Infantino’s offer to give member associations £30million if they accept it by September 19, which has met with such resistance around the globe including the threat of a UEFA boycott. But let’s not hold our breath. He will do what he always does these days. He will follow his master and nod along to whatever hare-brained idea Infantino comes up with next.

FIFA tried to extinguish the fire on Friday as its president faced growing calls to step down. ‘Nobody is selling football. This is not something FIFA would ever entertain,’ read a statement.

But they aren’t fooling anyone. The world can see Infantino for what he is now – and we see Wenger standing squarely behind him.

Sports.title: Welsh heavyweight boxer challenges Prince William to boxing fight: Commonwealth Games gold medallist offers cheeky invitation after heir opted to watch the netball with Kate and the kids in Glasgow
Sports.content:
Welsh heavyweight boxer challenges Prince William to boxing fight: Commonwealth Games gold medallist offers cheeky invitation after heir opted to watch the netball with Kate and the kids in Glasgow

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The Prince and Princess of Wales opted to spend their morning watching the netball in Glasgow but the real royal rumble was in the boxing ring.

England claimed three gold medals within two hours in the first session of the day, with Sacha Hickey, Patris Mughalzai and Isaac Okoh all topping the podium.

After defeating Welshman Connor Williams in the heavyweight final, Okoh sent a cheeky invitation to William: ‘If he wants a pad session, tell him to call me. But the fee is quite high!

‘I don’t know what they’re into. They might come down and enjoy the fights. The atmosphere has been great this week so hopefully one day they might see me box.’

It was a display of dominance from these amateur fighters, who train together in Sheffield.

England claimed three gold medals within two hours in the first session of the day, with Sacha Hickey, Patris Mughalzai and Isaac Okoh (right) all topping the podium

The Prince and Princess of Wales had opted to spend their morning watching the netball instead

After defeating Connor Williams in the heavyweight final, Isaac Okoh sent a cheeky invitation to Prince William: ‘If he wants a pad session, tell him to call me. But the fee is quite high!'

They have now turned their sights towards Olympic gold at LA 2028, following the likes of Nicola Adams, Anthony Joshua and Amir Khan.

‘You’re going to see us back at the top of the podium again,’ added Okoh. ‘I feel like I’m one of the best in the world at 90kgs at the minute. I’m still young.

'Since September last year I’ve been on an amazing run of form, picking up loads of medals. Come LA, I’ll be looking to win another gold medal.

‘It’s all building blocks towards the big pay-per-view nights that we all dream of. This is how we get there, winning medals like this at the Commonwealth Games and the Olympics. Hopefully one day you’ll see us on posters, buying our pay per views.’

Sports.title: 'I want to attack as quickly as possible': Why Matthias Jaissle's 'RB Style' can save Newcastle United - from 'elite' pressing to developing young stars, and the players who will thrive under new boss
Sports.content:
There’s going to be a new man in Toon – Matthias Jaissle is expected to soon replace Eddie Howe as Newcastle United’s head coach.

A close confidant of England boss Thomas Tuchel, under whom he played in Stuttgart's academy, the 38-year-old will take the reins after leading Saudi Pro League side – and Newcastle's sister club – Al Ahli to back-to-back Asian Champions League crowns. Before that he led Red Bull Salzburg to successive titles after taking over at just 33.

So, what can Newcastle fans expect?

Well, first of all, they can strap themselves in for some all-action football.

Jaissle is a fully fledged member of the ‘RB Style’ adopted by clubs in the Red Bull network, a philosophy implemented by German coach Ralf Rangnick of whom Jaissle is a steadfast disciple. Fast, flat-out, intense pressing, win it back high up the pitch and get to the goal as quickly as possible.

‘We want to be courageous, bold, and attack-minded,’ said Jaissle of his style back in 2022, after winning the Austrian double in his first season at RB Salzburg, having joined from their feeder club, second-division side FC Liefering. ‘Naturally, this should be combined with high pressing to put the opposition under a lot of pressure.’

Matthias Jaissle is on the brink of being named as the new Newcastle head coach, after Eddie Howe's abrupt departure this week

The 38-year-old German won the Austrian Bundesliga in both of his seasons at Red Bull Salzburg, and then won back-to-back Asian Champions Leagues at Al Ahli

JAISSLE'S JOURNEY Club Games Win % FC Liefering (2021) 17 64.71 Red Bull Salzburg (2021-23) 93 68.82 Al Ahli (2023-present) 138 65.22

He wants his teams to be relentless off the ball.

‘I want stress on the opponent as soon as possible,’ he told The Athletic in January. ‘And when we win the ball, I want to go as quickly as possible towards the opponent’s goal. I’m very vertical (forwards, rather than sideways) in that approach.’

As a coach, Jaissle likes to keep things simple. He talks of not wanting to ‘overwhelm’ his players with too much information and likes to use one-to-one meetings to convey his messages. While his principles have remained the same, he has tweaked his shape and approach over the years. During his time at Salzburg, he used a narrow diamond formation with his full-backs providing the width.

Since his switch to the Al Ahli, he’s been much more flexible. He’s opted for a 4-2-3-1 with Riyad Mahrez on one flank behind striker Ivan Toney, who notched 32 goals in the league last season. He’s played 4-4-2, 4-3-3 and even gone three at the back on occasion. His structure was more controlled but the demands to win the ball back high remained.

‘It is not about formations that much,’ said Jaissle. ‘It is more how you want to play, how you want to attack, how you want to defend.’ He even managed to get the mercurial Mahrez pressing. Only five other forwards won the ball back in the final third more often than the former Manchester City and Leicester winger.

What it will mean is a style shift for Newcastle. The Magpies were renowned for their intensity under Howe early in his tenure but drifted into a more pedestrian approach, especially as they tried – and struggled – to juggle Champions League commitments, which they do not have to worry about this year.

Jaissle’s Al Ahli moved the ball up the pitch faster than any Premier League side last season while only Sunderland and West Ham played a higher percentage of their passes forward than Al Ahli.

But they were by no means sitting back and counter-attacking. They were in your face at all times. Al Ahli allowed opponents fewer passes before trying to win it back than any Premier League side managed and, on average, started their attacks closer to the opposition goal than all but Man City. There are, of course, caveats to be made between the respective qualities of the two leagues, but Jaissle’s demands are clear.

HOW HE COMPARES TO HOWE Per match, 2025-26 Newcastle Al Ahli Passes 450 346 10+ pass sequences 10.2 6.3 Foward pass % 33.9 36.2 Crosses 16.7 11.6 Through balls 1.6 1.9 Shots 13.0 12.9 Shots faced 12.4 8.6 High turnovers 6.6 7.8

Newcastle were far from being the Premier League's possession kings last season, firmly in midtable with their 450 passes per game but that is Guardiola-esque compared to Al Ahli’s 346, which put them fourth-fewest across the entire Saudi Pro League.

The Magpies averaged far more attacks made up of ten or more passes, and almost twice the number of them that ended up in a shot on goal.

Toon fans can prepare themselves for some high-octane football. No tippy-tappy. Press hard, get it forward. It is, in many ways, exactly the style of football that is starting to dominate the Premier League.

So who will thrive under Newcastle's new man?

For a start, it’s a shame that Anthony Gordon, a willing runner and a real threat in a direct system has now joined Barcelona.

It’s a system that seems purpose-built for Anthony Elanga. The winger failed to score a single league goal last season after a £55million move from Nottingham Forest but a second chance in a side that wants to play in, for want of a less nerdy phrase, a ‘vertical transition team’ could be just what he needs. No player averaged more sprints per 90 minutes than Elanga last season.

Likewise, Newcastle’s £42.3million summer signing Bazoumana Touré, a rapid Ivorian who is highly touted as a star of the future. Get on yer bike, young man. Will Jacob Murphy, now 31, have the legs for the press?

Tino Livramento and Lewis Hall could also thrive under Jaissle. Even when he sets up in a 4-3-3, when his side has the ball, he wants his full backs to push up alongside the winger to help overload in wide areas.

You can see from the average position map of their victory over Al Kholood at the end of last season how the team moves into a 3-2-5 shape – also very common in the Premier League these days – with centre back Merih Demiral shifting wide and right back Ali Majrashi joining Mahrez high up the pitch.

New £42.3million signing Bazoumana Toure could thrive in Jaissle's high-intensity system

What that pitch map also shows is how Jaissle has room for someone to come crashing out of the midfield line. For Al Ahli in that game it was former AC Milan and Barcelona midfielder Franck Kessie, who assisted two of the goals in a 3-0 win.

For Salzburg, that was Brenden Aaronson, now at Leeds, who praised Jaissle for helping him adapt to a new position. ‘He’s taught me a different way of playing the No10 role,’ he said. ‘More runs in behind and late runs into the box. My playmaking skills and final pass have gotten better.’

For Newcastle, that could be Joelinton, although there are doubts over his future at the club after he asked to leave earlier this summer for Saudi Arabia. A few seasons ago, that could well have been Joe Willock, who made a reputation for himself for arriving late in the box to score.

Replacing £100million Sandro Tonali will be far from straightforward and Newcastle have bagged a couple of newbies in 18-year-old Sean Steur and 20-year-old Aladji Bamba. ‘The way he works and develops young players is exceptional,’ said Christoph Freund, the then-Salzburg sporting director. Newcastle fans will hope he’s right.

After a frustrating debut season for Newcastle curtailed by a knee injury, Jaissle’s arrival could well get the best out of Yoane Wissa. Like Elanga, the striker had a good World Cup. And he showed during his time at Brentford that he is superb at leading a team’s press from the front. During his final campaign with the Bees, he was among the leading strikers in the division for winning possession back in the final third.

How Nick Woltemade can adapt is the more interesting dilemma. Howe could never quite figure out where his best position was and you wonder whether Jaissle will have the same problem.

Jaissle has little need for a 6ft 6in target man, off whom he wants knockdowns and flicks with his back to goal, but Woltemade offers more than just that. He can drop between the lines and play as much as a creator as a goalscorer. Jaissle worked with 6ft 5in Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko at Salzburg, so can get the best out of big men. But Woltemade’s struggles with running the channels or leading the press will likely hold him back if he’s to remain up top.

Toney is hardly renowned as an elite presser, but proved that he’s still a ruthless goalscorer and even he showed he can get stuck in and win the ball back high.

Jaissle's Salzburg reached the knockout stages of the Champions League for the first time in the club's history in 2021, finishing above Sevilla and Wolfsburg in their group

Nick Pope’s future at Newcastle is already uncertain. The club have already signed 20-year-old keeper Ewen Jaouen and are believed to be closing in on Braga stopper Lukas Hornicek.

Jaissle’s arrival will do little to brighten Pope’s chances. ‘Goalkeeper is not a position by itself any more,’ said Jaissle. ‘It is completely included with the other guys. A goalkeeper has to have an understanding of all phases of the game.’ That, sadly, is not Pope's game.

Above all, Newcastle fans will hope Rasmus Kristensen, who played under Jaissle at Salzburg, has the right view of their new man.

‘He is a born winner,’ said Kristensen. ‘He possesses that special winning mentality.’

Sports.title: Hansi Flick admits Barcelona will 'miss' Marcus Rashford after LaLiga giants snubbed chance to sign Man United star despite impressive loan spell in Spain
Sports.content:
Hansi Flick admits Barcelona will 'miss' Marcus Rashford after LaLiga giants snubbed chance to sign Man United star despite impressive loan spell in Spain

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Barcelona manager Hansi Flick admits he will 'miss' Marcus Rashford after his impressive spell on loan with the LaLiga title winners - all but confirming that he won't rejoin.

Rashford scored 14 goals and provided as many assists on loan from Manchester United and indicated that he wanted to extend his stay in Spain's second city.

But Barca have since signed wingers Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi for a combined £106.5million, so it looks highly unlikely that they will activate Rashford's £26m optional purchase clause.

It leaves Rashford facing a return to Old Trafford, a place he previously admitted he was ready to leave, though it would be under new manager Michael Carrick.

Flick said: 'What I can say about Marcus is I appreciate a lot to work with him.

'Sometimes it’s not always that you do know what happens with the players who are on loan.

Barcelona manager Hansi Flick has said he will 'miss' Marcus Rashford - all but confirming that he won't rejoin them

Flick said that Rashford is a 'fantastic player and a fantastic person' after their LaLiga title win

'I think our situation is not easy for that, but I appreciate a lot working with him as he’s a fantastic player and fantastic person.

'I think also the team miss him and I will miss him, but that’s life. This is what we have to accept.'

Barcelona's financial restrictions have eased somewhat after half a decade of efforts to alleviate them but their hands are still tied to some extent.

They are yet to garner much money from player sales this window and still need to replace Robert Lewandowski, who has joined Chicago Fire on a free.

Rashford should have his fair share of suitors after an encouraging season which saw him break into England's World Cup squad.

The 28-year-old scored in England's opening match against Croatia, a 4-2 win, but did not set the tournament on fire from there.

He has two years remaining on his contract with boyhood club United.

Rashford said in May: 'I'm not a magician but if I was, I would stay.

'It's really good. I came here to win. I want to win as many things as I can.

'This team is a wonderful team. They're going to win so much in the future as well. To be a part of that would be special.'

Sports.title: 'Phenomenal horseman' praised for role in brilliant Goodwood week for Wathnan Racing
Sports.content:
"Phenomenal horseman" praised for role in brilliant Goodwood week for Wathnan Racing

Hamad Al Jehani took two big Goodwood prizes with his thoroughbreds, the Coral-backed Golden Mile and Stewards Cup. The team's seven winners were Wild Blossom, Flora Of Bermuda, Exclusive Code, Archivist, Silver Lake, Hopewell Rock and Evening Saigon

View 2 Images Trainer Hamad Al Jehani (left) with several members of the Wathnan Racing team after Evening Saigon won the Coral Stewards' Cup (Image: Andrew Matthews/PA Wire. Use subject to restrictions. Editorial use only, no commercial use without prior consent from rights holder)

"Phenomenal horseman" Hamad Al Jehani was praised for his role in a big week for Wathnan Racing at the 2026 Qatar Goodwood Festival.

‌



The trainer sent out Evening Saigon to land the Coral Stewards Cup on Saturday, just a day after fellow 16-1 shot Archivist bagged another big handicap on Friday, the Golden Mile with the same sponsors.

‌



The pair were among seven winners for the owners over the five days, scooping just over £218,000 in prize money from their races alone.

‌



"Hamad has turned up and won two of the hardest handicaps to win all year," said Wathnan's racing advisor Richard Brown.

"We plot these and work as a team – when these results come off, it’s just fantastic for Wathnan and what we are all about.

Top jockey Jim Crowley retires at 48 after horror fall at York led to five operations READ MORE :

“If you look at Hamad’s statistics since he started training, they match up with the best trainers in the country. He’s a phenomenal horseman and was a very good rider himself. He’s very modest about it but he showjumped to a good level.

‌



"We all work very closely together and to pull this off is huge for everybody involved.”

Wild Blossom got the ball rolling in the Alice Keppell Conditions Stakes on Wednesday and Flora Of Bermuda, Exclusive Code, Silver Lake and Hopewell Rock also hit the target.

James Doyle picked Evening Saigon from the three Wathnan Racing had in contention in the Coral Stewards Cup and although the sprinter used plenty of energy before the start, he had enough left to see off Stratusnine on the far side.

‌



Mitbaahy was closing the pair down and took third in Saturday's feature, with Completely Random a close-up fourth under the meeting's leading rider Ryan Moore.

View 2 Images Evening Saigon (red cap) won the Coral Stewards Cup (Image: Getty Images)

"I am very happy for Evening Saigon and very happy for the team," said Hamad Al Jehani. "He performed very well at Royal Ascot and it was the right decision from the management to keep him for the Stewards’ Cup.

‌



“It’s really important for us and it’s a really important race for the season. I’m very happy and thanks to James for giving the horse a great ride.

“It’s not easy to be competitive with the best trainers in the world but we try our best and I think we are building in a very good way, with great help from the management. Hopefully, we will improve year by year and we can make Wathnan be in the winner’s enclosure more and more.”

Handlers Archie Watson, William Haggas, Andrew Balding, Karl Burke and George Boughey all saddled winners for the team across the week.

Article continues below

"Obviously I was very deflated last year (at the meeting) so the memo was we need to do better and that’s everyone, including me as well,” Evening Saigon's rider James Doyle said.

"He’s not an easy conveyance, setting off he was that well in himself he tried to get rid of me the first few strides but that was great."

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua has nothing to prove and should think long and hard about carrying on
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua has nothing to prove and should think long and hard about carrying on

Our man Barry McGuigan runs the rule over Anthony Joshua following his unconvincing comeback win over Kristian Prenga before taking on Tyson Fury

View 2 Images AJ was knocked down twice in the first round (Image: Matchroom Boxing/Getty Images)

Saddened but not surprised was my reaction when Anthony Joshua sank to the canvas 20 seconds into the fight in Saudi Arabia.

‌



Yes he got to his feet and won in the second. The kind of power he carries is the last thing that leaves you. Punch resistance is another matter.

‌



Once that goes, it never comes back. It only ever gets worse. This is the stage Joshua is at. He is vulnerable and his opponents know it.

‌



Tyson Fury would have been watching those first-round knockdowns and rubbing his hands. Before the Kristian Prenga bout I had Joshua favourite against Fury. That dynamic has now shifted. Everything would have to go right for Joshua to win.

Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury winner offered world title shot READ MORE :

Anthony Joshua told exactly how he can beat Tyson Fury READ MORE :

This is a brutal business and if I were Joshua, I would be thinking hard about carrying on. I would not want to enter the ring knowing I was not at my best.

Joshua has nothing to prove to anybody. He has been a vibrant, positive presence in British boxing, won Olympic gold and the world heavyweight championship. And he certainly doesn’t need the money.

‌



However, I realise how difficult it would be for him to step down at this stage from a fight of such magnitude. It has been brewing for the best part of a decade and is important for the whole boxing economy.

Fury was far from convincing himself, labouring to victory 24 hours earlier in Thailand against a 46-year-old Mariusz Wach, who was annihilated by Moses Itauma. Wach just got tired in the end.

You would have worried for Fury prior to the Prenga shock. The truth is they are both fading rapidly.

‌



View 2 Images Anthony Joshua knocked out Kristian Prenga (Image: Getty Images)

Inactivity will not have helped Joshua, who had fought only once in 22 months and, of course, was involved in a tragic accident only last December, which took a huge emotional toll.

The only way Joshua prevails against Fury is to stand on him and back him up. If he lands early and big, it’s over, no matter how suspect his chin.

Article continues below

This is the dilemma. If you have to be aggressive to beat an opponent you are more likely to walk on to a counter. Fury is likely to keep his distance early, tee off his jab then look to send a right straight down the pipe.

Alternatively, having noted Joshua’s increased vulnerability, Fury could just go for it like he did in the second Deontay Wilder fight. Either way it’s not going the distance, that much is clear.

Follow Barry on X at @ClonesCyclone @McGuigan’s_Gym

Sports.title: UEFA 'accelerating' efforts to force Gianni Infantino out of FIFA after embarrassing U-turn
Sports.content:
UEFA 'accelerating' efforts to force Gianni Infantino out of FIFA after embarrassing U-turn

Gianni Infantino's position as FIFA president is looking more and more uncertain after he was forced to drop his plan to sell stakes in tournaments following a backlash led by UEFA

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino could be ousted as FIFA president (Image: Harry Murphy/UEFA via Getty Images)

UEFA have been emboldened by Gianni Infantino's humiliating U-turn on his controversial World Cup plans and are reportedly working hard to oust him from his position.

‌



Infantino's attempts to force through plans, in which stakes of tournaments like the World Cup would be sold to private investors, has fallen flat on its face. European football's governing body UEFA, CONCACAF, which represents North and Central America, and the Asian Football Confederation spoke out against the idea, killing it dead.

‌



Just days after announcing the plans, Infantino was forced to concede that it had "created divisions" and was "no longer in the interest" of the game. Having originally been conceived as a way of solidifying his support ahead of seeking re-election for a fourth term as FIFA president, the plans could now prove to be his downfall.

‌



UEFA have led the backlash against Infantino and are now considering the best way to remove him as FIFA president. Sky News reports that moves are 'accelerating' and there is 'a determined effort' to oust him. The report states that it is now not a question of if, but when, Infantino will be toppled.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

UEFA declare loss of confidence in Gianni Infantino in bombshell new statement READ MORE :

The easiest outcome would be to force Infantino to resign from a position he's held for 10 years. If not, they would need 43 of FIFA's 211 associations to ask for an emergency congress in order to hold a vote of no confidence in Infantino's leadership.

‌



Another option would be to rally support behind a rival in the upcoming election. TalkSPORT says UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin has asked federations who have previously endorsed Infantino for a fourth term to revoke their letters. CONCACAF leader Victor Montagliani, or Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al-Khelaifi, could be put forward to run against Infantino.

Whatever option they pursue, it is clear that UEFA is determined to use the current momentum to force lasting change at FIFA.

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino is facing mounting opposition (Image: PA)

‌



UEFA said in a statement on Saturday: "We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game. We must identify those responsible and hold them to account.

"It is right that, in the coming days and weeks, UEFA will work with its associations and in close cooperation with other confederations to reflect on how this happened and devise a plan to make sure that it cannot occur again.

"That review should be thorough and fundamental. No option should be off the table. The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA’s confidence but also that of many other members of the football family.

‌



"When Gianni Infantino asked for the trust and the votes of FIFA’s Member Associations to elect him as their President in 2016, he said, 'Of course we have to be transparent. I have been this in the last 15 years of my life in UEFA. You will have to play a part every day in the life of FIFA,' before telling the assembled stakeholders, 'The money of FIFA is your money. It’s not the money of the FIFA President. It’s your money. You are the national associations and the money of FIFA has to serve for the development of football and not for anything else.'

"On both these promises, he has failed to deliver. The shabby, back room, opaque deal he hatched and tried to force through was anything but transparent. And with reserves standing at over $5bn, he has also failed to use associations’ money for the benefit of the game.

‌



"UEFA will begin work immediately with partners and stakeholders all over the world and right across the game to propose a new way of distributing resources through the existing FIFA Forward programme.

"We must start to use some of that money that is sat idle in FIFA’s bank account to deliver the kick start that the grassroots and the wider game need in each of the 211 countries of FIFA. But we don’t need to sell off the family silver to pay for it.

"This is a victory for the whole game. But it must not be the end of the story. The proposal has gone. The task of rebuilding trust in FIFA has only just begun."

Sports.title: Bryan Mbeumo inspires Man Utd win vs Atletico Madrid as transfer hint drops - 6 talking points
Sports.content:
Bryan Mbeumo inspires Man Utd win vs Atletico Madrid as transfer hint drops - 6 talking points

MANCHESTER UNITED 2-1 ATLETICO MADRID: Bryan Mbeumo scored from the penalty spot before netting the winning goal as United came from behind to beat their Spanish opponents

View 3 Images Bryan Mbeumo bagged a brace (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United came from behind to defeat Atletico Madrid in Sweden. Bryan Mbeumo scored a brace to lead Michael Carrick's side to a 2-1 win as 15-year-old JJ Gabriel made his first senior appearance.

‌



United entered their third pre-season match of the summer at the Strawberry Arena in Solna, looking to build on the momentum from their thrashing of Rosenborg. It did not start well for the Premier League team.

‌



Atletico Madrid took the lead after just five minutes when a teasing cross from Arnau Ortiz ghosted into the net at the far post. It escaped the clutches of attack and defence to give Diego Simeone's side a one-goal advantage.

‌



Luke Shaw, Bryan Mbeumo and Amad all went close as United controlled much of the proceedings in the opening half but could only go into the break down a goal.

Seven minutes into the second period, Shae Lacey showed some quick feet in the Atletico area to force a challenge and win a penalty after tripping on a dangling leg. Mbeumo coolly dispatched his penalty to put United on level terms.

With a raft of changes, Atletico proved a more threatening force as the game went on but Carrick's men managed to find another breakthrough. Jack Fletcher pounced on an errant pass before playing in a dangerous ball for Mbeumo to grab his second.

‌



Mirror Football takes a look at the talking points that arose from the clash.

Marcus Rashford has chance to 'hurt' Man Utd as two transfer moves proposed READ MORE :

Lively Lacey

There isn't a great deal of room in the No.10 spot at Old Trafford. Bruno Fernandes is all but guaranteed to take on that role at the start of the season as United's captain and best player.

But Shea Lacey did not look out of place playing in behind Bryan Mbeumo and made a decisive contribution. The 19-year-old showed slick feet to win United's penalty and looked lively enough to give Carrick something to consider when forming his squad for a Premier League and Champions League assault.

‌



It was only a friendly, of course, but he looked ready to play somewhere.

View 3 Images Shea Lacey didn't look out of place (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Mount shines

It would be easy to think Mason Mount doesn't have a natural place in a midfield pairing. Alongside Andrey Santos, he continued to shine against Atletico Madrid. The former Chelsea star proved a useful glue between midfield and attack, having already impressed during pre-season.

‌



The 27-year-old was offered the freedom to attack while Santos sat deeper. Mount showed an array of smart turns and clever one-twos to press his case while the likes of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo are yet to return.

Mount has been trusted to be a leader by Carrick and is delivering so far this summer.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



View 3 Images Mason Mount looked the best player on the pitch (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Exit hints?

Michael Carrick made two changes to his pre-season side to face Atletico, with Tom Heaton and Amad coming in. The latter is the first of United's World Cup stars to return, and his introduction saw Mbeumo move into a forward position.

There is perhaps more to glean from Radek Vitek and Zirkzee dropping out. The goalkeeper has publicly spoken of his desire to leave to find first-team football, and while Heaton is unlikely to see a significant role in the coming season, Carrick is perhaps now looking with a more long-term view.

‌



Likewise, Zirkzee has been firmly linked with an exit, most prominently to Juventus. The Dutchman is unlikely to feature much in Carrick's plans, but the United boss wasted little time making the change, despite not being able to introduce a striker.

Even when Amad was replaced at half-time, it was Jack Fletcher who was introduced. Zirkzee was brought on with 17 minutes remaining.

Goalkeeper Altay Bayindir could also be on the way out. He completed an individual training session ahead of the match amid reports that Celta Vigo had agreed a deal for his services.

‌



Backline with work to do?

For much of the game, United were untroubled, but on the rare occasions Atletico made their way into the area, the Red Devils lacked much conviction. Carrick might have been pleased with his team's pressing but he would have be less impressed with the goal United conceded.

It may have been described as a 'freak' goal by some, but only an Atletico Madrid player attempted to get on the end of the cross. Neither Harry Maguire nor Ayden Heaven got off the ground as the ball bounded past a flat-footed Tom Heaton.

It's a goal that you may allow over the course of pre-season, however, and more defenders are set to return. The likes of Noussair Mazraoui, Diogo Dalot and Lisandro Martinez are still to return, and Leny Yoro may not be required to play at full-back once the season starts.

‌



The Frenchman showed some ambition going forward, but his end product wasn't always up to the task.

JJ Gabriel wait over

While Toby Collyer, Jacob Devaney, Dan Gore and Chido Obi are all set to play for United's under-21s against Altrincham on Saturday night, 15-year-old JJ Gabriel remained with Michael Carrick's squad. The youngster was named to the bench against Atletico as he continues to gain experience with the first team.

The teenager has received no shortage of hype despite his tender age, and that is set to continue if he continues to figure in Carrick's plans. Gabriel was introduced in the final 10 minutes to make his first senior appearance for the team. United will hope it's the first of many.

‌



Stepping up preparation

Carrick opted to use just one substitute at half-time in comparison to Atletico's four. With just three weeks until United face Hull, the head coach is clearly looking to build towards a match-fit group of players, even with key figures such as Bruno Fernandes yet to return.

"We’re just looking for improvement and signs of improvements, little bit of fitness, quality, technique, some connections and links in the team to keep moving forward in the right direction," Carrick said ahead of the game. "We’ve had a good spell in these three weeks and the boys are ready for another game today."

It wasn't quite exhilarating or dominant but Carrick will be encouraged by his team's pressing and attacking patterns. He probably got what he wanted from the game.

Sports.title: 'I suffered injury hell after leaving Man Utd – I'm fighting for my career and next move'
Sports.content:
'I suffered injury hell after leaving Man Utd – I'm fighting for my career and next move'

EXCLUSIVE: Former Manchester United forward Will Keane is a free agent and has been training with the PFA pre-season after leaving Preston North End at the end of last season

View 5 Images Former Manchester United and Preston forward Will Keane is a free agent (Image: Getty Images)

Will Keane's Manchester United career could have been a lot different if it wasn't for injuries.

‌



A graduate of United's world famous academy, Keane progressed through the ranks at Carrington before being handed his first-team debut in December 2011. The Stockport-born forward came on as a second-half substitute in a 3-2 defeat at home to Blackburn Rovers.

‌



But Keane would return to United's Under 21s for the rest of that season before suffering a serious knee injury while on international duty with England's Under 19s in May 2012.

‌



Keane, who was 19 at the time, ruptured his Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) and was kept out for the entire 2012/13 season. He made his return for United U21s in September 2013 before going out on a one-month loan to Championship side Wigan Athletic.

Although his time at the DW Stadium was cut short through a groin injury, he would go back out on loan to spend the second half of the 2013/14 campaign at QPR.

Inside England's most dramatic title race and last day promotion shootout READ MORE :

Ex-Man Utd star tipped for bright future by Alex Ferguson speaks out on being clubless READ MORE :

More time out on loan followed at Sheffield Wednesday and Preston before then United manager Louis van Gaal gave Keane another chance to impress in the first team.

‌



But he was restricted to just two further substitute appearances for the Reds, one in the Premier League at Sunderland and another in the FA Cup at Shrewsbury.

United decided to sell Keane to Hull City, who had just been promoted to the Premier League, in August 2016 for £1million, signing a three-year contract in the process.

Reflecting on his time at United, Keane exclusively told Mirror Football: "I look back now and it was the best place to come through the ranks and have that development. I was lucky to have a strong squad as a whole.

‌



View 5 Images Will Keane in action for Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

"At the time, the feeling was that a lot of us would go and break in and get around the first team, which a few did and stayed there for a long time. I loved it.

"I think the whole education, enjoying going in every day. It was a great place to learn our trade and to make that transition from academy to reserves. And then I think the coaches we had at the time were all brilliant.

‌



"I see now even a lot of lads are going on to have great careers. I think you've seen it at United, haven't you, over the years? It's been like a conveyor belt. The aim is to always play, but if you don't, lads are still on to have great careers. It was the perfect place to be."

Although Keane didn't get as much game time as he would have wanted at United, he still learnt a lot and gained some valuable experience with some of the best coaches and players in world football.

But Keane does believe that he would have had more opportunities if he hadn't have suffered the ACL injury that ended up keeping him out for almost 16 months.

‌



When asked why it didn’t work out at United, Keane added: "It's all ifs, buts and maybes, so there's no saying that I would have stayed there and played a lot more. But I think in football, a lot of it is timing, isn't it? I was quite unfortunate that I did have a bad knee injury at the time, which I'd just made my debut, and then it was the last game of the season.

View 5 Images Former Manchester United forward Will Keane (Image: Getty Images)

"I did my ACL and then I ended up being out for 15 or 16 months, so it was a long time when it was probably a key part of the transition and getting around the squad.

‌



"So obviously that hindered my progression then, and even then when I got back, it took time to get myself going, so that didn't help. And then I did it again, even when I left United and I went to Hull in the Premier League, played a few games and ended up redoing it. So then that was another year out.

"At the time it was shocking timing and it kind of killed me, but that is the way it goes. I've still managed to carve out a career. Obviously you never know, if I'd not had them, would I have stayed higher up? Potentially, but who knows?"

Soon after leaving United to sign for Hull, Keane ruptured his ACL for a SECOND time. It came on just his sixth appearance for the Tigers during a 2-1 win against Southampton in November 2016.

‌



Keane was forced to miss 14 months before returning in January 2018 following Hull's relegation to the Championship. He went on to score his first goal for the Tigers in a 5-0 win at Burton in April 2018.

Detailing the struggles he had while recovering from both ACL injuries, Keane revealed that it took a toll on him both from a physical and even a mental aspect. "Yeah, at the time it was a real challenge," he continued.

View 5 Images Will Keane suffered an ACL tear for a second time at Hull

‌



"I think the first one I didn't really know because I'd never had a bad injury like that before, I kind of just got on with it. It was obviously really tough to take, but I didn't know how long the actual rehab process was going to take.

"As it carried on, I thought this is never ending. And it was tough because I remember at the time I was thinking, even when I got back outside, I was really struggling to get going and thought, how am I going to be able to play again here to a certain level? It just takes time and a bit of reprogramming your body and your brain almost to do all the things you used to do, but you get there eventually.

"The second one was tough because it was almost like a second chance at playing at that top level in the Prem (Premier League). So that one was really hard, especially because I knew how long it was out because I'd been through it once before.

‌



"That season we got relegated at Hull, so then I've come back and we're not obviously in the same situation. That was hard to take because I felt like I'd had some setbacks at United, but then going to Hull was a fresh chance, a clean slate, and then to have that, it'd be such a major injury again, ruining the chance of getting more games in the Prem was really hard.

"Like I said, I've always tried to be optimistic and look to the positives, which is not easy at times. Still managed to grind it out and play at a good level and been at some great clubs."

View 5 Images Will Keane has had a successful EFL career (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Keane has since gone on to have a successful career in the EFL. After leaving Hull in 2019, he moved to Ipswich Town and then on to Wigan Athletic, where he enjoyed his most prolific season in 2021/22.

Indeed, Keane found the net 27 times in 50 appearances as the Latics won the League One title. The following season, he hit double figures for Wigan in the Championship and that earned him a move to Preston North End.

He was Preston's top scorer in the 2023/24 season with 13 goals and had his contract extended until June 2026. But Keane was unable to rediscover that same form in his second season at the club.

‌



And after then struggling to get a look-in under Paul Heckingbottom at the start of the 2025/26 campaign, Keane went out on loan to League One side Reading for the second half of the season.

He scored just twice in 14 matches for The Royals before becoming a free agent earlier this summer, following the expiration of his contract at Preston.

Now 33, Keane is still without a club and has spent the last five weeks at PFA pre-season, a summer programme that allows out-of-contract players to train and regain fitness with a view of finding their next move.

‌



"I feel really good," Keane said, when asked about his future during his time on the PFA pre-season camp. "It was disappointing not to have played more games at the end of last season, but I feel like this is a clean slate and I'm still raring to go. I feel like I've still got a lot to offer.

"I wanted to rediscover the form that I had a couple of years ago. I was playing consistently and scoring plenty of goals. I feel like I've still got that in me. I'm really itching to do that again.

"I had a few injuries early on in my career, but a few people in the game said to me, the coach and what not, that hopefully towards the end of my career I'll get them back.

Article continues below

"I'm not exactly a player who's always relied on pure pace, which I know sometimes as you get older you might lose that yard. But as long as you still keep sharp in the mind and keep getting in the right areas, hopefully I can still contribute and score goals. So that's the aim and hopefully I'll still have a successful couple of years."

Sports.title: 'Goodwood was my lucky track' - Jim Crowley retires and names best horse he rode
Sports.content:
'Goodwood was my lucky track' - Jim Crowley retires and names best horse he rode

The 48-year-old was given a guard of honour by his former weighing room colleagues including Ryan Moore, Oisin Murphy and Saffie Osborne. Crowley switched from the jumps to the Flat at the age of 27 and had numerous big race successes

View Image The guard of honour at Goodwood for retiring Jim Crowley (Image: Andrew Matthews/PA Wire. Use subject to restrictions. Editorial use only, no commercial use without prior consent from rights holder)

Jim Crowley said he made the decision to retire last night to coincide his farewell with the biggest meeting at his local course.

‌



Crowley, 48, celebrated his 2,000th career winner at Goodwood on Modmin in 2020 and took the feature Sussex Stakes three times, riding Here Comes When (2017), Mohaather (2021) and Baaeed (2022) - naming the latter as the best horse he rode.

‌



In a few months, the dad-of-three plans to take out a training licence from Coombelands in Pulborough, which is around 15 miles from the West Sussex course, where the five-day Qatar Festival concludes this afternoon.

‌



Crowley was given a guard of honour by a large number of his former colleagues including Ryan Moore, Oisin Murphy and Saffie Osborne.

"There are 1,000 emotions running through me. Good ones, sad ones - but I have had a lovely send off and there is no finer place," he said.

‌



Top jockey Jim Crowley retires at 48 after horror fall at York led to five operations READ MORE :

"Goodwood has always been a lucky track for me. I rode my 2,000th winner here as well so it's great to finish here. I made the decision last night.

He added: "I have been riding in racing since i was 16, had my first ride when I was 17 so it has been tough. Time doesn't wait for anybody and the injuries I had at York have took a lot longer than I anticipated but I feel very fortunate to have come out from that accident because it was a pretty nasty one.

"When I was a jump jcokey people said I wouldn't do any good on the Flat so that just made me more determined.

Article continues below

""Baaeed, Battash, so many here. Mohaather, Here Comes When in the rain. I have had a great time of it it is our local course and it is a very special place for me.

"I'm young enough to start training now and it's something I really want to get my teeth into."

Champion jockey in 2016, Crowley's long and successful stint was brought to a halt Almeraq fell in a race at York in September 2025 and the sportsman had to have five operations as he recovered from serious injuries.

Sports.title: Barcelona boss speaks out on Marcus Rashford as deal turned down - ‘I miss him’
Sports.content:
Barcelona boss speaks out on Marcus Rashford as deal turned down - ‘I miss him’

Marcus Rashford has returned to Manchester United after Barcelona turned down the chance to sign him permanently following a season-long loan switch at the Nou Camp

View 2 Images Hansi Flick has discussed the decision not to sign Marcus Rashford permanently (Image: Getty Images)

Barcelona boss Hansi Flick has said that the Spanish giants ‘miss’ Marcus Rashford following his return to Manchester United. The England wideman spent last season on loan in Spain.

‌



The Catalan giants had an option to sign him permanently for £26m but turned down that opportunity. It leaves Rashford in a difficult situation.

‌



As it stands, no clubs have made an approach to United to sign him, while he is valued at £40m by the Red Devils.

‌



Barcelona boss Flick has now discussed the winger following the club’s decision not to go through with a permanent deal and certainly has a high opinion of the wideman. He said: “What I can say about Marcus is I appreciate a lot to work with him. Sometimes it’s not always that you do know what happens with the players who are on loan.

Marcus Rashford has chance to 'hurt' Man Utd as two transfer moves proposed READ MORE :

“I think our situation is not easy for that, but I appreciate a lot working with him as he’s a fantastic player and fantastic person. I think also the team miss him and I will miss him, but that’s life. This is what we have to accept.”

While Barcelona opted not to sign Rashford, they did however move for his England colleague Anthony Gordon, paying Newcastle £75m for his services.

‌



On his new winger, Flick added: “At the end, Anthony Gordon comes and from the first call with him, when I first spoke with him, he is on fire with Barca and wants to go there and I am delighted he is on our team.”

Flick’s comments about Rashford come just days after the forward bid farewell to the club on social media. He wrote: "I'm very grateful to everyone at the club for making my time here such a positive and memorable experience.

View 2 Images Barcelona chose not to sign Marcus Rashford permanently (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"I've enjoyed every moment and will take many special memories with me. I wish the club and all its supporters the very best of luck and every success in the season ahead."

In all, Rashford made 49 appearances in all competitions for Barcelona during his time in Spain, scoring 14 goals and providing a further 14 assists. The Red Devils academy graduate also spent six months on loan at Aston Villa before joining Barcelona. He still has two years remaining on his contract with United.

Rashford has yet to link up with the Red Devils’ squad on their pre-season tour, having been granted additional time off following the World Cup.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
